### TRANSLATOR'S NOTE.

It might be inferred from the title of this work that it deals simply with the phenomena of the spiritual world <note>In this context, the "spiritual world" refers to the realm of the soul and the afterlife as described in Swedenborgian theology.</note> and its three distinct regions. But it will be seen that in its deeper meaning and purpose it sets forth the true relations and the disordered relations between man and man, or the heavenly life and the infernal life <note>The "infernal life" refers to a state of being driven by self-interest and malice, contrasted here with the "heavenly life" of service and love.</note> as exhibited in human experience everywhere.

The same aims and methods have been followed in the translation of this work as were followed in the translation of the *Divine Providence* <note>original: "Sapientia Angelica de Divina Providentia." This refers to another major work by Swedenborg concerning the laws of God's government.</note>, and defined in the preface to that work.

J. C. AGER. <note>John Curtis Ager (1835–1913) was a noted American translator and clergyman who spent much of his career translating Swedenborg’s voluminous Latin manuscripts into English for the Swedenborg Foundation.</note>

<summary>In this preface, translator J.C. Ager explains that while the book discusses the afterlife, its primary value lies in its psychological and ethical insights into human relationships. He notes that the translation style remains consistent with his previous work on Swedenborg's texts.</summary>
<keywords>spiritual world, heavenly life, infernal life, Divine Providence, J. C. Ager, Emanuel Swedenborg, translation ethics, human relations</keywords>

# HEAVEN AND HELL.

---

**1.** The Lord, speaking in the presence of His disciples of the **consummation of the age**, which is the final period of the church,<gloss>¹</gloss> says, near the end of what he foretells about its successive states in respect to love and faith :<gloss>²</gloss>

> “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken. And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven ; and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn ; and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And He shall send forth His angels with a trumpet and a great sound ; and they shall gather together His elect from the four winds, from the end of the heavens even to the end thereof ” (*Matthew* xxiv. 29-31).

**Those** who understand these words according to the literal sense have no other belief than that during that closing period, which is called the **final judgment**, all these things are to occur as they are described in the literal sense—that is, that the sun and moon will be darkened and the stars will fall from the sky, that the sign of the Lord will appear in the sky, and He Himself will be seen in the clouds, attended by angels with trumpets ; and furthermore, as is foretold elsewhere, that the whole visible universe will be destroyed, and afterwards a new heaven with a new earth will come into being. Such is the belief of most men in the church at the present day. But those who so believe are ignorant of the **arcana** <note>The word "arcana" refers to hidden, inner mysteries or secrets that are not immediately obvious.</note> that lie hid in every particular of the Word. For in every particular of the Word

# HEAVEN AND HELL.

There is an **internal sense** <term>internal sense: the deeper, spiritual meaning of sacred texts that lies beneath the literal words</term> which treats of things spiritual and heavenly, not of things natural and worldly which are treated of in the sense of the letter. And this is true not only of the general meaning of many expressions, it is true of every single expression.<note>In each and every particular of the Word there is an internal or spiritual sense (sections 1143, 1984, 2135, 2333, 2395, 2495, 4442, 9048, 9063, 9086).</note> For the Word is written wholly by **correspondences**,<term>correspondences: the systematic relationship between natural objects and spiritual realities</term> to the end that there may be in every particular an internal sense.<note>The Word is written wholly by correspondences, and for this reason each thing and all things in it have a spiritual meaning (sections 1404, 1408, 1409, 1540, 1619, 1659, 1709, 1783, 2900, 9086).</note> What that sense is can be seen from all that has been said and shown about it in the *Heavenly Secrets*<note>original Latin title: *Arcana Cælestia*</note>; also from quotations gathered from that work in the explanation of *The White Horse* spoken of in the *Revelation*<note>original Greek title: *Apocalypse*</note>.

It is according to that sense that what the Lord says in the words quoted above respecting His coming in the clouds of heaven must be understood. 

*   The **"sun"** there that is to be darkened signifies the Lord in respect to love;<note>In the Word the "sun" signifies the Lord in respect to love, and in consequence love to the Lord (sections 1529, 1837, 2441, 2495, 4060, 4696, 7083, 10809). Note: This footnote is labeled '2' in the original text but corresponds to the third reference.</note> 
*   the **"moon"** the Lord in respect to faith;<note>In the Word the "moon" signifies the Lord in respect to faith, and in consequence faith in the Lord (sections 1529, 1530, 2495, 4060, 4696, 7083).</note> 
*   **"stars"** knowledges of good and truth, or of love and faith;<note>In the Word "stars" signify knowledges of good and truth (sections 2495, 2849, 4697).</note> 
*   **"the sign of the Son of man in heaven"** the manifestation of Divine truth; 
*   **"the tribes of the earth"** that shall mourn, all things relating to truth and good or to faith and love;<note>"Tribes" signify all truths and goods in the complex, thus all things of faith and love (sections 3858, 3926, 4060, 6335).</note> 
*   **"the coming of the Lord in the clouds of heaven with power and glory"** His presence in the Word, and revelation,<note>The coming of the Lord signifies His presence in the Word, and revelation (sections 3900, 4060).</note> 
*   **"clouds"** signifying the sense of the letter of the Word,<note>In the Word "clouds" signify the Word in the letter or the sense of its letter (sections 4060, 4391, 5922, 6343, 6752, 8106, 8781, 9430, 10551, 10574).</note> 
*   and **"glory"** the internal sense of the Word;<note>In the Word "glory" signifies Divine truth as it is in heaven and [text breaks off]</note> 
*   **"the angels with a trumpet and [a great sound]"**

->THE GOD OF HEAVEN IS THE LORD.<-

A “great voice” signifies heaven as a source of **Divine truth**.<note>In the internal sense of the Word, a “voice” represents the truth coming from the Divine (sections 6971, 9926).</note> From the meaning of these words of the Lord, it is evident that at the end of the church—when there is no longer any love, and consequently no faith—the Lord will open the **internal meaning** of the Word and reveal the **arcana of heaven** <term>arcana of heaven: from the Latin "arcana caelestia," referring to the deep, hidden spiritual mysteries of the heavenly realm</term>. 

The secrets revealed in the following pages relate to heaven and hell, and also to the life of man after death. The person of the church today knows scarcely anything about heaven and hell or about their life after death, although these are set forth and described in the Word; and many of those born within the church even refuse to believe in them, saying in their hearts, “Who has come from that world and told us?” 

Lest, therefore, such a spirit of denial—which especially prevails among those who have much worldly wisdom—should also infect and corrupt those who are simple in heart and simple in faith, it has been granted me to associate with angels and to talk with them as one person with another. I have also been allowed to see what is in the heavens and what is in the hells, and this has continued for thirteen years. From what I have thus heard and seen, I am now permitted to describe these things, in the hope that ignorance may thus be enlightened and unbelief dissipated. Such immediate revelation is granted today because this is what is meant by the **Coming of the Lord**.

### I.

## THE GOD OF HEAVEN IS THE LORD.

**2.** It must first be known who the God of heaven is, since upon that everything else depends. Throughout all heaven, no other than the Lord alone is acknowledged as the God of heaven. There it is said, as He Himself taught,

> That He is one with the Father; that the Father is in Him, and He in [the Father]...

This is understood according to the **internal sense** <term>internal sense: the spiritual meaning within the literal text</term> of the Word.<note>Supporting references for this internal sense can be found in sections 4809, 5922, 8267, 8427, 9429, and 10574 of the author's larger work.</note>

***

1. A “trumpet” or “horn” signifies **Divine truth** in heaven, and truth revealed from heaven (sections 8815, 8823, 8915); and “voice” has the same signification (sections 6971, 9926).

<summary>Swedenborg explains that he has been granted thirteen years of spiritual sight to reveal the "arcana" (mysteries) of heaven and hell to counter modern skepticism. He establishes that Jesus Christ (the Lord) is the sole God recognized by all in the heavenly realm.</summary>

<keywords>Divine truth, arcana of heaven, life after death, Coming of the Lord, God of heaven, Emanuel Swedenborg, internal sense, skepticism</keywords>

--- Page 18 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Lord as the God of heaven, specifically addressing the nature of the Divine Trinity and the spiritual consequences for those who deny the Lord's divinity or separate faith from a good life.</meta>

the Father; that he who sees Him sees the Father; and that every thing that is holy goes forth from Him (*John* x. 30, 38; xiv. 9-11; xvi. 13-15).

**I** have often talked with angels on this subject, and they have invariably declared that in heaven they are unable to divide the **Divine** <term>Divine: the Latin "Divinum," used here as a noun to describe the essential nature of God</term> into three, because they know and perceive that the Divine is One and this One is in the Lord. They also declare that those of the church who come from this world having an idea of three Divine beings cannot be admitted into heaven, since their thought wanders from one Divine being to another; and it is not allowable there to think three and say one,¹ because in heaven every one speaks from his thought, speech there being the immediate product of the thought, or the thought speaking. Consequently, those in this world who have divided the Divine into three, and have adopted a different idea of each, and have not made that idea one and centred it in the Lord, cannot be received into heaven, because in heaven there is a sharing of all thoughts, and therefore if any one came thinking three while saying one he would be at once found out and rejected. But let it be known that all those who have not separated what is true from what is good, or faith from love, accept in the other life, when they have been taught, the heavenly idea of the Lord, that He is the God of the universe. It is otherwise with those who have separated faith from life, that is, who have not lived according to the precepts of a true faith.

**3.** Those within the church who have denied the Lord and have acknowledged the Father only, and have confirmed themselves in that belief, are not in heaven; and as they are unable to receive any **influx** <note>influx: the spiritual process by which life and thought flow from the Lord and heaven into human minds</note> from heaven, where the Lord alone is worshipped, they gradually lose the ability to think what is true about any subject whatever; and finally they either lose the power to speak or they talk stupidly, and ramble about with their arms dangling and swinging, as if weak in the joints. Again, those who, like the **Socinians** <term>Socinians: a sect that followed the teachings of Laelius and Faustus Socinus, who argued that Jesus was a person but did not possess a divine nature</term>, have denied the Divinity of the Lord and have acknowledged His Humanity only, are likewise not in heaven. **6.** There were certain spirits who, while living in the world, had claimed to believe in the Father; however, they viewed the Lord in the same way they viewed any other man, and therefore did not believe Him to be the God of heaven. Because of this, they were allowed to wander and search wherever they liked to see if there were any other heaven besides the heaven of the Lord. They searched for several days but found none. These were people who believed that the happiness of heaven consisted in fame and power. Because they were unable to get what they desired, and were told that heaven does not consist of such things, they became resentful. They wanted a heaven where they could rule over others and be distinguished by the same kind of glory found in the world.

## II.

## THE DIVINE NATURE OF THE LORD IS WHAT CREATES HEAVEN.

**7.** While the angels viewed as a whole are called "heaven"—because they are the ones who make it up—it is actually the Divine <note>original: "Divinum"; here referring to the essence or presence of God</note> that flows out from the Lord into the angels that truly constitutes heaven, both in general and in every detail. Since the Divine that comes from the Lord is the good of love and the truth of faith, the angels are only truly "angels" and "heaven" to the extent that they receive this good and truth from the Lord.

**8.** Everyone in the heavens knows, believes, and even feels that they cannot will or do anything good from themselves, nor can they think or believe anything true from themselves. They recognize that these things come only from the Divine, and thus from the Lord. They understand that "good" or "truth" originating from their own self is not truly good or true, because such things have no spiritual life from the Divine within them. Furthermore, the angels of the highest heaven <note>literally "the inmost heaven," the level of heaven closest to the Divine</note> clearly perceive and feel this influx <term>influx: from the Latin "influxus," referring to the constant spiritual flow of life, love, and light from God into the minds and hearts of people and angels</term>. The more of it they receive, the more they feel they are truly in heaven, because they are more fully immersed in love, faith, and the light of intelligence and wisdom, which brings them heavenly joy. Since all these things come from the Divine of the Lord, and it is in these things that the angels find their heaven, it is clear that it is the Lord’s Divine presence, and not the...

**9.** Because of their wisdom, angels go even further. They say that not only is every good and true thing from the Lord, but every spark of life itself comes from Him. They confirm this by the fact that nothing can arise from itself, but only from something that existed prior to it; therefore, all things spring from a First Cause, which they call the very Being <note>original: "Esse"; a Latin term for the essential nature or "to be-ness" of God</note> of the life of all things. In the same way, all things continue to exist because of Him, for continuous existence is a ceaseless "springing forth." Whatever is not held in an unbroken connection to this First Cause by means of intermediate steps instantly dies away and is completely scattered. They also say that there is only one Fountain of Life, and that a human being's life is like a small stream flowing from it; if it did not constantly continue to receive from its fountain, it would immediately dry up. [2.] Furthermore, they say that from this One Fountain of Life, which is the Lord, nothing flows out except Divine good and Divine truth. Each person is affected by these according to how they receive them. Those who receive them with faith and in their way of living find heaven within them, while those who reject or stifle them change them into hell; for they turn good into evil and truth into falsehood, and thus turn life into death. Again, they prove that every element of life is from the Lord by this: all things in the universe relate to good and truth—the life of a person’s will (which is the life of their love) relates to good, and the life of their understanding (which is the life of their faith) relates to truth. If everything good and true comes from above, it follows that every part of life must also come from above.

**[3.]** Because this is the core belief of the angels, they refuse all thanks for the good they do. They are even displeased and will distance themselves if someone tries to attribute goodness to them. They find it hard to understand how anyone can believe they are wise on their own or can do anything truly good from their own power. To an angel, doing good for the sake of one’s own reputation or benefit is not "good" at all, because it originates from the self. Instead, they recognize true goodness as that which is done for its own sake—which they call "good from the Divine" <note>original: "bonum a Divino"; the concept that true virtue is a reflection of God's character acting through a person</note>. This, they say, is the very essence that creates heaven, because this goodness is the Lord Himself.¹

**10.** Spirits who have spent their lives on earth convincing themselves that the good they do or the truths they believe originate from their own power—or belong to them personally—are not received into heaven. This includes everyone who attaches "merit" <note>original: "meritum"; the belief that one deserves a reward or spiritual status based on their own virtuous actions</note> to their good deeds or claims righteousness for themselves. The angels avoid such spirits, looking upon them as "stupid" and as "thieves." They are called stupid because they keep their focus on themselves rather than on the Divine; they are called thieves because they steal from the Lord the credit that belongs solely to Him. Such individuals are fundamentally opposed to the central reality of heaven: that it is the Lord’s Divine nature within the angels that makes heaven what it is.

**11.** The Lord teaches this principle—that those in heaven and in the church are in the Lord and the Lord is in them—when He says:

> “Abide in Me and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself except it abide in the vine, so neither can ye, except ye abide in Me. I am the Vine, ye are the branches. He that abideth in Me and I in him, the same beareth much fruit; for apart from Me ye can do nothing” (*John* xv. 4, 5).

**12.** From these points, it is clear that when the Lord dwells in the angels of heaven, He dwells in what is His own. Thus, the Lord is the "all in all" of heaven. This is because the goodness found in angels is actually the Lord’s presence within them; for whatever originates from the Lord is, in essence, the Lord. Consequently, to the angels, "heaven" consists of this goodness from the Lord, and not of anything belonging to their own self-nature <note>original: "proprium"; a technical term used by Swedenborg to describe the inherent human ego, which he views as being naturally void of spiritual life</note>.

### III.

## IN HEAVEN, THE DIVINE NATURE OF THE LORD IS LOVE FOR HIM AND CHARITY TOWARDS ONE'S NEIGHBOR.

**13.** The Divine power that radiates from the Lord is called "Divine Truth" in heaven, for reasons that will soon be explained. This Divine Truth flows into heaven from the Lord out of His Divine Love. The relationship between Divine Love and Divine Truth is like that of the sun’s fire and its light in our world: Love is like the fire of the sun, and Truth is like the light coming from it. Furthermore, through the law of <term>correspondence</term> <note>the spiritual principle where physical objects represent deeper spiritual realities</note>, <margin>|</margin> fire signifies love, and light signifies the truth that radiates from that love.¹

From this, it is clear that the Divine Truth coming from the Lord’s love is, in its essence, "Divine Good" joined with "Divine Truth." Because they are joined together, they give life to everything in heaven—just as in our world, when the sun’s heat is joined with its light, it makes the Earth fruitful during spring and summer. It is quite different when heat and light are not joined—when the light is cold, everything becomes numb and lies dead. For the angels, this "Divine Good" (compared to heat) is the good of love; and "Divine Truth" (compared to light) is the means through which that love is expressed and takes form.

**14.** The Divine presence in heaven which actually creates heaven is love, because love is a spiritual bond. It connects the angels to the Lord and to one another, joining them so closely that in the Lord’s sight, they are all as one. Moreover, love is the very <term>being</term> <note>original: "esse"; the fundamental essence or core existence of a thing</note> of everyone’s life; consequently, both angels and humans derive their life from love. Anyone who reflects on it can see that the deepest vitality of a human being comes from love, since a person grows warm in the presence of love and cold when it is gone.

**15.** In heaven there are two distinct loves: love for the Lord and love toward the neighbor. In the inmost or "third" heaven, love for the Lord prevails; in the second or "middle" heaven, it is love toward the neighbor. Both of these loves flow out from the Lord, and both together constitute heaven. How these two loves are distinct and how they are joined together is seen in heaven in clear light, but in our world, it is seen only obscurely. In heaven, "loving the Lord" does not mean loving Him for His person, but rather loving the **good** that comes from Him; and to love what is good is to will and to do it out of love. Similarly, "loving the <term>neighbor</term> <note>In this theology, 'neighbor' refers not to a nearby person, but to the spiritual quality or 'Truth' that a person embodies.</note>" does not mean loving a companion for their person, but loving the **truth** that comes from the Word; and to love truth is to will and to do it. This makes it clear that these two loves are as distinct as "good" and "truth" are distinct, and they are joined together just as good is joined with truth.² But this can scarcely be understood by people unless they know what love, good, and the neighbor truly are.³

This is because love is what receives everything that makes up heaven: peace, intelligence, wisdom, and happiness. Love is naturally receptive to anything that harmonizes with it; it yearns for these things, searches for them, and "drinks them in" almost instinctively, because it has an endless desire to be enriched and perfected by them. <note>Love contains countless qualities and naturally gathers everything that matches its nature.</note>

We can see this in human experience as well. In a person, love searches through the "storehouse" of the memory and pulls out everything that aligns with its feelings. It organizes these thoughts—keeping those that match its nature close to itself and treating others as servants—while discarding and pushing away anything that does not fit.

Once they were among the angels, they entered into **angelic wisdom** and **heavenly blessedness**. This happened because they had loved what was good and true for its own sake and had lived according to those values. By doing so, they had developed the capacity to receive heaven and all its indescribable wonders. 

In contrast, those who are consumed by love of self and love of the world have no capacity to receive what is good and true. They feel a loathing for it and reject it; at the first touch of heavenly light, they flee away and join those in **hell** who share their selfish desires. There were once certain spirits who doubted that heavenly love possessed such power, and they wanted to see if it were true. ### IV.

# HEAVEN IS DIVIDED INTO TWO KINGDOMS.

**20.** As there are infinite varieties in heaven, and no one society nor any one angel is exactly like any other,<sup>1</sup> there are in heaven general, specific, and particular divisions. The general division is into two <term>kingdoms: major organizational regions of heaven categorized by whether the inhabitants are primarily motivated by love for the Lord (the Celestial Kingdom) or by love for the neighbor (the Spiritual Kingdom).</term>, the specific into three heavens, and the particular into innumerable <term>societies: smaller communities of angels who share similar characters and types of goodness.</term>. **21.** There are angels that receive more interiorly <term>interiorly: in this context, "interior" refers to the deeper, more essential levels of the soul or mind</term> the Divine <note>original: *Divinum*; this refers to the spiritual energy or essence emanating from the Lord</note> that goes forth from the Lord, and others that receive it less interiorly; the former are called celestial angels, and the latter spiritual angels. **22.** As the angels that constitute the celestial kingdom receive the Divine of the Lord more interiorly they are called the interior or higher angels; and for the same reason the heavens that they constitute are called interior and higher heavens.² They are called higher and lower, because these terms designate what is interior and what is exterior.³ <note>Swedenborg uses spatial height as a metaphor for spiritual depth; "higher" does not mean physically above, but more central to the divine essence.</note>

**23.** Those who are in the celestial kingdom are in the love called celestial, which is love to the Lord. Those who are in the spiritual kingdom are in the love called spiritual, which is charity towards the neighbor. And as all good pertains to love (for good to any one is what he loves) the good also of the one kingdom is called celestial, and the good of the other spiritual. Evidently, then, the two kingdoms are distinguished from each other in the same way as good of love to the Lord is distinguished from good of love towards the neighbor.⁴ And as the good of love to the Lord is an interior good, and that love is interior love, so the celestial angels are interior angels, and are called higher angels.

->THERE ARE THREE HEAVENS.<-

# V.

## THERE ARE THREE HEAVENS.

**29.** There are three heavens, entirely distinct from each other: an inmost (or third), a middle (or second), and an outmost (or first). These follow the same order and relationship to each other as the highest part of man (the head), the middle part (the body), and the lowest part (the feet); or like the upper, middle, and lower stories of a house. The Divine influence that radiates and descends from the Lord follows this same order; consequently, by the very laws of order, heaven is threefold.

**30.** The interiors <note>The "interiors" refer to the inner levels of the human mind and soul, which Swedenborg describes as having distinct layers of depth.</note> of man, which belong to his mind and disposition, are also arranged in this same order. He has an inmost, a middle, and an outmost part; for when man was created, all aspects of Divine order were gathered together within him. He was created to be Divine order in a physical form, and consequently a heaven in miniature.¹ For this reason, a person's inner self is in constant communication with the heavens. After death, an individual joins the angels of either the inmost, middle, or outmost heaven, depending on how they accepted Divine good and truth from the Lord during their life in the world.

**31.** The Divine influence that flows in from the Lord and is received in the third or inmost heaven is called "celestial," and therefore the angels there are called celestial angels. The Divine influence that flows in from the Lord and is received in the second or middle heaven is called "spiritual," and consequently the angels there are called spiritual angels. Meanwhile, the Divine influence that flows in from the Lord and is received in the outmost or first heaven is

---

¹ All aspects of Divine order are brought together in man, and by creation, man is Divine order in form (references: n. 3628, 4219, 4220, 4223, 4523, 4524, 5114, 5168, 6013, 6057, 6605, 6626, 9706, 10156, 10472).
In man, the internal self was formed after the image of heaven, and the external self after the image of the world; this is why the ancients called man a "microcosm" <note>original: *microcosmus*; from the Greek meaning "small world," a concept suggesting that the human being reflects the structure of the entire universe.</note> (references: n. 3628, 4523, 5115, 6013, 6057, 9279, 9706, 10156, 10472).
Thus, in regards to his inner life, man is by creation a heaven in its smallest form, modeled after the greatest; man becomes this fully when he has been created anew or "regenerated" <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or transformation through living according to divine truths.</note> by the Lord (references: n. 911, 1900, 1928, 3624-3631, 3634, 3884, 4041, 4279, 4523, 4524, 4625, 6013, 6057, 9279, 9632).

connection from the First <note>The First: A term for the Lord or God, viewed as the primary source from which all existence flows.</note> to the Last that nothing unconnected is possible. **38.** Only he who knows how <term>degrees</term> <note>Degrees: Distinct levels of existence. This is a central concept in Swedenborg’s philosophy, used to explain how the spiritual world relates to the physical world without being made of the same "substance."</note> are related to <term>Divine order</term> <note>Divine Order: The inherent laws by which the universe is organized and maintained by God.</note> can comprehend how the heavens are distinct, or even what is meant by the internal and the external man. Most men in the world have no other idea of what is interior and what is exterior, or of what is higher and what is lower, than as something continuous, or coherent by continuity, from purer to grosser. But the relation of what is interior to what is exterior is discrete, not continuous. 

Degrees are of two kinds, those that are continuous and those that are not. Continuous degrees are related like the degrees of the waning of a light from its bright blaze to darkness, or like the degrees of the decrease of vision from objects in the light to those in the shade, or like degrees of purity in the atmosphere from its bottom upwards. These degrees are determined by distance. <margin>[</margin>[2.] On the other hand, degrees that are not continuous, but discrete, are distinguished like prior and posterior, like cause and effect, or like what produces and what is produced. Whoever looks into the matter will see that in each thing and all things in the whole world, whatever they are, there are such degrees of producing and compounding, that is, from one a second, and from that a third, and so on. 

[3.] Until one has acquired a perception of these degrees he cannot possibly understand the differences between the heavens, nor between the interior and exterior faculties of man, nor the difference between the spiritual world and the natural world, nor between the spirit of man and his body. So neither can he understand the nature and source of correspondences and representations, or the nature of influx. <term>Sensual men</term> <note>Sensual men: People who rely solely on their physical senses to understand reality, and are thus unable to perceive spiritual truths that transcend the material world.</note> do not apprehend these differences, for they make increase and decrease, even according to these degrees, to be continuous, and are therefore unable to conceive of what is spiritual otherwise than as a purer natural. And in consequence they remain outside of and a great way off from intelligence.²

² Things interior and things exterior are not continuous, but distinct <note>The note identifies that internal and external things are separated by "discrete degrees," meaning they exist on different planes of reality.</note>

->HEAVEN AND HELL<-

**39.** Finally, a certain <term>arcanum</term> <note>arcanum: a profound secret or mystery, often referring to knowledge hidden from the general public.</note> respecting the angels of the three heavens, which has not hitherto come into any one’s mind, because <term>degrees</term> <note>degrees: Swedenborg uses this to mean distinct levels of existence (like solid, liquid, gas) rather than a smooth gradient (like warm to hot).</note> have not been understood, may be related. In every angel and in every man there is an inmost or highest degree, or an inmost or highest something, into which the <term>Divine of the Lord</term> <note>The Divine of the Lord: The spiritual energy or "life-force" emanating from God.</note> first or most directly flows, and from which it disposes the other interiors in him that succeed in accordance with the degrees of order. This inmost or highest degree may be called the entrance of the Lord to the angel or man, and His veriest dwelling-place in them. It is by virtue of this inmost or highest that a man is a man, and is distinguished from the animals, which do not have it. From this it is that man, unlike the animals, is capable, in respect to all his interiors which pertain to his mind and disposition, of being raised up by the Lord to Himself, of believing in the Lord, of being moved by love to the Lord, and thereby beholding Him, and of receiving intelligence and wisdom, and speaking from reason. Also, it is by virtue of this that he lives to eternity. But what is arranged and provided by the Lord in this inmost does not distinctly fall into the perception of any angel, because it is above his thought and transcends his wisdom.

**40.** These are now the general truths respecting the three heavens; but in what follows the three heavens will be particularly treated of.

# VI.

**41.** The angels of each heaven are not together in one place, but are divided into larger and smaller societies in accordance with the differences of the good of love and faith in which they are <note>The text breaks off here; the continuation would describe how angels are grouped by their specific spiritual character.</note>.

One thing is formed from another, and the things so formed are not continuously purer and grosser <note>original references: n. 6326, 6465</note>.

Until the difference between what is interior and what is exterior according to such degrees is perceived, neither the internal and external man nor the interior and exterior heavens can be clearly understood <note>original references: n. 5146, 6465, 10099, 10181</note>.

**42.** Moreover, the angelic societies in the heavens are at a distance from each other as their goods differ in general and in particular. **43.** All who are in the same society are arranged in like manner in respect to each other; those who are more perfect—that is, who excel in good, thus in love, wisdom, and intelligence—being in the middle; those who are less pre-eminent being round about at a distance in accordance with the decrease of their perfection. The arrangement is like light diminishing from the middle to the circumference, those who are in the middle being in the greatest light, and those towards the circumference in less and less.

**44.** Like are drawn spontaneously as it were to their like; for with their like they are as if with their own and at home, but with others they are as if with strangers and abroad; also when with their like they are in their freedom, and consequently in every delight of life.

**56.** Again, heaven is where the Lord is acknowledged, believed in, and loved. Variety in worship of the Lord from the variety of good in different societies is not harmful, but beneficial, for the perfection of heaven is therefrom. This can scarcely be made clear to the comprehension without employing terms that are in common use in the learned world, and showing by means of these how unity, that it may be *perfect*, must be formed from variety. Every whole exists from various parts, since a whole without constituents is not anything; it has no form, and therefore no quality. But when a whole exists from various parts, and the various parts are in a perfect form, in which each attaches itself like a congenial friend to another in <term>series</term> <note>An ordered sequence or structured arrangement.</note>, then the quality also is perfect. So heaven is a whole from various parts arranged in a most perfect form; for the heavenly form is the most perfect of all forms. That this is the ground of all perfection is evident from the nature of all that is beautiful, pleasant, and agreeable, by which the senses and the mind are affected; for these qualities spring and flow from no other source than the concert and harmony of many concordant and congenial parts, either co-existing in order or following in order, and never from a whole without such parts. From this is the saying that variety gives delight; and the nature of variety, as is known, is what determines the delight. From all this it can be seen as in a mirror how perfection comes from variety even in heaven. For from the things that exist in the natural world the things of the spiritual world can be seen as in a *mirror*.<note>This "mirror" analogy refers to the idea that physical reality reflects spiritual truths, a concept known as "correspondence."</note>

**57.** What has been said of heaven may be said also of the church, for the church is the Lord’s heaven on earth. There are many churches, each one of which is called a church, and so far as the <term>good</term> <note>In Swedenborg's writing, "good" is not just a behavior but the spiritual essence of love and kindness that flows from the Divine.</note> of love and faith reigns therein is a church. Here, too, the Lord out of various parts forms a unity, that is, one church out of many churches.<sup>1</sup> And the same may be said of the man of the church in particular that is said of the church in general, namely, that the church is within man and not outside of him; and that every man is a church in whom the Lord is present in the good of love and of faith.<sup>2</sup> Again, the same may be said of a man that has the church in him as of an angel that has heaven in him, namely, that he is a church in the smallest form, as an angel is a heaven in the smallest form; and furthermore that a man that has the church in him, equally with an angel, is a heaven. ### VIII.

### ALL HEAVEN IN THE AGGREGATE REFLECTS A SINGLE MAN.

**59.** That heaven in its whole complex reflects a single man is a <term>sacred mystery</term> <note>original: "arcanum"; a profound spiritual truth previously hidden from human knowledge.</note> hitherto unknown in the world, but fully recognized in the heavens. To know this and the specific and particular things relating to it is the chief thing in the intelligence of the angels there, and on it many things depend which without it as a general principle would not enter distinctly and clearly into the ideas of their minds. Knowing that all the heavens with their societies reflect a single man they call heaven the **Greatest Man** <note>original: "Maximus Homo"</note> and the **Divine Man**;¹—Divine because it is the <term>Divine</term> <note>The essence of God's presence and power.</note> of the Lord that makes heaven (see above, n. 7-12).

**60.** That into such a form and image <term>celestial</term> <note>Related to the highest heaven and the principle of love.</note> and <term>spiritual</term> <note>Related to the middle heaven and the principle of wisdom or truth.</note> things are arranged and joined cannot be seen by those who have no right idea of spiritual and heavenly things. Such think that the earthy and material things of which man's <term>outmost nature</term> <note>The physical or external part of existence.</note> is composed are what make the man; and that apart from these man is not a man. But let them know that it is not from these that man is a man, but from his ability to understand what is true and to will what is good. Such **understanding** and **willing** are the spiritual and celestial things of which man is made. Moreover, it is acknowledged that every one's quality is determined by the quality of his understanding and will; and it can also be seen that his earthly body is formed to serve the understanding and the will in the world, and to skilfully accomplish their uses in the outmost sphere of nature. For this reason the body by itself can do nothing, but is moved always in entire subservience to the bidding of the understanding and will, even to the extent that whatever a man thinks he speaks with his tongue and lips, and whatever he wills he does with his body and limbs, and thus the understanding and the will are what act, while the body by itself does nothing. Evidently, then, the things of the understanding and will are what

**61.** Such being the angelic idea of man, the angels give no thought to what a man does with his body, but only to the **will** from which the body acts. This they call the man himself, and the **understanding** they call the man in the measure in which it acts in unison with the will.¹

For in the most perfect forms, the general whole is like its parts, and the parts are like the general whole, with simply such a difference as there is between like things of greater or less magnitude; consequently, as the angels claim, since the <term>Divine</term> <note>The underlying reality and power of God.</note> from what is inmost or highest sees all things, so in the Lord's sight heaven as a whole must be in the human form.

**63.** Such being the form of heaven, it is ruled by the Lord as a single man is ruled, thus as a one. Such likewise is heaven under the auspices and direction of the Lord.

EVERY ANGEL IN A COMPLETE HUMAN FORM.

It is evident how mistaken those are who believe that heaven may be closed by becoming full; for the opposite is true, that it will never be closed, but is perfected by greater and greater fullness. Therefore, the angels desire nothing so much as to have new angel guests come to them.

**72.** Each society, when viewed as a whole, appears as a man, for the reason that heaven as a whole so appears (as has been shown in the preceding chapter); moreover, in the most perfect form—such as the form of heaven is—there is a likeness of the parts to the whole, and of lesser forms to the greater. <note>This is a foundational concept in this philosophy: that the structure of the universe is "fractal" or holographic, meaning the same pattern of the "Grand Man" repeats from the highest level of heaven down to the individual.</note> The lesser forms and parts of heaven are the societies of which it consists, which are heavens in a smaller form (see sections 51–58). This likeness is perpetual because in the heavens the **good** <term>good: in this context, "good" (Latin: *bonum*) refers to the practical expression of love and the essence of a person's character</term> of everyone comes from a single love, that is, from a single origin. The single love, which is the origin of the good of all in heaven, is love to the Lord from the Lord. It is from this that the entire heaven in general, each society less generally, and each angel in particular, is a likeness of the Lord, as has been shown above (section 58).

->X.<-

## THEREFORE EVERY ANGEL IS IN A COMPLETE HUMAN FORM.

**73.** In the two preceding chapters it has been shown that heaven in its whole complex, and also each society in heaven, reflects a single man. From the sequence of reasons there set forth, it follows that this is equally true of each angel. As heaven is a man in its largest form, and a society of heaven is a man in a smaller form, so is an angel in the least. For in the most perfect form, such as the form of heaven is, there is a likeness of the whole in the part and of the part in the whole. This is so for the reason that heaven is a common sharing, for it shares all it has with each one, and each one receives all he has from that sharing. Because an angel is thus a recipient, he is a heaven in the least form, as shown above in its own chapter; and a person, so far as they receive heaven, is a recipient, a heaven, and an angel (see above, section 57). This is thus described in the Apocalypse <note>original: "Apocalypsi" — This refers to the Book of Revelation in the Bible.</note>:

HEAVEN AND HELL.

> "He measured the wall" of the holy Jerusalem, "a hundred and forty and four cubits, the measure of a man, which is that of an angel" (Revelation 21:17).

**"Jerusalem"** here signifies the Lord's church, and in a more exalted sense, heaven;¹ the **"wall"** signifies truth, which serves as a defense against the attacks of falsehoods and evils;² **"a hundred and forty and four"** signifies all the various "goods" and "truths" in one unified whole;³ **"measure"** signifies the essential quality of a thing;⁴ and a **"man"** signifies a person who contains these goods and truths in both general and specific ways—and thus, a person in whom heaven resides. Because an angel is defined by these same spiritual qualities, the text says **"the measure of a man, which is that of an angel."** This is the spiritual meaning of these words. Without this deeper perspective, how could anyone understand that "the wall of the Holy Jerusalem" could be "the measure of a man, which is that of an angel?"⁵

**74.** Let us now turn to direct experience. That angels are human forms, or men, is something I have witnessed a thousand times. I have spoken with them just as one person speaks to another, sometimes with one individual and sometimes with many together. I have seen nothing in their form that differs in any way from the human form; indeed, I have frequently been surprised to find them so identical to us. So that this would not be dismissed as a delusion or a trick of the imagination, I have been allowed to see angels while I was fully awake—possessing all my physical senses and in a state of clear mental perception. I have often told the angels that people in the Christian world are in such blind ignorance regarding spirits and angels that they believe them to be nothing more than formless "minds" <note>Swedenborg is critiquing the common 18th-century philosophical view that spirits were "incorporeal" or lacked any physical-like substance or shape.</note>

-># EVERY ANGEL IN A COMPLETE HUMAN FORM.<-

[...the people of the world think that angels are] without form, even pure thoughts, of which they have no idea except as something ethereal in which there is some vitality. And as they thus ascribe to angels nothing human except a thinking faculty, they believe that having no eyes they cannot see, having no ears they cannot hear, and having no mouth or tongue they cannot speak. **[2.]** To this the angels replied that they are aware that such a belief is held by many in the world, and is prevalent among the learned, and to their surprise, among the clergy. The reason, they said, is that the learned, who were the leaders and who first concocted this idea of angels and spirits, formed their ideas of them from the <term>sense-conceptions</term> <note>These are ideas derived strictly from the five physical senses, which can only perceive the material world.</note> of the <term>external man</term> <note>In this context, the "external man" refers to the part of human consciousness focused entirely on the physical, natural world.</note>; and those who think from these, and not from interior light and the general idea implanted in every one, must needs fabricate such notions, since the sense-conceptions of the external man take in only what belongs to nature, and nothing above nature, thus nothing whatever of the spiritual world.<gloss>1</gloss> From these leaders as guides this falsity of thought about angels extended to others who did not think from themselves but adopted the thoughts of their leaders; and those who first take their thoughts from others and make that thought their belief, and then view it with their own understanding, cannot easily recede from it, and in most cases are satisfied with confirming it. **[3.]** The angels said, furthermore, that the simple in faith and heart have no such idea about angels, but think of them as the men of heaven, and for the reason that they have not extinguished by learning what is implanted in them from heaven, and have no conception of anything apart from form. For a like reason angels in churches, whether sculptured or painted, are always depicted as men. In respect to this insight from heaven they said that it is the Divine flowing into such as are in the good of faith and life.

**75.** From all my experience, which is now of many years, I am able to state that angels are wholly men in form, having faces, eyes, ears, bodies, arms, hands, and feet; that they see [each other, hear each other, and talk together...]

**76.** However, it must be remembered that a person cannot see angels with their physical eyes, but only with the eyes of the spirit within them. It is even less capable of seeing things that exist above the realm of nature, which includes everything in the spiritual world.

## XI.

### IT IS FROM THE LORD’S <term>DIVINE HUMAN</term><note>The "Divine Human" is a central concept in Swedenborg's theology, referring to the belief that God became human to reach humanity, and that His humanity was subsequently made fully Divine.</note> THAT HEAVEN AS A WHOLE AND IN PART REFLECTS MAN.

**78.** That it is from the Lord’s Divine Human that heaven as a whole and in part reflects man, follows as a conclusion from all that has been stated and shown in the preceding chapters, namely: (i.) That the God of heaven is the Lord. (ii.) It is the Divine of the Lord that makes heaven. (iii.) Heaven consists of innumerable societies; and each society is a heaven in a smaller form, and each angel in the smallest form. (iv.) All heaven in the aggregate reflects a single man. (v.) Each society in the heavens reflects a single man. (vi.) Therefore every angel is in a complete human form. All this leads to the conclusion that as it is the Divine that makes heaven, heaven must be human in form. That this Divine is the Lord’s Divine Human can be seen still more clearly, because in a compendium, from what has been collected from the *<term>Heavenly Secrets</term>*<note>original: "Arcana Caelestia"; this is the author's most extensive work, an eight-volume commentary on the spiritual sense of Genesis and Exodus.</note> and placed as a supplement at the end of this chapter. That the Lord’s Human is Divine, and that it is not true that His Human is not Divine, as those within the church believe, is also shown in the same extracts, also in the chapter on The Lord, in *The New Jerusalem and its Heavenly Doctrine*, at the end.

**79.** That this true has been proved to me by much experience, about which something shall now be said. No angel in the heavens ever conceives of the Divine as being in any other than a human form; and what is remarkable, those in

**80.** Because the angels have no perception of an invisible Divine, which they call a Divine devoid of form, but perceive only a visible Divine in human form, they are accustomed to say that the Lord alone is man, and that it is from Him that they are men, and that each one is a man in the measure of his reception of the Lord. By receiving the Lord they mean receiving <term>good and truth</term><note>In this context, "good" refers to the intentions of the heart (love), and "truth" refers to the thoughts of the mind (wisdom). Together, they form the essence of a human being.</note> which are from Him, since the Lord is in His good and in His truth. This they call wisdom and intelligence. Every one knows, they say, that intelligence and wisdom make man, and not a face without these. The truth of this is made evident from the appearance of the angels of the interior heaven, for these, being in good and truth from the Lord and in consequent wisdom and intelligence, are in a most beautiful and most perfect human form; while the angels of the lower heavens are in human form of less perfection and beauty. On the other hand, those who are in hell appear in the light of heaven hardly as men, but rather as monsters, since they are not in good and truth but in evil and falsity, and consequently in the opposites of wisdom and intelligence. For this reason their life is not called life, but <term>spiritual death</term><note>A state where the soul is closed off from the light and love of heaven, resulting in a distorted, non-human spiritual appearance.</note>.

**82.** Because this perception of the Divine exists throughout the heavens, the idea of thinking of God in a human form is naturally <term>implanted</term><note>The author suggests this is an innate spiritual instinct rather than just learned behavior.</note> in every person who receives any <term>influx</term><note>A technical term referring to the spiritual "flow" of life, light, and influence from God into the human mind.</note> from heaven. This is how the people of ancient times thought of Him, and it is how people today—both inside and outside the church—think of Him when they are in a state of simple faith. Such simple-hearted people see Him in their thoughts as the "Ancient One" surrounded by shining light. However, this inner sight has been lost by those who have blocked the flow from heaven through their own <term>self-intelligence</term><note>Reliance on one's own ego and limited reasoning to the exclusion of spiritual wisdom.</note> or by living an evil life. Those who have snuffed out this insight through intellectual pride prefer the idea of an invisible God; those who have lost it through a life of evil prefer to believe in no God at all. Neither group is even aware that such an inner perception exists, because they do not possess it themselves. Yet, it is this very Divine influence that flows into a person from heaven, because humans are born for heaven, and no one can enter heaven without a clear concept of the Divine.

**83.** For this reason, anyone who has no concept of heaven—which is to say, no concept of the Divine from which heaven originates—cannot even be raised to the first threshold of the heavenly realm. As soon as such a person draws near to heaven, they feel a sense of resistance and a strong repulsion. This happens because their interior self, which ought to be open to receive heaven, is instead closed tightly because it is not in the "form of heaven." The closer they get to heaven, the more tightly those inner doors shut. This is the fate of those within the church who deny the Lord, and of those who, like the <term>Socinians</term><note>A historical theological group that followed the teachings of Lelio and Fausto Sozzini, who denied the full divinity of Jesus Christ, viewing him instead as a purely human moral teacher.</note>, deny His Divinity. As for those who are born outside the church and are ignorant of the Lord because they do not have <term>the Word</term><note>Refers to the Holy Scriptures or Divine Revelation.</note>, their situation will be described later in this work.

**84.** Evidence that the people of old had an idea of the Divine as human is found in the way the Divine appeared to Abraham, Lot, Joshua, Gideon, Manoah and his wife, and others. Although these figures saw God in the form of a man, they nevertheless worshipped Him as the God of the universe, calling Him the God of heaven and earth, and <term>Jehovah</term><note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, often translated as "The Lord."</note>. The Lord Himself teaches in the Book of John (8:56) that it was He who was seen by Abraham. That it was also He who appeared to the others is clear from His own words:

> No one has seen the Father, nor heard His voice, nor seen His form (*John* 1:18; 5:37).

**85.** However, the truth that God is a Human Being is difficult for those to grasp who judge all things based on the <term>sensual man</term><note>A person who relies entirely on physical senses and outward appearances rather than spiritual insight.</note>. This is because such a person can only think of the Divine in terms of the physical world. To them, a spiritual or Divine man must be exactly like a natural, physical man. From this perspective, they conclude that if God were a man, He would have to be as large as the entire universe; and if He ruled over heaven and earth, He would need to do so through many subordinates, much like an earthly king. If such a person were told that in heaven there is no "extension" of space as we know it on earth, they would not understand it at all. Those who think only from the light of nature must think in terms of the physical distances that appear before their eyes. 

But it is a great mistake to think this way about heaven. <term>Extension</term><note>The quality of occupying physical space or having dimensions (length, width, height).</note> in heaven is not like extension in our world. In our world, space is fixed and measurable, but in heaven, it is not. This concept of heavenly extension will be explained further when we discuss space and time in the spiritual world. Furthermore, everyone knows how far the physical eye can see—stretching even to the sun and stars—and anyone who thinks deeply realizes that our <term>internal sight</term><note>The mind's ability to perceive ideas and thoughts, which is not limited by physical distance.</note>, which is our thought, reaches even further. If our thoughts can travel so far, what can be said of the Divine Sight, which is the highest and most inward of all? Because thoughts have this kind of reach, everything in heaven is shared among those who live there, just as the Divine presence itself fills and makes heaven, as shown in previous chapters.

**86.** Those who live in heaven wonder how people on earth can consider themselves "intelligent" while believing that God is something invisible—that is, something that cannot be conceived in any form. They find it strange that these people label those who see God as a Human Being as "simple" or "unintelligent," when the opposite is actually true. The angels say, "Let those who think they are so intelligent examine themselves. Do they not end up treating nature as God—either the visible nature before them or some invisible force within it? Are they not so blind that they do not even know what God is, what an angel or spirit is, or what their own soul is which will live after death?" 

They point out that those they call "simple" actually understand these truths in their own way. These simple-hearted people have a clear idea of God as the Divine in a human form, they see an angel as a heavenly human, and they understand their own soul as something that is meant to live...

## XII.

### THERE IS A CORRESPONDENCE OF ALL THINGS OF HEAVEN WITH ALL THINGS OF MAN.

<margin>Ancient ways of knowing</margin>
<insert><image-desc>The number 87 is circled in pencil.</image-desc></insert>
**87.** At the present day, it is no longer known what <term>correspondence<note>The concept that every physical object or action in the natural world is a direct reflection or "outgrowth" of a specific spiritual reality.</note></term> is. There are several reasons for this, the most important being that humanity has distanced itself from heaven through the love of self and the love of the world. Those who prioritize themselves and material things above all else focus only on what is external; these things appeal to the physical senses and satisfy worldly desires. Such people ignore spiritual matters because these appeal to the inner mind and deeper senses. Consequently, they dismiss spiritual truths as being too abstract for their understanding. This was not the case for the ancient people. To them, the knowledge of correspondences was the most important of all sciences. Through this knowledge, they gained intelligence and wisdom, and those belonging to the church were able to communicate with heaven. This is because the knowledge of correspondences is the very language of angels. The most ancient people—who were <term>celestial men<note>A term describing people who lived in a state of direct, heart-centered love and perception of God, rather than relying on intellectual reasoning.</note></term>—thought in terms of correspondence, just as the angels do. Because of this, they were able to talk with angels and frequently saw and were taught by the Lord. But today, this knowledge has been so completely lost that people no longer even recognize the term.¹

**88.** Without a clear understanding of correspondence, we cannot truly grasp the nature of the spiritual world, how it flows into our natural world, or the relationship between the spiritual and the physical. We would remain ignorant of the human spirit—which we call the <term>soul</term>—and how it operates within the physical body, as well as our state after death. It is therefore necessary to explain exactly what correspondence is and how it works. This explanation will lay the foundation for everything that follows.

¹ See the author's work *Heavenly Secrets* <note>Original: "Arcana Cælestia." A multi-volume work where Swedenborg explains the spiritual meaning of the Bible.</note> regarding how much the knowledge of correspondences surpasses other sciences (n. 4280).
The knowledge of correspondences was the primary science of ancient peoples, but is now forgotten (n. 3021, 3419, 4280, 4749, 4844, 4964, 4966, 6004, 7729, 10252).
This knowledge was once widespread among Eastern nations and in Egypt (n. 5702, 6692, 7097, 7779, 9391, 10407).

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "correspondence," moving from the historical loss of this knowledge (noted on page 57) to a formal definition of how the spiritual and natural worlds interact. It specifically applies these concepts to the human body and mind.</meta>

->HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

**89.** First, we must define what **correspondence** is. The entire natural world reflects the spiritual world—not just in a general sense, but in every specific detail. Because of this, anything in the natural world that originates in the spiritual world is called a **correspondent**. It is important to realize that the natural world exists, and continues to exist, because of the spiritual world, just as an effect follows its <term>effecting cause<note>In this philosophy, a 'cause' is the spiritual intent or energy, and the 'effect' is the physical result we see in our world.</note></term>. All that exists under the sun and receives its heat and light constitutes the "natural world," along with everything that depends on those elements for survival. However, the "spiritual world" is heaven, and everything within the heavens belongs to that world.

**90.** Because a human being is both a "heaven" and a "world" in miniature, created in the image of the <term>Greatest World<note>Referring to the 'Macrocosm' or the 'Grand Man,' the idea that the universe and heaven are organized in the shape and function of a human being.</note></term> (as mentioned in section 57), both a spiritual and a natural world exist within each person. The inner things belonging to the mind—specifically the **understanding** and the **will**—make up one's spiritual world. Meanwhile, the outer things belonging to the body—its physical senses and actions—make up one's natural world. Therefore, everything in a person's natural world (the body and its senses) that arises from their spiritual world (the mind's thoughts and desires) is called a **correspondent**.

**91.** The human face is a perfect example of what correspondence looks like. In a face that has not been trained to hide its feelings, every emotion of the mind is visible in a natural form. This is why the face is often called the "index of the mind"; it is the spiritual world of the person showing itself in their natural world. In the same way, a person's thoughts are expressed in their speech, and their will is expressed in the movements of their body. Therefore, any physical result—whether it is a facial expression, a spoken word, or a movement—is called a **correspondence**.

**92.** This also clarifies the difference between the **internal** and **external** man. The internal man is what we call the spiritual man, and the external is the natural man. These two are as distinct from one another as heaven is from the physical world. Everything that happens or appears in the external/natural man originates from the internal/spiritual man.

**93.** Having discussed the correspondence between a person’s internal (spiritual) and external (natural) self, we now turn to the

### CORRESPONDENCE OF HEAVEN WITH THE HUMAN BEING

In this section, we will discuss how the whole of heaven corresponds to every part of the human being.

**94.** It has already been shown that the entire heaven reflects the form of a single person—it is, in essence, a human being in its greatest form, and is therefore called the <term>Greatest Man<note>Often referred to in Latin as the *Maximus Homo*; this is the concept that the entire spiritual universe is organized like a colossal human body, where every individual or group has a specific function similar to a cell or organ.</note></term>. It has also been shown that the societies of angels, which make up heaven, are arranged just like the members, organs, and <term>viscera<note>The internal organs of the body, such as the heart, lungs, and intestines.</note></term> in a human. Some societies are located in the "head," some in the "chest," some in the "arms," and so on, throughout every specific part of the body (as seen in sections 59–72). Consequently, the angelic communities in any given "member" of heaven correspond to the same part of the human body: those in the heavenly head correspond to the human head, those in the heavenly chest to the human chest, and so on. It is because of this connection—this correspondence—that human beings are able to exist and continue living; for humanity draws its life and continued existence from heaven alone.

**95.** Heaven is divided into two primary kingdoms: the **celestial kingdom** and the **spiritual kingdom** (as explained in an earlier chapter). 
*   The **celestial kingdom** corresponds generally to the **heart** and to everything connected to the heart throughout the body. 
*   The **spiritual kingdom** corresponds to the **lungs** and to everything connected to the lungs throughout the body. 

In the same way, the heart and lungs form two distinct systems within a person. The heart rules the body through the arteries and veins, while the lungs rule through the <term>tendinous and motor fibers<note>An older anatomical description referring to the way the breath and the movement of the chest coordinate the physical actions of the muscles.</note></term>; both work together in every movement we make. 

Furthermore, within every person's internal "spiritual world"—which we call the **spiritual man**—there are also two kingdoms: the **will** and the **understanding**. The will governs through the "affections for good" (our desires and loves), while the understanding governs through the "affections for truth" (our thoughts and beliefs). These internal kingdoms correspond directly to the physical kingdoms of the heart and lungs in the body. 

This same structure exists in the heavens: the celestial kingdom is the "will" of heaven, where the "good of love" is the ruling principle. The spiritual kingdom is the "intellect" of heaven, where "truth" is the ruling principle. Because of this deep connection, in <term>the Word<note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note></term>, the "heart" symbolizes the human will and the goodness of love, while the "breath" of the lungs symbolizes the understanding and the truth of faith. This is why we still describe our emotions and feelings as being "in the heart," even though physically they do not originate there.¹

**96.** The correspondence between the two kingdoms of heaven—the heart and the lungs—represents the general way heaven relates to a human being. However, there is also a more specific correspondence with each individual limb, organ, and internal <term>viscera<note>The internal organs of the body, such as the liver or kidneys.</note></term>; I will now explain this relationship. In the <term>Greatest Man<note>original: *Maximus Homo*; the concept that the entire spiritual universe is organized in the form of a human body.</note></term>, which is heaven, those who reside in the "head" surpass all others in every kind of excellence. They live in a state of love, peace, innocence, wisdom, and intelligence, which brings them immense joy and happiness. These heavenly qualities flow directly into the human head and everything associated with it. In the Greatest Man, those in the "breast" (or chest) live in the good of charity and faith; these qualities flow into the human chest and correspond to it. Those in the "loins" and the organs of generation in the Greatest Man are in <term>marriage love<note>original: *amor conjugialis*; a high spiritual state of committed, loving union between partners.</note></term>. Those in the "feet" represent the lowest level of heavenly goodness, known as spiritual-natural good. Those in the "arms and hands" represent the power that truth derives from goodness. Those in the "eyes" represent understanding; those in the "ears" represent attention and obedience; those in the "nostrils" represent perception; those in the "mouth and tongue" represent the ability to speak from understanding and perception. Those in the "kidneys" represent truths that search, separate, and correct; those in the "liver, pancreas, and spleen" represent various ways that goodness and truth are purified; and so it continues for the rest of the body. All these heavenly influences flow into the matching parts of a human being. This influx from heaven focuses on the functions and uses of the bodily members. Because these "uses" originate in the spiritual world, they take on a physical form using the materials found in the natural world, thus manifesting as physical effects. This relationship is what we call correspondence.

**97.** For this same reason, these limbs, organs, and viscera have the same symbolic meaning in <term>the Word<note>The Bible; Swedenborg teaches that the scriptures contain a hidden spiritual meaning based on these correspondences.</note></term>; every element mentioned there has a meaning based on these correspondences. Correspondences in the mineral kingdom are metals more and less noble, stones precious and not precious, earths of various kinds, and also the waters. Besides these, the things prepared from them by human activity are correspondences, such as foods of every kind, clothing, dwellings, and other buildings, along with many other things.

**105.** Also the things above the earth, such as the sun, moon, and stars, and those in the atmosphere, such as clouds, mists, rain, lightning, and thunder, are likewise correspondences. Things resulting from the presence and absence of the sun, such as light and shade, heat and cold, are also correspondences, as well as those that follow in succession from them, such as the seasons of the year—spring, summer, autumn, and winter—and the times of day—morning, noon, evening, and night.

**106.** In a word, all things that have existence in nature, from the least to the greatest, are correspondences. <note>Swedenborg suggests that the physical world is not an independent machine, but a "theatre" where spiritual realities are physically acted out.</note> They are correspondences because the natural world, with all things in it, springs forth and subsists from the spiritual world, and both worlds from the Divine. They are said to "subsist" also, because everything subsists from that from which it springs forth—subsistence being a permanent springing forth. <note>original: *subsistentia est perpetua existentia*. This means that existence is not a one-time event of creation, but a continuous flow of life from God. If that flow stopped for a second, the universe would vanish.</note> Also, nothing can subsist from itself, but only from that which is prior to itself—thus from a "First"—and if separated from that source, it would utterly perish and vanish.

**107.** Every thing in nature that springs forth and subsists in accordance with Divine order is a correspondence. Divine order is caused by the Divine good <term>Divine good: the warm, loving essence of God that provides the underlying structure and purpose for all of creation.</term> that flows forth from the Lord. It begins in Him, goes forth from Him through the heavens in succession into the world, and is terminated there in outmosts; <term>outmosts: the most external or physical level of reality. Think of it as the "skin" or the "foundation" where spiritual energy finally takes a solid, fixed form.</term> and

---

**108.** That all things in the world spring from the Divine, and are clothed with such things in nature as enable them to exist there and perform use, and thus to correspond, is clearly evident from the various things seen in both the animal and vegetable kingdoms. In both there are things that anyone who thinks interiorly can see to be from heaven. For illustration, a few things out of a countless number may be mentioned; and first, some things from the animal kingdom. Many are aware of the knowledge that is engrafted, as it were, in every animal. Bees know how to gather honey from flowers, to build cells out of wax in which to store their honey, and thus provide food for themselves and their families, even for a coming winter. That a new generation may be born, their queen lays eggs, and the rest take care of them and cover them. They live under a sort of government which all know by instinct. They preserve the working bees and cast out the drones, depriving them of their wings; besides many other wonderful things implanted in them from heaven for the sake of their use—their wax everywhere serving the human race for candles, and their honey for adding sweetness to food.

[**2.**] Again, what wonders do we see in worms <note>This likely refers to caterpillars and silkworms, often used as emblems of spiritual transformation in 18th-century literature.</note>, the meanest creatures in the animal kingdom! They know how to get food from the juice of the leaves suited to them, and afterwards, at the appointed time, to invest themselves with a covering and enter as it were into a womb, and thus hatch offspring of their own kind. Some are first turned into nymphs and chrysalids, spinning threads about themselves; and this travail being over, they come forth clad with a different body, furnished with wings with which they fly in the air as in their heaven, and pair together and lay eggs and provide for posterity.

Often when I have been in gardens and have been looking at the trees, fruits, flowers, and plants, I have recognized their correspondences in heaven. I have spoken with the spirits there who are associated with these things, and I have been taught where they come from and what they represent.

# CORRESPONDENCE OF HEAVEN WITH THE EARTH.

**110.** Today, however, no one can understand the spiritual realities in heaven that relate to the physical things in our world except through revelation from heaven, because the knowledge of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The principle that every physical object or action in the natural world reflects a specific spiritual quality or divine truth.</note> has been completely lost. I would like to illustrate the nature of this connection between spiritual and natural things with a few examples. 

The animals of the earth, in a general sense, correspond to <term>affections</term> <note>In this context, "affections" refer to our inner emotions, desires, or the various "feelings" that motivate us.</note>. Gentle and useful animals represent good affections, while fierce and useless ones represent evil affections. Specifically, cattle and their young correspond to the feelings of the <term>natural mind</term> <note>The part of our consciousness focused on the physical world and external life.</note>, while sheep and lambs represent the feelings of the <term>spiritual mind</term> <note>The higher part of our consciousness that relates to God, morality, and eternal life.</note>. Birds, depending on their species, correspond to the "intellectual things"—the thoughts and ideas—of either the natural or spiritual mind. 

For this reason, various animals—such as cows, oxen, calves, rams, sheep, goats, and lambs, as well as pigeons and turtledoves—were used for sacred purposes in the <term>Israelitish Church</term> <note>The ancient religious system of the Israelites, which Swedenborg describes as a "representative church" because its rituals were symbols of spiritual truths.</note>. They were used in sacrifices and burnt offerings because, in that context, they represented spiritual qualities. In heaven, these rituals were understood according to these symbolic meanings. Furthermore, because animals possess life, they are essentially "living affections"; the life of every animal comes solely from and acts according to its specific emotion or drive. Consequently, every animal is born with innate knowledge that matches its specific nature. In terms of his external or "natural" self, man is like an animal, which is why we often compare people to animals in everyday speech. For example, a gentle person is called a sheep or a lamb; a fierce person is called a bear or a wolf; a cunning person is called a fox or a snake, and so on.

**111.** There is a similar correspondence within the vegetable kingdom. In general, a garden represents the intelligence and wisdom found in heaven; and for this reason, heaven is often described as a paradise.
