**112.** How the joining together of heaven and the world is achieved by means of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The spiritual law where a natural object or action perfectly reflects a spiritual state or reality.</note> will also be explained in a few words. The Lord’s kingdom is a kingdom of <term>ends</term> <note>From the Latin "finis," meaning the ultimate purpose or goal behind any action.</note>, which are <term>uses</term> <note>From the Latin "usus," referring to practical service or the beneficial function something performs for the whole.</note>; or what is the same thing, a kingdom of uses which are ends. For this reason, the universe has been so created and formed by the Divine that uses may be everywhere "clothed" in such a way as to be expressed in action, or in effect—first in heaven and afterwards in the world—thus by degrees and one after another, down to the very lowest things of nature. 

Evidently, then, the correspondence of natural things with spiritual things, or of the world with heaven, is through uses, and uses are what join them together; the forms in which these uses are clothed are correspondences, and they act as connections exactly to the extent that they are forms of uses. In nature, throughout its <term>threefold kingdom</term> <note>The mineral, vegetable, and animal kingdoms.</note>, everything that exists according to the proper order consists of forms of uses, or effects shaped from a use for the sake of a use; this is why the things in nature are correspondences.

To love the Lord and the neighbor means, in a general sense, to perform uses.¹ Furthermore, it must be understood that a human being is the means by which the natural world and the spiritual world are joined; that is, a human being is

Consequently, to the extent that a person is spiritual, they act as the bridge of connection; but to the extent that a person is merely natural and not spiritual, they fail to be that bridge. Nevertheless, even without this human mediation, a <term>Divine influx</term> <note>The constant flow of life, light, and order from God into creation.</note> into the world and into the worldly things belonging to man continues, though it does not reach into the person’s <term>rational faculty</term> <note>The part of the mind capable of logical thought and spiritual understanding.</note>.

**113.** Just as all things that align with <term>Divine order</term> <note>The laws and structure by which God governs the universe.</note> correspond to heaven, so all things contrary to Divine order correspond to hell. Everything corresponding to heaven relates to what is good and true; but those things corresponding to hell relate to what is evil and false.

**114.** Something must now be said about the knowledge of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The spiritual science of how natural things represent and act in unison with spiritual realities.</note> and its practical use. It was mentioned earlier that the spiritual world, which is heaven, is joined to the natural world by means of these correspondences; therefore, it is through correspondences that communication with heaven is granted to humanity. The angels of heaven do not think from natural things the way humans do. However, when a person has acquired a knowledge of correspondences, they are able—in their thoughts—to be associated with the angels. In this way, their spiritual or "internal" self is joined with them. 

To ensure such a connection between heaven and humanity, the <term>Word</term> <note>Referring to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> was written entirely through correspondences, where every single detail acts as a counterpart to a spiritual reality. If a person understood correspondences, they would understand the spiritual sense of the Bible, and would thereby gain knowledge of <term>arcana</term> <note>From the Latin "arcana," meaning deep secrets or hidden mysteries.</note> of which they see nothing in the literal letter of the text. In the Word, there is a literal sense and a spiritual sense: the literal sense consists of things found in this world, while the spiritual sense consists of things found in heaven. Such a Word—in which every tiny detail is a correspondence—was given to humanity specifically because the connection between heaven and the world is maintained through these relationships.

# CORRESPONDENCE OF HEAVEN WITH THE EARTH.

**115.** I have been taught from heaven that the <term>most ancient men</term> <note>Referring to the earliest era of human history, characterized by direct spiritual perception.</note> on earth, who were <term>celestial men</term> <note>People whose lives were governed by love for God and direct connection to the spiritual realm.</note>, thought directly through **correspondences** themselves. The natural things of the world before their eyes served as the means for this way of thinking. Because they thought in this way, they were able to be in fellowship with angels and talk with them, and thus through them heaven was <term>conjoined</term> <note>Joined together or united.</note> to the world. For this reason, that period was called the **Golden Age**; ancient writers said of this time that the inhabitants of heaven lived with men and associated with them as friends with friends. 

But after this, a period followed when men thought not from correspondences themselves, but from a *knowledge* of correspondences. There was still a connection between heaven and man during this time, but it was less intimate. This period was called the **Silver Age**. After this, men still had a knowledge of correspondences but did not think from that knowledge, because they were in <term>natural good</term> <note>A state of being motivated by simple kindness or tradition rather than deep spiritual insight.</note>, rather than being in <term>spiritual good</term> <note>Goodness motivated by a conscious understanding of spiritual truth and faith.</note> like those before them. This period was called the **Copper Age**. 

After this, men gradually became focused on external things, and finally became <term>corporeal</term> <note>Entirely focused on the physical body and its senses, ignoring the soul or spiritual life.</note>. At that point, the knowledge of correspondences was completely lost, and with it, the knowledge of heaven and the many things belonging to heaven. It was because of these correspondences that these ages were named after gold, silver, and copper—specifically because, in the language of correspondences, **gold** signifies <term>celestial good</term> <note>The highest form of love and goodness originating from God.</note> (in which the most ancient people lived), **silver** signifies **spiritual good** (the focus of the ancient people who followed), and **copper** signifies **natural good** (the state of the next generations). Meanwhile, **iron**—from which the last age takes its name—signifies hard truth separated from goodness.

**Copper** signifies natural good (see sections 425, 1551).
**Iron** signifies truth in the <term>outmost of order</term> <note>The lowest or most external level of reality.</note> (see sections 425, 426).

### XIV.
## THE SUN IN HEAVEN.

**116.** In heaven, neither the sun of our physical world nor anything originating from that sun is visible, because that sun is entirely <term>natural</term> <note>Meaning it belongs to the physical world of matter, space, and time.</note>. In fact, the natural world begins with that sun, and anything produced through its influence is called "natural." However, the <term>spiritual</term> realm <note>The realm of mind, soul, and life itself, which exists independently of physical matter.</note>—to which heaven belongs—exists above nature and is entirely distinct from what is natural. There is no direct communication between these two realms except through **correspondences** <note>The functional relationship where a natural object reflects or represents a spiritual reality.</note>. The nature of this distinction can be understood from what was previously stated regarding <term>degrees</term> <note>referring to discrete levels of existence, such as the difference between a thought and the action that follows it; see paragraph 38.</note>, and the way they communicate can be understood from the two previous chapters on correspondences.

**117.** Even though the sun of our world is not seen in heaven, nor anything belonging to it, there is still a sun there, as well as light and heat. All things found in our world—and countless others—exist there too, though they do not share the same origin. This is because everything in heaven is spiritual, while everything in our world is natural. The **Sun of heaven** is the **Lord** <note>In this context, "the Lord" refers to God as the source of all life and love.</note>. The light in heaven is <term>Divine Truth</term>, and the heat is <term>Divine Good</term>; both radiate from the Lord as if from a sun. All things that appear or exist in the heavens originate from this source. While the following chapters will explore this light, heat, and the objects they create, this chapter focuses specifically on the Sun itself. The Lord appears in heaven as a sun because He is **Divine Love**, which is the source of all spiritual existence—just as the physical sun is the source of all natural existence. It is that Love which shines as a sun.

**118.** I have not only been told by angels that the Lord is actually seen in heaven as a sun, but I have also been granted the opportunity to see it myself many times. I will briefly describe what I have heard and seen regarding the Lord as a sun. The Lord is seen as a sun not within heaven itself, but high above the heavens. He is not positioned directly overhead or at the <term>zenith</term> <note>The highest point in the sky directly above an observer.</note>, but appears before the faces of the angels at a middle height. He is seen at a great distance, appearing in two distinct locations: one before the right eye and the other before the left eye. Before the right eye, He appears exactly like a sun, possessing a similar radiant glow and size as our physical sun...

**121.** However, when the Lord appears within heaven—which happens frequently—He does not appear surrounded by a sun. In heaven, it is a common phenomenon for people to appear present in the specific place where their "look" or attention is focused, even if that place is far from where they actually are. # HEAVEN AND HELL.

**122.** To the angels, the sun of our natural world appears as a dense darkness, positioned directly opposite the sun of heaven. Likewise, the moon of our world appears as a darkness opposite to the moon of heaven. This is a constant state of affairs. The reason for this is that the heat or "fieriness" of this world corresponds to the <term>love of self</term>, and the light it produces corresponds to <term>falsity</term> <note>In this context, "falsity" refers to distorted thinking or "fake truths" that justify selfish behavior.</note> arising from that love. Because the love of self is the direct opposite of Divine love, and its resulting falsity is the direct opposite of Divine truth, these things appear as total darkness to the angels. 

Therefore, in the <term>Word</term> <note>The common term used in these writings for the Sacred Scriptures or Bible.</note>, to worship the sun and moon of this world and to bow down to them signifies a devotion to the self and the lies that spring from selfish desires. It is written that those who do so will be "cut off" <note>original: "exscindantur"; referring to being spiritually separated from the source of life.</note> (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3–5; Jeremiah 8:1, 2; Ezekiel 8:15, 16, 18; Revelation 16:8 <note>original: "Apoc." refers to the Apocalypse or Book of Revelation.</note>; Matthew 13:6).¹

**123.** Because the Lord appears as a sun in heaven due to the Divine love within Him, all those in the heavens are constantly turned toward Him. Those in the <term>celestial kingdom</term> <note>The highest level of heaven, where residents act from pure love.</note> turn to Him as a sun, while those in the <term>spiritual kingdom</term> <note>The second level of heaven, where residents act from intellectual truth and charity.</note> turn to Him as a moon. However, those in hell turn themselves away toward the opposite darkness. They turn their backs to the Lord because everyone in the hells is in the love of self and the world, and is therefore antagonistic to Him. 

Those who turn toward the thick darkness where our world’s sun would be are located in the "back" hells and are called <term>genii</term> <note>Evil spirits who act primarily from the will and hidden emotions.</note>. Those who turn toward the darkness where the moon would be are in the "front" hells and are called <term>spirits</term> <note>In this specific context, those who act from intellectual errors and false beliefs.</note>. This is why it is said that those in hell are in "darkness" and those in heaven are in "light"—darkness signifies the falsity that comes from evil, and light signifies the truth that comes from good. 

They turn in these directions because, in the life after death, everyone looks toward whatever rules their <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner state of the heart and mind.</note>; they look toward their deepest loves. For angels and spirits, these internal states actually determine the direction of the face. In the spiritual world, the "quarters" (north, south, east, and west) are not fixed as they are in our physical world, but are—

Man's spiritual light is the light of his understanding, and the objects of that light are truths, which he arranges analytically into groups, forms into reasons, and from them draws conclusions in series.² The natural man does not know that the light from which the understanding sees such things is the real light, for he neither sees it with his eyes nor perceives it by thought. And yet there are many who recognize this light, and distinguish it from the natural light in which those are who think naturally and not spiritually. Those think naturally who take account of the world only, and attribute all things to nature; while those think spiritually who take account of heaven and attribute all things to the Divine. It has often been granted me to perceive and also to see that there is a true light that enlightens the mind, wholly distinct from the light that is called natural light (*lumen*). <note>Swedenborg distinguishes between *lux* (spiritual light) and *lumen* (natural or reflected light).</note> I have been raised up interiorly into that light by degrees; and as I was raised up my understanding became so enlightened as to enable me to perceive what I did not perceive before, and finally such things as I could not even comprehend by thought from natural light. **136.** Angels, like men, have understanding and will. The light of heaven constitutes the life of their understanding, because that light is Divine truth and Divine wisdom therefrom; and the heat of heaven constitutes the life of their will, because that heat is Divine good and Divine love therefrom. The <term>veriest</term> <note>Meaning the most essential or true form of life.</note> life of the angels is from heat, and from light only so far as heat is in it. That heat is the source of life is shown by the fact that when heat is taken away life perishes. The same is true of faith without love or of truth without good; since the truth that is called truth of faith is light, and the good that is called good of love is heat.¹ This is more clearly shown by the heat and light of the world, to which the heat and light of heaven <term>correspond</term> <note>"Correspondence" is the idea that every natural thing on earth has a spiritual counterpart or cause in heaven.</note>. By the world's heat when conjoined with light, as in spring and summer, all things on the earth are quickened and grow, but by light separate from heat nothing is quickened or grows, but everything lies <term>torpid</term> <note>Inactive or dormant, like a hibernating animal or a frozen plant.</note> and dies. This takes place in winter, when heat is absent though light remains. From this correspondence heaven is called paradise, since truth is there united with good, or faith with love, as light is with heat in springtime on the earth. All this makes more clear the truth set forth in its own chapter (n. 13–19), that *The Divine of the Lord in Heaven is love to Him and Charity towards the Neighbor.*

**140.** Because the Lord, appearing as a sun, is Divine Love, and Divine Love is the essence of Divine Good, the energy that flows from Him into heaven is called **Divine Truth** for the sake of clarity—even though it is actually Divine Good and Divine Truth joined together. This flowing Divine Truth is what is referred to as the "Holy" influence that proceeds from Him.

### XVI.

## THE FOUR DIRECTIONS IN HEAVEN.

**141.** In both heaven and the physical world, there are four quarters: east, south, west, and north. In each world, these directions are determined by its sun; in heaven by the Sun of Heaven, which is the Lord, and in our world by the physical sun. Yet, there are significant differences between them.

First, in our world, the "south" is defined as the point where the sun reaches its highest altitude above the earth; "north" is the opposite position; "east" is where the sun rises during the equinox; and "west" is where it sets. Thus, in the physical world, all directions are determined by the south. 

In heaven, however, the **east** is wherever the Lord is seen as a sun. Directly opposite to Him is the west; to the right is the south, and to the left is the north. This remains the case regardless of which way an angel turns their face or body. Therefore, in heaven, all directions are determined by the east. We use the term "East" <note>original Latin: *oriens*, meaning "rising" or "east"</note> because the "origin" <note>original Latin: *origo*</note> of all life is from the Lord as the sun. Furthermore, as the angels receive heat and light (representing love and intelligence) from the Lord, He is said to "arise" <note>original Latin: *exoriri*</note> upon them. For this same reason, the Lord is called "the East" in <term>the Word</term> <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note>.¹

**142.** Another difference is that for the angels, the east is always directly before their faces, the west is behind them, and the south is to their right, <note>In the highest sense, the Lord is the East because He is the Sun of Heaven, which is eternally rising and never sets (references: 101, 5097, 9668).</note>

---

<summary>This page explains that heaven's directions are oriented entirely toward the Lord as the Sun/East, unlike the physical world which is oriented toward the south. It defines Divine Truth as the "Holy" radiation of the Lord's Divine Love.</summary>

...and the north to the left. <note>This sentence completes the thought from the previous page: in heaven, the Lord is the East, making the West opposite Him, the South to the right, and the North to the left.</note> But since this cannot be easily comprehended in the world—for the reason that men turn their faces toward every quarter—it shall be explained. The entire heaven turns itself to the Lord as to its common center; thus all the angels turn themselves to Him. Also on the earth, as is well known, there is a directing of all things towards a common center; but there is this difference between this directing in the world and that in heaven: in heaven, the front parts of the body <note>the face and chest</note> are turned to the common center, but in the world, the lower parts of the body <note>the feet and base</note> are directed there. In the world, this directing is called <term>centripetal force</term> <note>original Latin: *vis centripeta*; the force that pulls an object toward a center</note>, and also <term>gravitation</term>. The <term>interiors</term> <note>original Latin: *interiora*; the inner levels of the mind, soul, and will</note> of angels are actually turned forwards; and since these interiors manifest themselves in the face, it is the face that determines the quarters.¹

**143.** *It is still more difficult to comprehend in the world that in every turning of the face and body, the angels have the east before their face, since a person in our world, according as he turns, has every quarter before his face. This, then, must be explained.* Although angels, like men, turn and direct their faces and bodies in every direction, they nevertheless have the east always before their eyes. But the turnings of angels are unlike the turnings of men, because they arise from a different origin. They appear the same, but they are not. The origin of these turnings is their <term>ruling love</term> <note>original Latin: *amor regnans*; the fundamental desire or motivation that governs a person’s entire character</note>, and by this all directions with angels and spirits are determined. For, as just said, their interiors are actually turned towards their common center, which in heaven is the Lord as a sun; consequently, their ruling love is always before their face. This is because their love is always before their interiors, and the face has its existence from the interiors and is their outward form. # THE FOUR QUARTERS IN HEAVEN

**148.** All those in the heavens have their own places of residence determined by the four quarters <note>The "four quarters" refer to the cardinal directions: East, West, North, and South.</note>. Those who live in the "good of love" <note>In this context, "good" refers to the lived expression of love.</note> dwell toward the east and west; those who have a clear perception of this love live toward the east, while those with a more obscure or dim perception of it live toward the west. Those who live in wisdom derived from the good of love dwell toward the north and south—those in the clear light of wisdom toward the south, and those in the obscure light of it toward the north. 

The angels of the Lord's spiritual kingdom and those of His celestial kingdom <note>The celestial kingdom is the highest heaven (focused on love), and the spiritual kingdom is the second heaven (focused on truth and charity).</note> live in this same arrangement, though their positions differ because their quality of love and light of truth are different. In the celestial kingdom, love is directed toward the Lord, and the resulting light of truth is called wisdom. In the spiritual kingdom, however, love is directed toward the neighbor (which is called charity), and the resulting light of truth is called intelligence or faith (see above, section 23). As mentioned previously (section 146), the quarters in these two kingdoms also differ from each other by thirty degrees.

**149.** The angels within each specific heavenly society <note>A "society" is a community of angels who share similar spiritual qualities.</note> live in this same relationship to one another. Toward the east are those in a greater degree of love and charity, and toward the west are those in a lesser degree. Toward the south are those in greater light of wisdom and intelligence, and toward the north are those in less. This arrangement exists because every society represents heaven as a whole and is a version of heaven in a smaller form (see above, sections 51–58). This same order is maintained in their public assemblies. 

They are brought into this order naturally by the very "form of heaven," through which everyone intuitively knows their own place. The Lord also ensures that every society contains a variety of individuals so that the form of heaven remains consistent everywhere. Yet, the arrangement of the entire heaven differs from that of a single society in the way a whole differs from its parts: the societies toward the east are more excellent than those toward the west, and those toward the south surpass those toward the north.

**150.** Because of this, the quarters in the heavens signify the specific qualities of those who live there. The east signifies love and its "good" clearly perceived; the west signifies the same—

***

And "the Lord's blood" signifies Divine truth and the holiness of faith (see *Arcana Coelestia* <note>original: "n." followed by numbers; these refer to specific paragraph numbers in Swedenborg's multi-volume work, *Arcana Coelestia* (Heavenly Secrets).</note> nos. 4735, 6978, 7317, 7326, 7846, 7850, 7877, 9127, 9393, 10026, 10033, 10152, 10210).

...obscurely perceived, the south signifies wisdom and intelligence in clear light, and the north signifies the same in obscure light. Because the quarters have these meanings in heaven, they have the same meanings in the internal or spiritual sense of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible; the "internal sense" is the author’s term for a deeper, symbolic meaning hidden beneath the literal text.</note>, since the spiritual sense of the Word is in perfect harmony with the realities of heaven.

**151.** The opposite is true for those in the hells. They do not look toward the Lord as a sun or a moon; instead, they look backward, away from the Lord, toward the thick darkness that exists where the sun of our world would be, and toward the darkness where the earth's moon would be. Those known as *genii* <term>genii: in this context, refers to those in hell who are driven by evil desires of the will, rather than false thoughts of the intellect</term> look toward the darkness of the "sun," while those known as *spirits* <note>In the author's terminology, "spirits" often refers specifically to those in the spiritual world who are not yet fully settled in heaven or hell, or here, those in hell who focus on false ideas rather than pure evil intent.</note> look toward the darkness of the "moon."² It was shown earlier (section 122) that the sun and moon of our physical world are not visible in the spiritual world; instead, in place of that sun, there is a mass of dense darkness opposite the sun of heaven, and in place of that moon, there is a darkness opposite the moon of heaven. 

For this reason, the quarters for those in the hells are the exact opposite of the quarters in heaven. To them, the "east" is where that dense darkness lies; the "west" is where the sun of heaven is; the "south" is to their right, and the "north" is to their left. This orientation remains constant regardless of how they turn their bodies. They are unable to face any other way because the entire inclination and resulting direction of their interiors <term>interiors: the inner spiritual or mental state of a person</term> strives in that direction. As shown before (section 143), the inner direction of everyone in the afterlife is determined by their love. The love of those in the hells is the love of self and the love of the world. These loves are symbolized by the sun and moon of our physical world (see section 122), and they are the direct opposites of love for the Lord and love for one's neighbor.³ This is why these individuals turn their backs on the Lord and face the dense darkness.

**155.** Angels are not always in the same state in respect to love, or in the same state in respect to wisdom; for all their wisdom is from their love and in accordance with their love. Sometimes they are in a state of intense love, sometimes in a state of love not so intense. The state decreases by degrees from its greatest degree to its least. When in their greatest degree of love they are in the light and warmth of their life, or in a clear and delightful state; but in their least degree they are in shade and cold, or in an obscure and undelightful state. From this last state they return again to the first, and so on, these alternations following one after another with variety. There is a sequence of these states like the varied states of light and shade, or of heat and cold, or like morning, noon, evening, and night, day after day in the world, with unceasing variety throughout the year. Moreover, there is a <term>correspondence: the spiritual principle that every natural object or event reflects a specific spiritual reality</term> between times and states, morning corresponding to the state of their love in its clearness, noon to the state of their wisdom in its clearness, evening to the state of their wisdom in its obscurity, and night to a state of no love or wisdom. But it must be understood that there is no correspondence of night with the states of life of those in heaven, although there is what corresponds to the dawn that precedes morning; what corresponds to night is with those in hell.¹ From this correspondence "day" and "year" signify in the **Word** <note>The Word: A term referring to the Bible, which the author believes contains a hidden, symbolic meaning regarding spiritual life.</note> states of life in general; "heat" and "light" signify love and wisdom; "morning" the first and highest degree of love; "noon" wisdom in its light; "evening" wisdom in its shade; "dawn" the obscurity that precedes the morning; and "night" the absence of love and wisdom.²

### CHANGES OF STATE OF THE ANGELS. ###

**156.** Along with the changing states of the angels' inner lives—specifically their love and wisdom—the appearance of the world around them changes as well. The things they see with their eyes take on a form that matches what they are feeling and thinking within. What these external things are, and what they look like, will be described soon in the chapter on Representatives and Appearances in Heaven.

**157.** Every angel, and every angelic society as a whole, passes through these changes of state. However, everyone experiences them differently because no two angels are identical in their love and wisdom. Those in the "center" of a society exist in a more perfect state than those toward the edges <note>This refers to the spiritual geography mentioned in sections 43 and 128, where those with the most intense love dwell at the heart of a community</note>. It would be a long task to list every specific difference, but essentially, the cycles each person experiences are determined by the specific quality of their love and faith. Consequently, while one angel may be in a state of bright clarity and joy, another in the same society might be in a state of dimness and lack of delight at the very same time. These states also vary between different societies, such as the difference between those in the celestial kingdom <note>the kingdom characterized by love for the Lord</note> and those in the spiritual kingdom <note>the kingdom characterized by charity toward the neighbor</note>. These fluctuations are much like the varying climates of Earth, where it is morning for some while it is evening for others, or summer for some while others are in winter.

**158.** I have been taught from heaven why these changes of state exist. The angels explained that there are several reasons. First, the joy of heaven and the delight of life—which they receive from the Lord through love and wisdom—would slowly lose its value if they remained in it constantly. This is much like what happens to people on earth who lose their appreciation for pleasures and attractions when there is no variety. A second reason is that angels, like humans, have a <term>proprium: an inherent sense of self or "own-hood" which, if left to itself, tends toward self-love</term> <note>original: "proprium"</note>. Everyone in heaven is carefully held away from this self-centered state by the Lord. To the extent that they are held away from their "self," they are in a state of love and wisdom; but to the extent that they...

->TIME IN HEAVEN.<-

I was told that this is the fourth state for those in the <term>celestial kingdom<note>The highest region of heaven, where life is defined by a direct, heartfelt love for the Lord.</note></term> and the first state for those in the <term>spiritual kingdom<note>The second region of heaven, where life is defined by an intellectual love for truth and neighborly charity.</note></term>. For them, "heaven" consists in being held away from their own self-interest.

## XVIII.

### TIME IN HEAVEN.

**162.** Although there is a succession and a progression of all things in heaven just as there is in the world, angels have no concept or idea of time and space; in fact, they do not even know what time and space are. We will consider time in heaven here, and address space in its own dedicated chapter.

**163.** Angels do not know what "time" is, even though everything with them moves forward in a continuous sequence just as it does in our world, without any difference at all. This is because, in heaven, they do not have years and days; instead, they experience "changes of state."

<summary>This page concludes the explanation of how the Sun of Heaven appears to change based on an angel's spiritual state and introduces the concept that heaven operates through "changes of state" rather than linear time.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the nature of time in the spiritual world, specifically how the concept of time is replaced by the concept of "state" among angels. ->HEAVEN AND HELL<-

...and where there are years and days there are times, but where there are changes of state there are states.

**164.** In the world, time exists because the sun of our physical world appears to move in a steady progression from one degree to another, creating the periods we call the seasons of the year. It also appears to revolve around the earth, creating the periods we call times of day; both of these occur in predictable, fixed cycles. With the sun of heaven, it is quite different. This sun does not mark years and days through physical movement or revolutions. Instead, it marks changes of <term>state<note>In this context, "state" refers to an angel's internal spiritual condition—their level of love, wisdom, and closeness to the Divine.</note></term> by the way it appears to the angels. As shown in the previous chapter, these changes do not happen in fixed cycles. Consequently, angels cannot conceive of "time" as we do; instead, they have an idea of "state" (see above, section 154).

**165.** Just as angels have no concept of time like people in the world, they also have no understanding of time-related terms. They do not even know the meaning of words like "year," "month," "week," "day," "hour," "today," "tomorrow," or "yesterday." When angels hear these terms used by humans—for the Lord always keeps angels closely associated with people—they perceive spiritual states and things related to those states instead. In this way, the natural thought of a human is transformed into spiritual thought for the angel. This is why "times" in the <term>Word<note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible or Sacred Scripture, which he believes contains a hidden spiritual meaning.</note></term> signify internal states, and why specific time-related words signify corresponding spiritual concepts.<sup>1</sup>

**166.** The same principle applies to everything that arises from time, such as the four seasons of the year (spring, summer, autumn, and winter); the four periods of the day (morning, noon, evening, and night); and the four ages of man (infancy, youth, manhood, and old age). It applies to all other things that either exist because of time or follow a sequence based on time. In thinking of...

Spring and morning are transformed into an idea of the state of love and wisdom as they exist in angels in their "first state"; summer and noon are transformed into an idea of love and wisdom as they exist in their "second state"; autumn and evening represent the "third state"; while night and winter represent a state such as exists in hell. This is why these periods of time have a similar symbolic significance in the <term>Word<note>Swedenborg's term for the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note></term> (see above, n. 155). This makes it clear how natural things in the thoughts of a human become spiritual for the angels who are present with that person.

**167.** Since angels have no concept of time, they have an idea of eternity that is different from the one held by people on earth. To the angels, eternity signifies an infinite <term>state<note>In this context, "state" refers to an internal spiritual condition—the quality of one's love or wisdom—rather than a duration of years.</note></term>, not infinite time.<note>original: "Eternitas angelis significat statum infinitum, non tempus infinitum."</note> I was once reflecting on the nature of eternity and, using the human idea of time, I was able to perceive what "to eternity" means (namely, existence without end); however, I could not grasp what "from eternity" meant—that is, what God did from eternity before the creation of the world. When anxiety over this arose in my mind, I was lifted up into the sphere of heaven, and thus into the perception that angels have regarding eternity. It was then made clear to me that eternity must not be thought of in terms of time, but in terms of state; once this is done, the meaning of "from eternity" can be clearly seen, as happened to me then.

**168.** When angels speak with men, they never express themselves using ideas specific to humans—all of which are derived from time, space, matter, and similar physical things. Instead, they speak in spiritual ideas, all of which are derived from "states" and the various changes happening within and around the angels. Nevertheless, when these angelic ideas (which are spiritual) flow into a person, they are instantly and naturally transformed into the natural ideas specific to humans, which correspond perfectly to those spiritual ideas. Neither angels nor humans are aware that this transformation takes place; yet this is the nature of all <term>influx<note>The spiritual process by which life, thought, and feeling flow from the spiritual world into the natural world or the human mind.</note></term> from heaven into man. Certain angels were once permitted to enter more closely into my thoughts, even into the natural...

**[2.]** I have been allowed to know through experience just how ignorant the angels are regarding time. Time varies even in a state of hope or expectation. They become unlimited and expansive only to the degree that they do not include these elements, since the mind is then raised above bodily and worldly concerns. ### XIX.

### REPRESENTATIVES AND APPEARANCES IN HEAVEN. <note>In this context, "representatives" are not people, but spiritual symbols or outward objects that perfectly mirror the inner thoughts and feelings of angels.</note>

**170.** A person who thinks only from <term>natural light<note>Human reasoning based solely on what we can see, touch, and measure in the physical world.</note></term> is unable to understand that there is anything in heaven similar to what is on earth. This is because many have convinced themselves that angels are nothing but "minds," and that these minds are like ghostly breaths or ethereal vapors. They assume angels have no senses like humans do—specifically no eyes—and if they have no eyes, they would have no objects to look at. Yet, in reality, an angel has every sense that a human has, and their senses are far more sharp and refined. The light by which angels see is much brighter than the light of our world. That angels are truly human beings in a perfect form and enjoy every sense was explained earlier (in sections 73–77); and that the light in heaven is far more brilliant than the light on earth was also discussed (in sections 126–132).

**171.** It is difficult to describe the nature of the objects that angels see in heaven in just a few words. For the most part, they look like things found on earth, but they are far more perfect in their shape and much more numerous. The fact that such things exist in the heavens is clear from the visions of the prophets. For example, *Ezekiel* described a new temple and a new earth (chapters 40 to 48); *Daniel* recorded visions (chapters 7 to 12); and *John* described the wonders of the <term>Apocalypse<note>The Book of Revelation.</note></term> from the first chapter to the last. Other examples appear throughout both the historical and prophetic parts of <term>the Word<note>The Bible.</note></term>. 

These prophets saw these things when heaven was "opened" to them. Heaven is said to be opened when a person’s <term>interior sight<note>The ability of the human spirit to see into the spiritual world, which is usually closed while we are focused on our physical bodies.</note></term>—the sight of their spirit—is activated. The things in the heavens cannot be seen with the physical eyes of the body; they are seen by the eyes of the spirit. Whenever it pleases the Lord, these spiritual eyes are opened. When this happens, the person is temporarily withdrawn from the natural light of the physical senses and raised into spiritual light. It is in this spiritual light that I have seen the things that exist in heaven.

<summary>This page explains that heaven is a tangible, visual realm filled with objects that resemble those on earth but in a more perfect form. It argues that angels possess heightened senses and that these heavenly "representatives" can be seen by humans when their spiritual sight is opened, as occurred with the biblical prophets.</summary>

<keywords>representatives, appearances, spiritual light, natural light, angelic senses, interior sight, Ezekiel, Daniel, Book of Revelation, spiritual vision</keywords>

**172.** But even though most things seen in heaven look like things on earth, they are fundamentally different in their essence. This is because everything in heaven originates from the <term>Sun of heaven</term>, while everything on earth originates from the sun of our physical world. The things that come from the Sun of heaven are called **spiritual**, whereas those that come from the sun of our world are called **natural**.

**173.** Furthermore, things in heaven do not come into being in the same way they do on earth. All things in heaven are brought forth by the Lord through <term>correspondence<note>A core concept in this work: the idea that every outward physical object reflects an inner spiritual reality or state of mind.</note></term> with the "interiors" of the angels. Every angel has both "interiors"—their inner thoughts and feelings—and "exteriors"—their outward appearance and environment. All things within their inner life relate to love and faith, which reside in the **will** and the **understanding** (the "containers" for these qualities). Their outward environment perfectly matches these inner states. We have already seen (in sections 87–115) how the outer world reflects the inner world. This is best shown by the way angels experience heat and light: they feel heat according to how much love they have, and they see light according to how much wisdom they possess (sections 128–134). The same rule applies to every other thing their senses perceive.

**174.** Whenever I have been allowed to be in the company of angels, the objects around me appeared exactly like those in the physical world. They were so clear that I would not have known I wasn't on earth, or perhaps in the palace of a king. I even spoke with the angels just as one person speaks to another.

**175.** Because everything that matches an angel's inner state also symbolizes it, these things are called *representatives*. And because these things change depending on the state of the angel's mind, they are called *appearances*. Even so, the things that angels see and feel are just as real to them as the things on earth are to us—in fact, they are much clearer, more distinct, and more vivid. These are known as **real appearances** because they actually exist. There are also appearances that are not real, which are things that are visible but do not truly match an angel's inner state.¹ These will be discussed later.

**176.** To illustrate the nature of the things that appear to angels through the process of <term>correspondence<note>The relationship where a physical appearance perfectly mirrors a spiritual reality.</note></term>, I will describe one example. Those who have cultivated their <term>intelligence</term> see beautiful gardens and parks filled with every kind of tree and flower. These trees are arranged in a stunningly beautiful order, weaving together to form arbors with arched entryways and winding paths—all more magnificent than words can describe. In these places, the intelligent walk about, gathering flowers and weaving garlands to decorate little children. These gardens even contain species of trees and flowers that have never been seen and could not even exist on earth. When such people think about heaven, they often say that it contains things "which ear hath not heard and eye hath not seen."

### XX.

### THE GARMENTS WITH WHICH ANGELS APPEAR CLOTHED.

**177.** Since angels are human beings and live together in society just as people do on earth, they have garments, dwellings, and other similar things. The difference, however, is that because angels exist in a more perfect state, everything they possess is also in a state of greater perfection. Just as angelic wisdom surpasses human wisdom to such a degree that it is called <term>ineffable<note>Beyond the power of words to express; indescribable.</note></term>, so it is with everything perceived and seen by them, because everything in their environment <term>corresponds<note>The spiritual law where outward appearances perfectly mirror inward realities.</note></term> to their wisdom (see above, n. 173).

**178.** The garments with which angels are clothed, like everything else in their world, are based on correspondence; they have a real, tangible existence because they correspond to the angel's inner state (see above, n. 175). Their clothing corresponds to their <term>intelligence</term>. For this reason, everyone in the heavens appears dressed in a way that matches their level of understanding; as one person is more intelligent than another, their clothing is more magnificent. Some of the most intelligent have garments that blaze as if with flame, while others have garments that glisten as if with light. Those who are less intelligent wear garments that are glistening white or plain white without that radiant glow, and those with even less intelligence wear garments of various colors. However, the angels of the <term>inmost heaven<note>The highest or "third" heaven, characterized by the most direct love for the Divine.</note></term> are not clothed. <gloss>They appear naked to signify their state of pure innocence.</gloss>

**179.** Because the garments of angels correspond to their intelligence, they also correspond to truth, since all true intelligence comes from <term>Divine truth</term>. Therefore, it is the same whether you say angels are clothed according to their intelligence or according to Divine truth. The garments of some blaze as if with flame, and those of others glisten as if with light, because flame corresponds to <term>good<note>The quality of the will or the heart's intentions.</note></term>, and light corresponds to <term>truth<note>The clarity of the intellect or understanding.</note></term>...

**181.** The garments of angels do not merely *look* like clothing; they are real garments. We know this because angels can both see and feel them. They possess many different outfits, which they put on and take off as needed. They even store the garments they are not currently using and put them back on when they are required. I have seen them clothed in a great variety of garments many times. When I asked where they obtained them, they replied that they come from the Lord, and that they receive—

### XXI.

### THE PLACES OF ABODE AND DWELLINGS OF ANGELS.

**183.** Because there are societies in heaven and the angels live as men, they also have places of abode, and these differ according to each one’s state of life. They are magnificent for those in a higher state of dignity, and less magnificent for those in a lower condition. I have frequently talked with angels about these places of abode in heaven, remarking that scarcely anyone at the present day will believe that they have homes and dwellings. Some disbelieve because they cannot see them; some because they do not know that angels are truly human; and others because they believe that the "angelic heaven" is merely the physical sky seen with their eyes. Because the sky appears empty and they suppose angels are mere ethereal forms, they conclude that they live in the ether. Furthermore, they do not comprehend how there can be things in the spiritual world similar to those in the natural world, because they know nothing about the nature of the spiritual. [**2.**] The angels replied that they are aware that such ignorance prevails in the world today, and they expressed astonishment that this is found chiefly within the church, and more among the "intelligent" than among those who are considered simple. They said also that it might be known from <term>the Word<note>The author's term for the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note></term> that angels are men, since those who have been seen by prophets and others were clearly human in form.

...have been seen as human beings; and the Lord, who took His entire **Human** form with Him <note>original: "Humanum." This refers to Swedenborg’s doctrine that God became Divine-Human, making the human form the blueprint for all heaven.</note>, appeared in the same way. It can also be known that because angels are human, they have dwellings and places to live; they do not simply fly through the air, as some mistakenly believe in their ignorance—an idea the angels actually call **insanity**. Even though they are called "spirits," they are not merely winds or wisps of air. 

This reality could be understood if people would only think independently of the notions they have been taught about angels and spirits. Most people have an intuitive, general idea that angels have a human form and live in homes called the "mansions of heaven," which are far more magnificent than any dwellings on earth. This general idea flows into the mind from heaven itself. However, it quickly vanishes as soon as it is brought under direct academic scrutiny or "learned" inquiry. This happens especially to the scholars and the learned, who, through their own intellectual pride, have closed off heaven and the entrance of heavenly light to themselves. 

[3.] The same is true regarding the belief in life after death. When someone speaks of it naturally—without simultaneously thinking about the "soul" through the lens of worldly learning or the religious doctrine of its reunion with the physical body—they believe that after death they will live as a human being. They expect to live among angels if they have lived well, seeing magnificent things and feeling joy. But as soon as they turn their thoughts to the doctrine of the body's resurrection, or to their own theories about the nature of the soul, they begin to question if such a thing could be true, and their former intuitive belief is destroyed.

**184.** But it is better to present the evidence of experience. Whenever I have talked with angels face to face, I have been with them in their own dwellings. These abodes are precisely like the homes on earth that we call houses, but they are more beautiful. Inside them, there are many chambers, parlors, and bedrooms; there are also courtyards, gardens, flower-beds, and lawns surrounding them. Where angels live together in societies, their houses are arranged near one another in the form of a city, with avenues, streets, and public squares, exactly like the cities we see on earth. I have been permitted to pass through them, looking about on every side and sometimes entering the houses themselves. This occurred when my <term>inner sight<note>Also called "spiritual sight"; the capacity of the soul to see the spiritual world as clearly as the eyes see the physical world.</note></term> was opened and I was fully awake.¹

**185.** I have seen palaces in heaven of such magnificence as cannot be described. Above they glittered as if made of pure gold, and below as if made of precious stones, some more splendid than others. It was the same within. Both words and knowledge are inadequate to describe the decorations that adorned the rooms. On the side looking to the south there were parks, where, too, every thing shone, in some places the leaves glistening as if made of silver, and fruit as if made of gold; while the flowers in their beds formed rainbows with their colors. Beyond the borders, where the view terminated, were seen other palaces. <insert>A pencil bracket in the right margin marks the following sentence to the end of the paragraph.</insert> Such is the architecture of heaven that you would say that art there is in its art <note>This phrase suggests that heavenly art is the very essence or source of all earthly creativity; it is "art itself."</note>; and no wonder, because the art is itself from heaven. The angels said that such things and innumerable others still more perfect are set forth before their eyes by the Lord; and yet these things are more pleasing to their minds than to their eyes, because in every one of them they see a <term>correspondence</term> <note>Correspondence is the core idea that every physical object in the spiritual world is a direct reflection of an inner, spiritual reality.</note>, and through the correspondences what is Divine.

**186.** As to these correspondences I have also been told that not only the palaces and houses, but all things and each thing, both inside and outside of them, correspond to the interior things which they have from the Lord. The house itself in general corresponds to their "good" <note>In this context, "good" refers to the quality of an angel's love and will.</note>, the particular things inside of a house to the various things of which their good consists,¹ and the things outside to "truths" derived from good, and also to their perceptions and knowledges (see note, page 103). As these things correspond to the goods and truths they have from the Lord, they also correspond to their love, and to their wisdom and intelligence from love—since love belongs to good, wisdom to both good and truth together, and intelligence to truth derived from good. These are what the angels perceive when they behold what is around them, and thus their minds are more delighted and moved by them than their eyes.

**187.** All this makes clear why the Lord called Himself the temple at Jerusalem (*John* ii. 19, 21),¹ namely, because the temple represented His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>Latin: *Divinum Humanum*. **188.** The angels of whom the Lord's <term>celestial kingdom</term> <note>The highest of the three heavens, characterized by a direct, heart-centered love for the Lord.</note> consists dwell for the most part in elevated places that appear as mountains of soil; the angels of whom the Lord's <term>spiritual kingdom</term> <note>The middle heaven, characterized by an intellectual love for neighbor and truth.</note> consists dwell in less elevated places that appear like hills; while the angels in the lowest parts of heaven dwell in places that appear like ledges of stone. All these things spring from <term>correspondence</term> <note>The law by which the internal (spiritual) state of an angel is mirrored perfectly by their external (physical) environment.</note>, for interior things correspond to higher things, and exterior things to lower things;³ and this is why in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures (the Bible).</note> "mountains" signify celestial love, "hills" spiritual love, and "rocks" faith.⁴

## XXIII.

### THE FORM OF HEAVEN WHICH DETERMINES AFFILIATIONS AND COMMUNICATIONS THERE.

**200.** What the form of heaven is can be seen in some measure from what has been shown in the preceding chapters; as that heaven is like itself both in its greatest and in its least divisions (n. 72); that consequently each society is a heaven in a smaller form, and each angel in the smallest form (n. 51–58); <note>This suggests a "fractal" nature to heaven, where the whole structure is mirrored in every small part.</note> that as the entire heaven reflects a single man, <note>This refers to the concept of the "Grand Man" (Maximus Homo), the idea that the collective of all heaven functions as a single, perfectly organized human body.</note> so each society of heaven reflects a man in a smaller form, and each angel in the smallest form (n. 59–77); that the wisest are at the centre, and the less wise are round about even to the borders, and the same is true of each society (n. 43); and that those who are in the good of love dwell from the east to the west in heaven, and those who are in truth from good from the south to the north; and the same is true of each society (n. 148, 149). All this is in accord with the form of heaven; consequently it may be concluded from this what this form is in general. <note>These references (e.g., n. 148) point to other sections in the author’s theological works, particularly *Secrets of Heaven* (Arcana Coelestia), which detail the laws of spiritual order.</note>

**201.** It is important to know what the form of heaven is, because not only is all affiliation <note>Affiliation refers to how angels are grouped into societies based on their shared values and character.</note> there in accord with it, but also all mutual communication, and in consequence of this all spread of thoughts and affections, and thus all the intelligence and wisdom of angels. From this it follows that each one there is wise just to the extent that he is in the form of heaven, and is thus a form of heaven. It makes no difference whether you say *in the form of heaven*, or *in the order of heaven*, since the form of any thing is from its order and in accordance with its order.<sup>1</sup>

**202.** Let us consider first what is meant by being in the form of heaven. Man was created both in the image of heaven and in the image of the world; his internal <note>The "internal" refers to the soul or the spiritual mind, while the "external" refers to the physical body and natural mind.</note> in the image of heaven, and his external in the image of the world (see above, n. 57); and *in the image* means the same thing as in accordance with the form. But as man by the evils of his will and consequent falsities of thought has destroyed in himself the image of heaven, that is, the form of heaven, and in place of it has brought in the image and form of hell, his internal is closed up from his very birth; and this is why man is born into pure ignorance, while animals of every kind are not. <note>The author argues that because animals act by instinct—an inherent natural order—they are born with necessary knowledge, whereas humans must relearn spiritual order because our original nature has been corrupted.</note> And that man may have the image of heaven or form of heaven restored to him he must be taught the things that pertain to order; since form, as has been said, is in accord with order. The Word <note>The Bible or Divine Revelation.</note> contains all the laws of Divine order, for its precepts are the laws of Divine order; therefore to the extent that man learns these and lives in accordance with them his internal is opened and the order or image of heaven is there formed anew. This makes clear what is meant by being in the form of heaven, namely, that it is to live in accordance with those things that are in the Word.<sup>2</sup>

Even if a person does not perceive this extension (for the reasons given in section 196), it remains true. ->### THE FORM OF HEAVEN.<-

**205.** Everyone in heaven is connected through a kind of spiritual kinship. These relationships are based on "good" and "truth" <note>In this context, "good" refers to the essence of love and kindness, while "truth" refers to the wisdom or principles that give that love direction.</note> in their proper order. This organizational structure applies to the entirety of heaven, to every individual community, and even to every household. Because of this, angels who share similar levels of goodness and wisdom recognize one another instantly—much like relatives or old friends on earth—even if they have never met before. The goodness and truth within each angel, which make up their intelligence, are connected in the same way. These qualities "recognize" each other and join together.¹ Consequently, those whose inner lives are organized according to this heavenly pattern can see how ideas follow one another in a logical series and how they connect to a vast web of knowledge. However, those whose inner lives are not organized this way cannot see these connections.

**206.** Each level of heaven follows this pattern. It is through this structure that angels are able to share their thoughts and feelings, which is how they grow in wisdom. However, the way one heaven communicates with another is different from how communication happens within a single level. For example, the communication between the third (highest) heaven and the second (middle) heaven—or between the middle and the first (lowest)—is unique. This interaction between the levels should be called **influx** <term>Influx: A term describing how life or influence flows from a higher spiritual level into a lower one, rather than a two-way conversation.</term> rather than simple communication. We will explore this further now. As noted in a previous chapter (sections 29–40), there are three distinct heavens.

**207.** The fact that there is "influx" rather than "communication" between the different heavens can be seen by how they are positioned. The third heaven is at the top, the second is in the middle, and the first is at the bottom. A similar arrangement exists within every community. For instance, some angels live in high places that look like mountains (see section 188); those from the highest level of that community live on the peaks, while the second level lives below them, and the lowest level lives at the base. This pattern is found everywhere, whether in high places or in the surrounding areas.³

The thoughts of these communities remain stable and are not disturbed by this flow of influence.

# HEAVEN AND HELL.

...those who have not been elevated to that state. A community in a higher heaven has no communication with a community in a lower heaven except through **correspondences** <term>Correspondences: The spiritual connection where a higher, internal reality is reflected in a lower, external form.</term> (see section 100 above). This communication through correspondences is what we call **influx** <term>Influx: The process by which life, wisdom, and influence flow from the Divine through the higher levels of existence into the lower ones.</term>.

**208.** One heaven is joined with another—or a community of one heaven with a community of another—by the Lord alone. This connection happens through a "flowing in" (influx) that is both direct and indirect. It flows directly from the Lord Himself, and indirectly through the higher heavens, moving in descending order into the lower ones.¹ Because this connection is managed entirely by the Lord, there is a strict spiritual safeguard: an angel from a higher heaven is prevented from looking down into a lower community to speak with the inhabitants there. If an angel were to do this, they would immediately lose their intelligence and wisdom.

There is a specific reason for this. Just as there are three levels of heaven, every angel has three levels—or "degrees"—of life. 
*   Angels in the highest (third) heaven have their deepest level open, while their middle and lower levels are closed. 
*   Angels in the middle heaven have their second level open, while the highest and lowest are closed. 
*   Angels in the lowest heaven have only their first level open. 

Consequently, if an angel from the third heaven looks down and tries to talk to someone in the second heaven, their highest level (the source of their wisdom) is instantly shut. Since they possess no wisdom in the lower two levels, they become spiritually empty. This is the inner meaning behind the Lord’s words in the Gospel of *Matthew*:

> “Let the one on the housetop not go down to take what is in his house; and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment” (24:17, 18).

And in the Gospel of *Luke*:

> “In that day, let the one on the housetop whose goods are in the house not go down to take them away; and let the one in the field likewise not turn back. Remember Lot’s wife” (17:31, 32). <note>In the Bible, Lot’s wife was turned into a pillar of salt for looking back at the city she was fleeing. Here, it symbolizes the danger of a higher spiritual state "looking back" or descending into a lower, more worldly state.</note>

### GOVERNMENTS IN HEAVEN.

Order must be maintained. However, the governments in the heavens vary; they are of one kind in the communities that constitute the Lord's **celestial kingdom** <term>Celestial kingdom: The highest of the three heavens, characterized by a direct, heart-centered love for the Lord rather than intellectual reasoning.</term>, and of another kind in the communities that constitute His **spiritual kingdom** <term>Spiritual kingdom: The second heaven, characterized by love for the neighbor (charity) and an intellectual focus on spiritual truths.</term>; they differ also in accordance with the functions of the several communities. Nevertheless, no government other than the government of **mutual love** <note>A state where everyone desires the well-being of others more than their own; the opposite of selfish rule.</note> is possible in the heavens, and the government of mutual love is heavenly government.

**214.** Government in the Lord's celestial kingdom is called **righteousness** because all in that kingdom live in the "good of love" to the Lord from the Lord, and whatever flows from that good is called righteous. Government there belongs to the Lord alone; everyone there is led and taught by Him in the practical affairs of life. The truths that are called "truths of judgment" are written on their hearts; every one knows them, perceives them, and sees them;¹ and in consequence, matters of legal judgment never come into question there, but only matters of righteousness, which belong to the way one lives. About these matters, the less wise consult the more wise, and these consult the Lord and receive answers. Their heaven—that is, their deepest joy—is to live rightly from the Lord.

**215.** In the Lord's spiritual kingdom the government is called **judgment**; because those in that kingdom live in "spiritual good," which is the good of **charity** <note>Active kindness and service toward others.</note> towards the neighbor, and that good in its essence is truth;² and truth pertains to judgment, just as good pertains to righteousness.³ These, too, are led

**216.** As government from **good** <note>In this context, 'good' refers to the motivations of the heart and the celestial kingdom.</note>, which is the kind of government which exists in the Lord’s **celestial kingdom**, is called **righteousness**; and government from **truth** <note>'Truth' here refers to the intellectual principles and laws that guide the spiritual kingdom.</note>, which is the kind of government that exists in the Lord’s **spiritual kingdom**, is called **judgment**, so the terms “righteousness and judgment” are used in **the Word** <note>The Word: A term used to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> when heaven and the church are treated of, “righteousness” signifying celestial good, and “judgment” spiritual good—which good, as has been said above, is in its essence truth—as in the following passages:

> “Of peace there shall be no end upon the throne of **David** and upon his kingdom, to establish it and to uphold it in **judgment** and in **righteousness** from henceforth and even to eternity” (*Isaiah* ix. 7).

By “David” here the Lord is meant;¹ and by “His kingdom” heaven, as is evident from the following passage:

> “I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and He shall reign as King, and shall deal intelligently and shall execute **judgment** and **righteousness** in the land” (*Jeremiah* xxiii. 5).

“Zion” also means heaven and the church.²

> “I, Jehovah, doing . . **judgment** and **righteousness** on the earth, for in these things I delight” (*Jeremiah* ix. 24).
> “I will betroth thee unto Me forever, and I will betroth thee unto Me in **righteousness** and **judgment**” (*Hosea* ii. 19).
> “O Jehovah, in the heavens . . . Thy **righteousness** is like the mountains of God, and Thy **judgments** <note>original: "Judicia magna" — 'Great judgments' mean the laws of Divine order, and thus Divine truths (n. 7206).</note> are like the great deep” (*Psalm* xxxvi. 5, 6).

So in other places.

Each one, moreover, receives good in the measure in which he loves the common good; for so far as he loves the common good he loves all and every one; and as that love is love of the Lord he is to that extent loved by the Lord, and good comes to him.

**218.** From all this it can be seen what the governors there are, namely, that they are such as are pre-eminent in love and wisdom, and therefore desire the good of all, and from wisdom know how to provide for the realization of that good. Such governors do not domineer or dictate, but minister and serve (to serve meaning to do good to others from a love of the good, and to minister meaning to see to it that the good is done); nor do they make themselves greater than others, but less, for they put the good of society and of the neighbor in the first place, and put their own good last; and whatever is put in the first place is held to be greater and what is put last to be less. Nevertheless, the rulers have honor and glory; they dwell in the midst of the society, in higher position than the rest, and also in magnificent palaces; and this glory and honor they accept not for the sake of themselves but for the sake of obedience.

## XXV.

### DIVINE WORSHIP IN HEAVEN.

**221.** Divine worship in the heavens is not unlike Divine worship on the earth in its outward forms, but it differs in its inner essence. In the heavens, just as on the earth, there are doctrines, preachings, and church buildings. In their essential principles, the doctrines there are the same everywhere; however, in the <term>higher heavens<note>Swedenborg describes heaven as being organized into three levels: the Celestial (highest), Spiritual (middle), and Natural (lowest), each reflecting a different depth of wisdom.</note></term> they contain a more profound, interior wisdom than in the lower ones. The sermons are given in harmony with these doctrines. And just as angels have houses and palaces, they also have church buildings in which preaching takes place. These things exist in heaven because the angels are being perfected continually in wisdom and love. Like human beings, they possess both understanding and <term>will<note>In this context, 'will' refers to the seat of a person's intentions and affections—what they love—while 'understanding' refers to their thoughts and intellect.</note></term>; both are capable of being continually refined—the understanding through the truths of intelligence, and the will through the good qualities of love.¹

**222.** However, essential Divine worship in the heavens does not consist merely in attending church and listening to a sermon, but in a life of love, <term>charity<note>Here, 'charity' refers to 'caritas' or neighborly love—acting with kindness and justice in one's daily work—rather than just giving to the poor.</note></term>, and faith, lived in accordance with doctrine. Preaching in churches serves only as a means of instruction for how to live. I have spoken with angels on this topic and told them that in our world, many believe Divine worship consists solely in attending church, listening to sermons, taking the <term>sacrament of the Supper<note>The Holy Communion or Eucharist.</note></term> three or four times a year, and performing other prescribed rituals, such as setting aside specific times for prayer and behaving devoutly during them. The angels replied that these are outward acts that ought to be done, but they are of no value unless they come from an internal source—namely, a life lived according to the practical teachings of one’s faith.

---

As all things in existence relate to truth and goodness, every aspect of a person’s life relates to their understanding and their will <note>original: "n. 803, 10122"</note>.
Angels continue to grow in perfection for all eternity <note>original: "n. 4803, 6648"</note>.

**223.** In order that I might learn about their gatherings in places of worship, I have been permitted at times to attend and to hear the preaching. The preacher stands in a pulpit at the east. Those who are in the light of wisdom more than others sit in front of him; those who are in less light sit to the right and left of these. There is a circular arrangement of the seats, so that all are in the preacher's view, no one so sitting at either side as to be out of his view. At the entrance, which is at the east of the building and on the left of the pulpit, those stand who are being initiated. No one is permitted to stand behind the pulpit; when there is anyone there the preacher is confused. It is the same if anyone in the congregation dissents; and for this reason the dissenter must needs turn away his face. The wisdom of the preachings is such as to be above all comparison with the preachings of this world, for those in the heavens are in interior light. The church edifices in the <term>spiritual kingdom<note>The second of the three heavens, characterized by an intellectual love for truth and neighborly charity.</note></term> are apparently built of stone, and those in the <term>celestial kingdom<note>The highest heaven, characterized by a direct, heart-centered love for the Lord.</note></term> of wood; because stone <term>corresponds<note>In this context, 'correspondence' refers to the symbolic link between a physical material and a spiritual state.</note></term> to truth, and those who are in the spiritual kingdom are in truth, while wood corresponds to good, and those in the celestial kingdom are in good.<gloss>1. Stone signifies truth and wood signifies good. For this reason the most ancient people, who were in celestial good, had sacred buildings of wood.</gloss> In that kingdom the sacred edifices are not called churches but houses of God. There they are without magnificence; but in the spiritual kingdom they are more or less magnificent.

**224.** I have also talked with one of the preachers about the holy state in which those who listen to the preaching in the churches find themselves. He said that every one is pious, devout, and holy in harmony with his <term>interiors<note>A person's 'interiors' are their deepest thoughts and feelings, as opposed to their outward behavior or 'exteriors.'</note></term>, which pertain to love and faith, for holiness itself is in love and faith, because the <term>Divine of the Lord<note>The 'Divine of the Lord' refers to the presence of God's essence within a person or angel.</note></term> is in them. He also declared that outward holiness apart from love and faith he knew nothing about; and if he thought about it it would be as something counterfeiting holiness in outward appearance, either conventional or hypocritical; and that such holiness is kindled and sustained by <term>spurious fire<note>A metaphor for motivations that appear passionate or 'warm' but are actually driven by selfish desires rather than divine love.</note></term> from the love of self and the world.

## XXVI.

### THE POWER OF THE ANGELS OF HEAVEN.

**228.** That the angels possess power is something that cannot be understood by those who know nothing about the `<term>spiritual world<note>A realm of existence beyond the physical, inhabited by spirits and angels, which serves as the internal reality behind the natural world.</note>` and its `<term>influx<note>From the Latin 'influere,' meaning to flow in. This refers to the continuous movement of life, thought, and energy from the Divine through the spiritual realm into the natural world.</note>` into the natural world. Such people think that angels can have no power because they are spiritual beings—so pure and light that no human eye can see them. But those who look more deeply into the causes of things take a different view. They know that all the power a human has comes from their `<term>understanding and will<note>In this philosophy, these are the two fundamental parts of the human mind: the 'will' is the seat of love and intention, while the 'understanding' is the seat of thought and reason.</note>`; without these, a person is powerless to move even a tiny part of their body. It is the "spiritual man" within that moves the physical body and its limbs as it pleases; whatever the mind thinks, the mouth and tongue speak, and whatever the mind wills, the body performs. As a person's will and understanding are guided by the Lord through angels and spirits, so too are all the functions of the body. If you can believe it, without this spiritual influence from heaven, a person could not even take a single step. I have learned this through much personal experience; angels have been permitted to move my steps, my actions, and my speech as they pleased by flowing into my will and thought. Through this, I learned that I could do nothing of myself. I was later told by the angels that every person is ruled in this way. One can know this from church doctrine and from the Word <note>A common term for the Bible or Holy Scripture.</note>, for people pray that God may send His angels to lead them, direct their steps, teach them, and inspire what they should think and say. However, people often say and believe otherwise when they are thinking by themselves, apart from religious teachings. All this has been said to make known the power that angels have within a human being.

**229.** Furthermore, the power of angels in the spiritual world is so great that if I were to describe everything I have witnessed, it would exceed belief. If there is any obstacle there that needs to be removed because it is contrary to `<term>Divine order<note>The fundamental laws of reality and morality established by God, which govern the structure of both heaven and earth.</note>`, the angels cast it down or overthrow it merely by an effort of the will and a look. Thus, I have seen mountains that were...
