**244.** In heaven, as has been said above, all share one common language; however, it varies according to wisdom. The speech of the wise is more interior and filled with a greater variety of **affections** <note>In this context, "affections" refers to the underlying emotional states or desires that drive a person's thoughts and speech.</note> and ideas. The speech of those who are less wise is more external and less nuanced, while the speech of the simple is more external still, consisting of words from which the meaning must be gathered in the same way that humans talk to one another. 

There are also other forms of communication:
*   Speech by the **face**, which ends in a resonant sound shaped by ideas.
*   Speech where **heavenly representatives** <note>These "representatives" are spiritual symbols or visual manifestations that appear to the sight of angels to convey deep meanings.</note> are mingled with ideas, moving from thought into visible forms.
*   Speech through **gestures** that correspond to affections and represent the same things expressed by their words.
*   Speech using the **generals** <note>Original: "generalia." These are broad, universal categories or "summaries" of feelings and thoughts rather than specific details.</note> of affections and thoughts.
*   Speech that sounds like **thunder**; among many other kinds.

**245.** The speech of evil and infernal spirits is likewise natural to them because it flows from their affections; however, it springs from evil affections and the resulting "filthy" ideas, which angels find utterly repulsive. Consequently, the ways of speaking in **hell** <note>original: "infernum"</note> are the exact opposite of those in heaven. Because of this, evil spirits cannot stand to hear angelic speech, and angels cannot endure the speech of hell. To an angel, infernal speech feels like a foul odor hitting the nostrils. The speech of **hypocrites**—those who can pretend to be "angels of light"—resembles angelic speech in its words, but it is the total opposite in its underlying affection and thought. When the true nature of a hypocrite’s speech is perceived by wise angels, it sounds like the **gnashing of teeth** <note>A biblical image often used by Swedenborg to describe the collision of false ideas or the harsh reality of hidden malice.</note> and strikes them with horror.

**248.** The speech of an angel or spirit with man is heard by him as audibly as the speech of a man with him, yet by himself only, and not by others who stand near; and for the reason that the speech of an angel or spirit flows first into a man's thought, and by an inner way into his organ of hearing, which is therefore affected from within; while the speech of man with man flows first into the air and by an outward way into his organ of hearing, thus affecting it from without. This explains why man is not permitted to speak with them in return; if he did they would be aware of his presence. Again, those who meditate much on religious subjects, and are so intent upon them as to see them as it were inwardly within themselves, begin to hear spirits speaking with them; for religious persuasions, whatever they are, when man dwells upon them by himself and does not adapt them to the various things of use in the world, penetrate to the <term>interiors</term><note>The deeper levels of the human soul or mind that are capable of experiencing the spiritual world.</note> and rest there, and occupy the whole spirit of the man, and even enter into the spiritual world and act upon the spirits there. But such persons are <term>visionaries and enthusiasts</term><note>In Swedenborg’s time, an "enthusiast" was someone who believed they were receiving direct, private revelations from God, often viewed with skepticism as being fueled by personal delusion rather than divine truth.</note>; and whatever spirit they hear they believe to be the Holy Spirit, when, in fact, such spirits are enthusiastic spirits. Such spirits, however, have been gradually removed, because they began to lure others into evil and to gain control over them. Enthusiastic spirits are distinguished from other spirits by their believing themselves to be the Holy Spirit, and believing what they say to be Divine. As man honors such spirits with Divine worship they do not try to harm him. I have sometimes talked with them, and the wicked things they infused into their worshippers were then disclosed. They dwell together towards the left, in a desert place.

**250.** To speak with the angels of heaven is granted only to those who are in truths from good, especially to those who are in the acknowledgment of the Lord and of the Divine in His Human, because this is the truth in which the heavens are. For, as it has been shown above, the Lord is the God of heaven (n. 2–6); it is the Divine of the Lord that makes heaven (n. 7–12); the Divine of the Lord in heaven is love to Him and charity towards the neighbor from Him (n. 13–19); the whole heaven in one complex reflects a single man; also every society of heaven; and every angel is in complete human form, and this from the <term>Divine Human</term><note>The concept that God became Human in the person of Jesus Christ to reach humanity, and that His Human nature was made entirely Divine.</note> of the Lord (n. 59–86). All of which makes evident that only those whose interiors are opened by Divine truths, even to the Lord, are able to speak with the angels of heaven, since it is into these truths with man that the Lord flows, and when the Lord flows in heaven also flows in. Divine truths open the interiors of man because man was so created as to be in respect to his <term>internal man</term> an image of heaven, and in respect to his <term>external</term> an image of the world <note>Swedenborg views the human being as a bridge between two worlds: the soul (internal) reflecting the spiritual heavens, and the body/senses (external) reflecting the physical universe.</note>.

**251.** The <term>influx</term><note>The "flowing in" of spiritual energy or thought from the divine or spiritual realm into the human mind.</note> of the Lord Himself into man is directed toward his forehead, and from there into the whole face. This is because the forehead of man <term>corresponds</term><note>In Swedenborg’s system, "correspondence" is the functional relationship between a physical thing and a spiritual reality; for example, a physical part of the body performs a task that mirrors a spiritual process.</note> to love, and the face corresponds to all of his inner thoughts and feelings.¹ The influx of <term>spiritual angels</term><note>Angels who primarily belong to the second or middle heaven, characterized by their intelligence and love for truth.</note> into man is into his head everywhere, from the forehead and temples to the entire region containing the <term>cerebrum</term><note>The larger, upper part of the brain associated with conscious thought and intelligence.</note>, because that region of the head corresponds to intelligence. However, the influx of <term>celestial angels</term><note>Angels of the highest heaven, characterized by their deep wisdom and love for the Lord.</note> is into that part of the head containing the <term>cerebellum</term><note>The lower, back part of the brain associated with deeper, often subconscious, wisdom and emotion.</note>, which is called the occiput, stretching from the ears all the way to the neck, for that region corresponds to wisdom. All the speech of angels with man enters by these paths into his thought; and by this means I have perceived what kind of angels they were that spoke with me.

**252.** Those who talk with the angels of heaven also see the things that exist in heaven, because they are then seeing in the light of heaven, for their internal minds are in that light. Furthermore, the angels are able to see the things that are on the earth through those people,² because in those individuals, heaven is joined to the world and the world is joined to heaven. For (as has been said above, section 246), when the angels turn themselves toward a man, they join themselves to him so closely that they are scarcely aware that what belongs to the man is not actually theirs—this applies not only to his speech but also to his sight and hearing. Man, on the other hand, believes that the thoughts flowing in through the angels are entirely his own. Such was the connection that existed between the angels of heaven and the most ancient people on this earth, and for this reason their era was called the **Golden Age**. Because this race acknowledged the Divine in a human form—that is, the Lord—they talked with the angels of heaven as if with their friends, and angels of heaven talked with them in return.

[The angels talked with] them as with their friends; and in them heaven and the world became a single realm. In consequence, he began to feel the delights of the love of self and the world as separate from the delights of heaven, and finally reached a point where he was ignorant of any other delight. Then his <term>interiors</term><note>The inner levels of the human mind and soul that are capable of perceiving spiritual light.</note> that had been open into heaven were closed up, while his <term>exteriors</term><note>The outward parts of a person’s consciousness focused on the physical world and the senses.</note> were open to the world. When this takes place, man is in light regarding all things of the world, but in thick darkness regarding all things of heaven.

**253.** Since those times, it is only rarely that anyone has talked with the angels of heaven; instead, some have talked with spirits who are not in heaven. This is because man's interior and exterior faculties are structured such that they are turned either toward the Lord as their common center (see section 124), or toward the self—which is to say, backwards from the Lord. Those faculties turned toward the Lord are also turned toward heaven. But those turned toward the self are turned also toward the world. To elevate these worldly faculties is a difficult matter; nevertheless, the Lord elevates them as much as is possible by turning the person's love around, which is accomplished by means of truths from the <term>Word</term><note>Referring here to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>.

**254.** I have been told how the Lord spoke with the prophets to whom the Word was given. He did not speak with them as He did with the ancients, by an <term>influx</term><note>The "flowing in" of spiritual life or thought from the Divine into the human mind.</note> into their inner minds, but through spirits who were sent to them. The Lord filled these spirits with His look, and thus inspired them with the words which they dictated to the prophets. Therefore, this was not a conceptual "flowing in" (influx) but a direct dictation. Because these words came forth directly from the Lord, each one of them was filled with the Divine and contains within it an <term>internal sense</term><note>The hidden, spiritual meaning within the literal stories of the Bible that describes heavenly realities.</note>. This sense is such that the angels of heaven understand the words in a heavenly and spiritual way, while humans understand them in a natural way. In this way, the Lord has joined heaven and the world together by means of the Word. 

How the Lord fills spirits with the Divine by His look has also been made clear. A spirit that has been filled by the Lord with the Divine does not know otherwise than that he is the Lord, and that it is the Divine that is speaking; this state continues until he has finished speaking. After that, he perceives and acknowledges that he is a spirit, and that he spoke from the Lord and not from himself. Because this was the state of the spirits who spoke with the prophets, they said that it was <term>Jehovah</term><note>original: "Jehovah." In the Hebrew tradition, the personal name of God, often translated as "The LORD."</note> that spoke; the spirits even called themselves Jehovah, as can be seen [in many passages of the Word].

**255.** To understand how angels and spirits connect with humans, I have been allowed to mention some remarkable facts that explain and prove how it works. When angels and spirits turn toward a person, they believe entirely that the person’s language is their own and that they have no other. This is because they are immersed in the person's language and have temporarily forgotten their own. However, as soon as they turn away from the person, they return to their own angelic and spiritual language and remember nothing of the human language. I have experienced this myself; while in the company of angels and in a state like theirs, I spoke with them in their language and knew nothing of my own. But as soon as I was no longer with them, I was back in my own language. 

[2.] Another remarkable fact is that when angels and spirits turn toward a person, they can talk with them from any distance. They have spoken to me from a great distance as clearly as if they were right next to me. Yet, when they turn away from a person to speak with each other, the person hears nothing at all, even if they are speaking right next to the ear. This makes it clear that all connection in the spiritual world is determined by the direction in which a spirit turns. 

[3.] It is also a fact that many spirits can speak together with one person, and the person with them. They do this by sending one spirit from their group to the person they wish to speak with. This sent spirit turns toward the person, while the others turn toward that spirit, concentrating their thoughts for the spirit to speak. In this state, the spirit believes he is speaking for himself, and the group believes they are the ones speaking. This is how a connection between a group and an individual is made through "turning."¹ We will say more later about these <term>emissary spirits</term><note>Spirits acting as representatives or messengers for a larger group.</note>, who are also called <term>subjects</term><note>In this context, a "subject" is a spirit who serves as a channel or mouthpiece for a community of spirits.</note>, and how they communicate.

## XXIX.

### WRITINGS IN HEAVEN.

**258.** As the angels have speech, and their speech consists of words, they also have writings; and by writing as well as by speech they give expression to what is in their minds. At times I have had papers sent to me, traced with written words precisely like manuscripts in the world, and others like printed sheets; and I was able to read them in the same way, but was allowed to get from them only an idea here and there; for the reason that it is not in accordance with <term>Divine order</term><note>The underlying laws and structure of the universe established by God, which maintain the necessary boundaries between the spiritual and physical realms.</note> for man to be taught by writings from heaven; but he must be taught by means of <term>the Word</term><note>Referring to the Sacred Scriptures (the Bible), which the author views as the essential bridge between the Divine and humanity.</note> only; for it is only by means of the Word that there is communication and conjunction of heaven with the world, thus of the Lord with man. That papers written in heaven were seen also by the prophets is shown in *Ezekiel*,

> "When I looked, behold a hand was put forth by a spirit unto me, and a roll of a book was therein which unrolled in my sight; it was written on the front and on the back" (ii. 9, 10).

And in *John*,

> "I saw upon the right hand of Him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the back, sealed up with seven seals" (*Apoc.* v. 1)<note>The "Apocalypse" is another name for the Book of Revelation, the final book of the New Testament.</note>.

**259.** The existence of writings in heaven is a provision of the Lord for the sake of the Word; for the Word in its essence is Divine truth, and from it is all heavenly wisdom, both with men and with angels; for the Word was dictated by the Lord, and what is dictated by the Lord passes through all the heavens in order and terminates with man. Thereby it is adapted both to the wisdom of angels and the intelligence of men. Thereby, too, the angels have a Word, and read it the same as men do on the earth, and draw from it their <term>doctrinals</term><note>The formal systems of teaching or principles that define a religious or spiritual framework.</note>, and preach from it (n. 221). It is the same Word; but its natural sense, which is the sense of the letter with us, does not exist in heaven, but only the <term>spiritual sense</term><note>The deeper, symbolic meaning hidden within the literal words of scripture, which relates directly to spiritual realities and the soul.</note>, which is its internal sense. What this sense is can be seen in the small treatise on *The White Horse*<note>original: "De Equo Albo"; a reference to the author's 1758 work which explains the spiritual meaning of the white horse in the Book of Revelation.</note> spoken of in the *Apocalypse*.

## XXX.

### THE WISDOM OF THE ANGELS OF HEAVEN.

**265.** The nature of angelic wisdom can scarcely be comprehended, because it too greatly transcends human wisdom to be compared with it; and whatever is thus transcendent does not seem to be any thing. Moreover, some truths that must enter into a description of it are as yet unrecognized, and until these are recognized they exist in the mind as shadows, and thus hide the thing as it is in itself. Nevertheless, these truths can be both recognized and comprehended, provided the mind takes any interest in them; for interest carries light with it because it is from love; and upon those who love the things pertaining to <term>Divine and heavenly wisdom</term><note>The specific type of understanding that comes from God and characterizes life in the spiritual world</note> light shines forth from heaven and gives <term>enlightenment</term><note>A spiritual awakening or clarity provided by God that allows a person to perceive deeper truths</note>.

(That the heat of heaven is Divine good or Divine love may be seen above, in sections 133–140.) That the angels are so steeped in wisdom that they may even be called "wisdoms" follows from the fact that their thoughts and affections all flow in accordance with the "heavenly form." This form is the very pattern of Divine wisdom, and the angels’ inner selves—which receive this wisdom—are arranged in that same form. (That the thoughts and affections of angels, and consequently their intelligence and wisdom, flow in accordance with the form of heaven may be seen above, in sections 201–212.) 

**[2.]** The superior nature of angelic wisdom is shown by the fact that their speech is the speech of wisdom itself. It flows directly and spontaneously from their thought, and their thought flows from their affection; thus, their speech is simply their inner feeling and thought taking an outward form. Consequently, there is nothing to distract them from the <term>Divine influx</term><note>The constant flow of life, light, and love from the Divine into the spirits of angels and men.</note>, and no outside interference like the worldly thoughts that enter into human speech. (That the speech of angels is the direct expression of their thought and affection may be seen above, in sections 234–245.) That the angels possess such wisdom is also consistent with the fact that everything they see with their eyes and perceive with their senses agrees with their wisdom. These things are <term>correspondences</term><note>The spiritual principle where outward, visible things perfectly mirror and represent inward, spiritual states.</note> of their wisdom; the objects they perceive are visible forms representing the things that make up their intelligence. (That all things seen in the heavens correspond with the inner states of angels may be seen above, in sections 170–182.) 

**[3.]** Furthermore, the thoughts of angels are not limited or narrowed by ideas of space and time as human thoughts are. Space and time belong to the world of nature, and things belonging to nature tend to withdraw the mind from spiritual realities and limit the reach of intellectual vision. (That the ideas of angels exist apart from time and space, and are thus less limited than human ideas, may be seen above, in sections 162–169 and 191–199.) Again, the thoughts of angels are neither dragged down to earthly and material things, nor are they interrupted by anxieties about the necessities of life. Thus, they are not pulled away from the delights of wisdom by the worries that affect people in the world. All things are provided to them freely by the Lord; they are clothed, fed, and housed at no cost to themselves (sections 181–190); and because...

**267.** Angels are capable of receiving such wisdom because their <term>interiors</term><note>In this context, "interiors" refers to the inner levels of the mind and spirit which are capable of connecting with the Divine.</note> are open; and wisdom, like every other perfection, increases toward the interiors—thus, to the extent that these inner levels are opened. In every angel, there are three degrees of life, corresponding to the three heavens (see sections 29–40). Those in whom the first degree has been opened are in the first or <term>outmost heaven</term><note>Also known as the natural heaven, the level of heaven closest to the experience of the physical world.</note>; those in whom the second degree has been opened are in the second or middle heaven; and those in whom the third degree has been opened are in the third or inmost heaven.

The wisdom of angels in the heavens is in accord with these degrees. Therefore, the wisdom of the angels of the inmost heaven immeasurably surpasses the wisdom of angels of the middle heaven, and the wisdom of these immeasurably surpasses the wisdom of angels of the outmost heaven (see above, sections 209, 210; and for an explanation of degrees, see section 38). These differences exist because the higher degree consists of <term>particulars</term><note>Specific, detailed units of spiritual information.</note>, while the lower degree consists of <term>generals</term><note>Broad or universal concepts that contain many specific details within them.</note>, and generals are the containers of particulars. Particulars, when compared with generals, are as thousands or myriads to one; such is the wisdom of the angels of a higher heaven compared with the wisdom of the angels of a lower heaven. In like manner, the wisdom of the lower angels surpasses the wisdom of man, for man exists in a bodily state and in those things belonging to the bodily senses, and such things belong to the lowest degree. This makes clear what kind of wisdom is possessed by those who think only from things of—

**270.** The wisdom of the angels of the **third or inmost heaven** shall now be described, and also how far it surpasses the wisdom of the angels of the **first or outmost heaven**. The wisdom of the angels of the third or inmost heaven is incomprehensible even to those who are in the outmost heaven. This is because the **interiors**<note>The internal spiritual faculties or levels of the soul.</note> of the angels of the third heaven have been opened to the **third degree**, while the interiors of angels of the first heaven have been opened only to the **first degree**. All wisdom increases as one moves toward these interior levels and is perfected as they are opened. 

[2.] Because the interiors of the angels of the third or inmost heaven have been opened to the third degree, **Divine truths** are, as it were, inscribed upon them. The interiors of the third degree are more fully in the **form of heaven** than the interiors of the lower degrees; and since the form of heaven originates from Divine truth—and is thus in harmony with Divine wisdom—truth seems to be inscribed on these angels, or even instinctive and inborn in them. 

Therefore, as soon as these angels hear genuine Divine truths, they instantly acknowledge and perceive them; they later see them as if they were deep within themselves. Because the angels of that heaven are of this nature, they never reason about Divine truths, and they certainly do not dispute whether a thing is true or not. In fact, they do not even know what it means "to believe" or to have **faith**. They say, "What is faith? For I can see and perceive that this is so." 

They illustrate this using comparisons. For example, they say it would be like someone standing with a companion and looking at a house and the objects in and around it. If that person were to tell his companion that he "ought to believe" these things exist, or that they are exactly as they appear to be, it would be absurd—he is seeing them clearly with his own eyes. Or, if they were looking at a garden with trees and fruit, it would be like telling the companion to "have faith" there is a garden, even though it is right in front of him. For this reason, these angels never mention faith and have no concept of what it is; neither do they...

**272.** There is a still further reason—and in heaven this is the primary reason—why the angels are able to receive such great wisdom: they are without the **love of self**. To the extent that anyone is free from the love of self, they have the capacity to be wise in Divine things. It is that self-centered love that closes up the <term>interiors</term><note>The "interiors" refers to the deeper, spiritual levels of the human mind and soul that are capable of connecting with heaven.</note> against the Lord and heaven, and opens the exteriors, turning them only toward oneself. As a consequence, all those ruled by self-love are in thick darkness regarding the things of heaven, no matter how much "light" or cleverness they may have in worldly matters. 

The angels, on the other hand, exist in the light of wisdom because they are without the love of self. The heavenly loves they possess—love to the Lord and love toward the neighbor—open their inner selves, because these loves come from the Lord and the Lord Himself is present within them. (That these loves constitute heaven in general, and form the heaven within each person in particular, may be seen above, numbers 13-19.) As heavenly loves open the inner mind to the Lord, all angels turn their faces towards the Lord (n. 142); because in the <term>spiritual world</term><note>The reality beyond the physical realm where thoughts and affections determine one's environment and orientation.</note>, love turns the inner self of everyone toward what it loves. Whichever way the inner self turns, the face follows, since in that world the face is one with the inner mind—it is simply the outward form of it. **273.** Although the angels are unceasingly perfected in wisdom,¹ their wisdom, even to eternity, cannot become so perfect that there can be any <term>ratio</term><note>In this context, ratio means a mathematical proportion or direct comparison; the finite can never "catch up" to the infinite.</note> between it and the Lord's Divine wisdom; for the Lord's Divine wisdom is infinite and the wisdom of angels finite; and between what is infinite and what is finite no ratio is possible.

**274.** As it is wisdom that makes the angels perfect and constitutes their life, and as heaven with its good things flows into every one in the measure of his wisdom, so all in heaven desire and hunger for wisdom much as a hungry man hungers for food. So, too, knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom are <term>spiritual nutriment</term><note>Just as the body needs food to grow, the soul needs truth and wisdom to develop; this is a core concept of "correspondence" between the physical and spiritual worlds.</note>, as food is natural nutriment; and the one corresponds to the other.

**275.** The angels in the same heaven, or in the same society of heaven, are not all in like wisdom; their wisdom differs. Those at the centre are in the greatest wisdom, and those round about even to the borders are in less wisdom. The decrease of wisdom in accord with the distance from the centre is like the decrease of light verging to shade (see sections 43 and 128). Their light is in the same degree as their wisdom, since the light of heaven is the Divine wisdom, and every one is in light in the measure of his reception of wisdom. ### THE STATE OF INNOCENCE OF ANGELS IN HEAVEN.

**276.** What innocence is and its nature few in the world know, and those who are in evil know nothing about it. It is, indeed, visible to the eyes, as seen in the face, speech, and movements, particularly of children; and yet what innocence is, and especially that it is that in which heaven is stored up in

The nature of innocence is as yet unknown to humanity. In order to make this clear, let us proceed in order: considering first the innocence of childhood, then the innocence of wisdom, and finally the state of heaven in relation to innocence.

**277.** The <term>innocence of childhood</term><note>Swedenborg distinguishes between the natural, "empty" innocence of a baby and the "wise" innocence of an adult who has chosen good over evil.</note> is not genuine innocence; it is innocence in its external appearance only, not its inner reality. Nevertheless, we can learn what true innocence is by observing it, for it shines through the faces of children, their movements, and their first attempts at speech, deeply affecting those around them. It is evident that children have no internal world of thought, for they do not yet distinguish between what is good and what is evil, or what is true and what is false—the very things that form our inner thoughts. 

[2.] Because of this, they possess no <term>prudence</term><note>In this context, "prudence" refers to a self-serving cleverness or the ability to calculate for one's own advantage.</note> of their own. They have no hidden agendas or deliberate schemes, and therefore no intent that aims at doing harm. They have not yet acquired a "self" rooted in the love of themselves or the world. They do not claim ownership over anything, viewing everything they have as a gift from their parents. They are satisfied with the small and simple things given to them and find genuine joy in them. They feel no anxiety about food or clothing, and no worry about the future. They do not look toward the world with greed or desire to possess many things. They love their parents, their nurses, and their playmates with whom they interact in simple goodness. They allow themselves to be led; they listen and they obey. 

[3.] Being in this state, they receive everything as a part of their very life. This is why, without knowing how or why, they adopt graceful manners, learn to speak, and begin to develop memory and thought. Their state of innocence acts as a <term>medium</term><note>A "medium" here is like a fertile soil or a bridge that allows spiritual qualities to take root in the physical mind.</note> through which these abilities are received and planted. However, as mentioned before, this innocence is external because it belongs only to the body and not yet to the mind;¹ for their minds are not yet fully formed—a "mind" being the combination of understanding, will, and the thoughts and feelings that grow from them. 

[4.] I have been told from heaven that children are under the Lord’s special <term>auspices</term><note>Divine care or guidance.</note>, and that they receive <term>influx</term><note>The spiritual concept of life or energy "flowing in" from the Divine into the human soul.</note> from the inmost heaven, where the state is one of pure innocence.

### INNOCENCE OF ANGELS IN HEAVEN.

...rld. <note>The text continues from the previous page's discussion on children not looking toward the "world."</note> Instead, they look toward heaven, where there is a state of innocence. This divine influence flows through their inner being, and as it passes through, their deepest thoughts and feelings are affected purely by that innocence. For this reason, innocence is visible in their faces and in their movements, and it becomes clearly evident. It is this very innocence that touches parents so deeply in their own hearts, giving rise to the instinctive love called <term>storge</term><note>original: "storge". A Greek term referring specifically to the natural, instinctive affection of parents for their offspring.</note>.

**278.** The "innocence of wisdom" is the only true, genuine innocence because it is internal. It belongs to the mind itself—specifically to the human <term>will</term> and <term>understanding</term><note>In Swedenborg’s philosophy, the "will" is the seat of what we love and desire, while the "understanding" is the seat of what we think and believe.</note>. When innocence is present in these two parts of the mind, wisdom is also present, for wisdom also resides in the will and the understanding. This is why it is said in heaven that innocence lives within wisdom, and that an angel possesses exactly as much innocence as they have wisdom. This is proven by the fact that those who live in a state of innocence do not take credit for any good they do. Instead, they see all things as gifts and credit them to the Lord. They wish to be led by Him and not by themselves. They love everything that is good and find joy in everything that is true because they know and perceive that loving what is good—that is, wanting it and doing it—is actually loving the Lord, and loving truth is loving one's neighbor. They live content with what they have, whether it is little or much, because they know they receive exactly what is useful for them: those who need little receive little, and those who need much receive much. They also recognize that they do not know what is best for themselves; only the Lord knows this, as He looks toward eternity in everything He provides.

[2.] They feel no anxiety about the future. They call such worry "care for the morrow," which they define as grief over losing or failing to receive things that are not necessary for the requirements of life. In their dealings with companions, they never act from motives that look toward evil, but only from what is good, just, and sincere. Acting from evil motives is what they call cunning, which they avoid like the poison of a snake, as it is completely opposite to innocence. Because they love nothing more than being led by the Lord, giving Him credit for everything they receive, they are kept away from <term>what is their own</term><note>original: "proprium". A technical term in this theology referring to the "self-hood" or the human ego that believes it is independent of God.</note>. To the extent they are kept away from their own ego, the Lord flows into them. As a result, whatever they hear from the Lord—whether through the Word or through preaching—they do not merely store up in the memory, but they obey it instantly; that is, they will it and do it. Their will effectively becomes their memory. Outwardly, these people often appear simple, but inwardly they are wise and prudent. These are the people the Lord meant when He said:

Therefore, so far as an angel is in innocence he is in heaven, in other words, is in **Divine good** and **Divine truth**, for to be in these is to be in heaven.

### INNOCENCE OF ANGELS IN HEAVEN.

Consequently, the heavens are distinguished by degrees of innocence. Those who dwell in the outmost or first heaven exist in innocence of the first or outmost degree. Those in the middle or second heaven exist in innocence of the second or middle degree. However, those in the inmost or third heaven exist in innocence of the third or inmost degree; these are the **true embodiments of innocence** <note>original: "veriest innocences". This refers to those who represent the purest form of the quality.</note> within heaven. More than all others, they love to be led by the <term>Lord</term><note>The author uses "the Lord" to refer to the Divine as the guide and father of all.</note> as little children are led by their father. For this same reason, they receive the <term>Divine truth</term><note>Spiritual reality or communication flowing from the Divine.</note>—which they hear either directly from the Lord or indirectly through the **Word** and preaching—straight into their will and put it into practice, thereby making it part of their life.

This is why their wisdom is so much greater than that of the angels in the lower heavens (see sections 270 and 271). Because these angels of the inmost heaven are of such a character, they are nearest to the Lord, from whom they receive their innocence. They are so far removed from their own "self" <note>Referring to the "proprium" or the selfish ego.</note> that they live, as it were, in the Lord. Outwardly, they appear simple; to the eyes of the angels in the lower heavens, they even look like children—very small and seemingly not very wise—even though they are actually the wisest of all the angels in heaven. They are wise because they know they have no wisdom of their own, and they recognize that this acknowledgment is the very heart of being wise. They also know that what they do know is as nothing compared to what they do not know; they say that knowing, acknowledging, and perceiving this is the first step toward true wisdom. These angels wear no clothing, because in the spiritual world, nakedness corresponds to innocence.¹

**281.** I have spoken extensively with angels about innocence, and I have been told that innocence is the <term>essential being<note>original: "esse". In this context, it refers to the fundamental soul or inner core that makes a thing what it is.</note></term> of everything good. Consequently, "good" is only truly good to the extent that innocence is within it. Likewise, wisdom is only true wisdom to the extent that it shares in innocence; the same applies to love, charity, and faith.²

**283.** Every one who is in the good of innocence is affected by innocence, and is affected to the extent that he is in that good; but those who are not in the good of innocence are not affected by innocence. # XXXII.

## THE STATE OF PEACE IN HEAVEN.

**284.** Only those that have experienced the peace of heaven can have any perception of the peace in which the angels are. As man is unable, as long as he is in the body, to receive the peace of heaven, so he can have no perception of it, because his perception is confined to what is natural. To perceive it he must be able, in respect to thought, to be raised up and withdrawn from the body and kept in the spirit, and at the same time be with angels. In this way has the peace of heaven been perceived by me; and for this reason I am able to describe it, yet not in words as that peace is in itself, because human words are inadequate, but only as it is in comparison with that rest of mind that those enjoy who are content in God. <note>The author, Emanuel Swedenborg, frequently claims that his descriptions of the afterlife are not mere theories but based on his direct spiritual experiences and "sight" into the angelic realm.</note>

**285.** There are two inmost things of heaven, namely, innocence and peace. These are said to be inmost things because they proceed directly from the Lord. From innocence comes every good of heaven, and from peace every delight of good. Every good has its delight; and both good and delight spring from love, for whatever is loved is called good, and is also perceived as delightful. From this it follows that these two inmost things, innocence and peace, go forth from the Lord's Divine love and move the angels from what is inmost. That innocence is the inmost of good may be seen in the preceding chapter, where the state of innocence of the angels of heaven is described. That peace is the inmost of delight from the good of innocence shall now be explained.

**286.** The origin of peace shall be first considered. Divine peace is in the Lord; it springs from the union of the Divine itself and the <term>Divine Human</term> <note>original: "Divinum Humanum." This term refers to the concept of God in a human form that is accessible to human understanding and relationship.</note> in Him. The Divine of peace in heaven is from the Lord, springing from His <term>conjunction</term> <note>original: "conjunctio." A deep spiritual union or bonding between the Lord and the individual, or between the concepts of "good" and "truth."</note> with the angels of heaven, and in particular from the conjunction of good and truth in each angel. These are the origins of peace. From this it can be seen that peace in the heavens is the Divine inmostly affecting with blessedness every thing good there, and from this is every joy of heaven; also that it is in its essence the Divine joy of the Lord's Divine love, resulting from His conjunction with heaven and with every one there.

<summary>This page defines heavenly peace as an internal state of blessedness that flows from the Lord, acting as the core delight within all heavenly good. It explains that this peace originates from the union of the Divine and the Divine Human and is experienced through the spiritual union of good and truth.</summary>
<keywords>peace, heavenly delight, innocence, Divine Human, conjunction of good and truth, spiritual perception, Divine love, Emanuel Swedenborg</keywords>

"Odor of rest" in the heavenly sense signifies a perception of peace.<gloss>1</gloss> As peace signifies the union of the Divine itself and the <term>Divine Human</term> <note>This term refers to the Lord’s humanity made Divine, which serves as the bridge between the infinite God and finite human beings.</note> in the Lord, and also the conjunction <note>In this context, "conjunction" means a deep, spiritual connection or joining together.</note> of the Lord with heaven and with the church—including all in heaven and all in the church who receive Him—the Sabbath was instituted as a reminder of these things. Its very name means *rest* or *peace*, and it served as the most holy <term>representative</term> <note>A "representative" is an outward ritual or object that mirrors a deeper spiritual reality.</note> of the church. For the same reason, the Lord called Himself "the Lord of the Sabbath"

->(*Matthew* 12:8; *Mark* 2:27, 28; *Luke* 6:5).<gloss>2</gloss><-

**288.** Because the peace of heaven is the Divine influence affecting the very core of the angels with blessedness, they can only clearly perceive it through the delight of their hearts when they are living in goodness. It is felt in the pleasure they take in hearing truths that align with their good, and in the gladness of mind they feel when they perceive the joining of good and truth. From this source, peace flows into every act and thought of their lives, manifesting as joy, even in their outward appearance. [**2.**] But peace in the heavens varies in quality and quantity, depending on the <term>innocence</term> <note>For Swedenborg, "innocence" is not just a lack of guilt, but a state of being led by the Lord rather than by oneself.</note> of those who dwell there; for innocence and peace always walk hand in hand. Every good of heaven, indeed, is born from the union of these two...

In a personal sense, it symbolized the connection between the Lord and man, because man then experiences peace and salvation (numbers 8494, 8510, 10360, 10367, 10370, 10374, 10668, 10730).

heaven, as said above, is from innocence, and every delight of that good is from peace. Evidently, then, what has been said in the foregoing chapter about the state of innocence in the heavens may be said here of the state of peace there, since the conjunction <note>A deep spiritual joining or union.</note> of innocence and peace is like that of good and its delight; for good is felt in its delight, and delight is known from its good. This being so, it is evident that angels of the inmost or third heaven <note>The "third heaven" is the highest level of celestial existence, characterized by direct love for the Lord.</note> are in the third or inmost degree of innocence; and that angels of the lower heavens are in a less degree of peace, because they are in a less degree of innocence (see above, n. 280). 

[**3.**] That innocence and peace go together like good and its delight can be seen in little children, who are in peace because they are in innocence; and because they are in peace are in their whole nature full of play. Yet the peace of little children is external peace; while internal peace, like internal innocence, is possible only in wisdom, and for this reason only in the conjunction of <term>good and truth</term> <note>In this context, "good" refers to the inclination of the will toward love, and "truth" refers to the understanding of spiritual reality. Their union is the foundation of spiritual life.</note>, since wisdom is from that conjunction. Heavenly or angelic peace is also possible in men who are in wisdom from the conjunction of good and truth, and who in consequence have a sense of content in God; nevertheless, while they live in the world this peace lies hidden in their interiors, but it is revealed when they leave the body and enter heaven, for their interiors are then opened.

**289.** As the Divine peace springs from the conjunction of the Lord with heaven, and specially from the conjunction of good and truth in each angel, so when the angels are in a state of love they are in a state of peace; for then good and truth are conjoined in them. (That the states of angels undergo successive changes may be seen above, n. 154-160.) This is true also of a man who is being <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth and character transformation.</note>. As soon as good and truth come to be conjoined in him, which takes place especially after <term>temptations</term> <note>Spiritual trials or internal conflicts between selfish desires and heavenly ideals.</note>, he comes into a state of delight from heavenly peace.¹ This peace may be likened to morning or dawn in spring, when, the night being passed, with the rising of the sun all things of the earth begin to live anew, the fragrance of growing vegetation is spread abroad with the dew that descends from heaven, and the mild vernal temperature gives fertility to the fields and creates a sense of joy in the human heart.

**290.** I have talked with the angels about peace, saying that what is called peace in the world is when wars and hostilities cease between kingdoms, or when enmities or discords cease among men; also that internal peace is believed to consist in rest of mind when cares are removed, especially in tranquility and enjoyment from success in business. But the angels said that rest of mind and tranquility and enjoyment from the removal of cares and success in business seem to be constituents of peace, but are so only with those who are in <term>heavenly good</term> <note>A state where an individual's motivations are rooted in love for others and the Divine rather than selfish gain.</note>, for only in that good is peace possible. 

For peace flows in from the <term>Lord</term> <note>A reference to the Divine, specifically Jesus Christ, who is viewed in this theology as the source of all heavenly life.</note> into the <term>inmost</term> <note>The deepest or highest part of the human spirit, which is the first to receive life and influence from the spiritual world.</note> of such, and from their inmost descends and flows down into the lower faculties, producing a sense of rest in the mind, tranquility of disposition, and joy therefrom. But to those who are in evil peace is impossible.² There is an appearance of rest, tranquility, and delight when things succeed according to their wishes; but it is external peace and not at all internal, for inwardly they burn with enmity, hatred, revenge, cruelty, and many evil <term>lusts</term> <note>Self-centered or worldly cravings that drive the soul away from spiritual harmony.</note>, into which their disposition is carried whenever any one is seen to be unfavorable to them, and which burst forth when they are not restrained by fear. Consequently the delight of such dwells in insanity, while the delight of those who are in good dwells in wisdom. The difference is like that between hell and heaven.

### XXXIII.

## THE CONJUNCTION OF HEAVEN WITH THE HUMAN RACE.

**291.** It is acknowledged in the <term>church</term> <note>Refers generally to the Christian religious tradition and its established doctrines during the 18th century.</note> that all good is from God, and that nothing of good is from man, consequently that no one ought to ascribe any good to himself as his own. It is also acknowledged that evil is from the devil. Therefore those who speak from the doctrine of the church say of those who behave well, and of those who speak and preach piously, that they are led by God; but the opposite of those who do not behave well and who speak impiously. For this to be true there must be <term>conjunction</term> <note>A spiritual union or connection that allows influence to flow from one entity to another.</note> of heaven and of hell with man; and this conjunction must be with man's will and with his understanding; for it is from these that his body acts and his mouth speaks. What this conjunction is shall now be told.

**292.** With every individual there are good spirits and evil spirits. Through good spirits he has conjunction with heaven, and through evil spirits with hell. These spirits are in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>In this theological system, the "world of spirits" is an intermediate realm located between heaven and hell where individuals go immediately after death.</note>, which lies midway between heaven and hell. This world will be described particularly hereafter. When these spirits come to a man they enter into his entire memory, and thus into his entire thought, evil spirits into the evil things of his memory and thought, and good spirits into the good things of his memory and thought. These spirits have no knowledge whatever that they are with man; but when they are with him they believe that all things of his memory and thought are their own; neither do they see the man, because nothing that is in our <term>solar world</term> <note>The physical, material universe illuminated by the natural sun, as opposed to the spiritual world.</note> falls into their sight.¹ The Lord exercises the greatest care that spirits may not know that they are with man; for if they knew it they would talk with him, and in that case evil spirits would destroy him; for evil spirits, being joined

Man without spirits attending him cannot live (section 5993).

**293.** The reason why spirits that communicate with hell are associated with man is that man is born into <term>evils</term> <note>In this context, "evils" refers to inherited tendencies or inclinations toward selfish or worldly desires rather than specific individual sins.</note> of every kind; consequently, his first life is wholly from evil. He is therefore both held in his own life by means of evil spirits and withheld from it by means of good spirits; and by the two he is kept in **equilibrium**. Being in equilibrium, he is in freedom, and can be drawn away from evils and turned towards good. In this state, good can be implanted in him, which would not be possible if he were not in freedom; and freedom is possible to man only when the spirits from hell act on one side and spirits from heaven on the other, and man is between the two. Again, it has been shown that so far as a man’s life is from what he inherits, and thus from self, if he were not permitted to be in evil he would have no life; also if he were not in freedom he would have no life; also that he cannot be forced to what is good, and that what is forced does not abide; also that the good that man receives in freedom is implanted in his will and becomes as it were his own.¹ These

But the Lord maintains this association with such as can be <term>reformed</term> <note>The process of correcting one's outward life and thoughts to align with spiritual truths.</note> and <term>regenerated</term> <note>The deeper stage of spiritual growth where the inner heart and will are transformed by God.</note>. It is otherwise with such as cannot be reformed.

**296.** Humanity is guided by the Lord through spirits because we are not naturally born into the <term>Divine order</term> <note>The inherent laws of harmony and goodness by which God created and maintains the universe.</note> of heaven. Through this general influence, a person is guided in everything that moves from their thought and will into action—that is, in their speech and physical deeds. These follow the laws of the natural world, and therefore the spirits associated with a person have nothing in common with these outward movements. Animals are also guided by this general influence from the spiritual world because they live according to the natural order of their lives. Animals have not been able to corrupt or destroy that order because they lack a <term>rational faculty</term> <note>The ability to reason, reflect, and make conscious moral choices.</note>.¹ The difference between humans and animals can be seen in earlier sections (n. 39).

**297.** Regarding the further details of how heaven is joined to the human race, it should be noted that the Lord Himself flows into every person according to the laws of heaven. This influence reaches into a person's <term>inmosts</term> <note>The deepest, most private level of the soul where a person is most closely connected to the Divine.</note> as well as their <term>outmosts</term> <note>The external aspects of life, including physical actions and worldly thoughts.</note>. The Lord prepares the individual to receive the influence of heaven and governs their outward life from their inner soul, while simultaneously governing the inner soul from the outward life. In this way, everything within a person is held together in a single connection.

This movement of Divine life is called **direct influx**; meanwhile, the other type of influence, which happens through the mediation of spirits, is called **mediate influx**. The second kind is only possible because of the first. **Direct influx**, which comes from the Lord Himself, originates from His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>The concept that God is not an abstract energy but exists in a perfect, Divine-Human form that people can relate to and love.</note>. It flows into a person’s **will**, and through the will into the **understanding**. This means it flows into what is **good** and through that into what is **truth**—or, to put it another way, into **love** and through love into **faith**. It never happens in reverse; the Divine influence never flows into faith without love, or into truth without goodness, or into thoughts that do not come from the heart. This Divine influence is constant. Those who are good receive it in a good way, but those who are evil do not; they either reject it, stifle it, or twist it. As a result, they live an evil life, which, in a spiritual sense, is considered "death."

**298.** The spirits who are present with a person—both those connected to heaven and those connected to hell—never influence a person from their own personal memories or thoughts. If they were to flow in from their own memories, everything belonging to the spirit would seem to the person as if it were their own (as mentioned previously in section 256). Nevertheless, there...

The Lord influences both the highest things and the lowest things at the same time—and in a specific way (5147, 5150, 6473, 7004, 7007, 7270).
The Lord’s influence enters into the "good" within a person, and through that good into "truth," but never the other way around (5482, 5649, 6027, 8685, 8701, 10153).

HEAVEN AND HELL.

Through these spirits, a feeling <note>The text uses the word "affection" to describe a deep-seated desire or emotional inclination toward something.</note> for the love of what is good and true flows into a person from heaven, while a feeling for the love of what is evil and false flows in from hell. To the extent that a person's own desires match what is flowing in, those feelings are accepted into their thoughts. This is because a person’s inner thoughts always align with what they love. However, if their desires do not match, the influence is not received. It is clear, then, that because spirits do not force thoughts into a person, but only offer these feelings of good or evil, the person retains the power of choice. They have freedom. They can use their thoughts to accept the good and reject the evil, especially since they know the difference from the Word <note>A reference to the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note>. Whatever someone accepts into their thoughts with a genuine feeling becomes a part of who they are; whatever they do not accept in this way does not stay with them. This explains how good flows in from heaven and how evil flows in from hell.

**299.** I have also been allowed to learn the source of human anxiety, mental grief, and the deep sadness known as melancholy. There are certain spirits who are not yet fully connected to hell because they are still in their "first state"—a concept I will explain later when discussing the <term>World of Spirits</term> <note>The intermediate realm where souls go immediately after death before transitioning to heaven or hell.</note>. These spirits are drawn to things that are undigested and foul, similar to how food becomes spoiled in the stomach. Because they find delight in such things, they remain near a person where these conditions exist, speaking to one another out of their own twisted desires. The feeling behind their speech flows into the person from this source. When this feeling is the opposite of the person's own desires, it manifests as sadness and melancholic anxiety; but if it happens to align with the person's desires, it produces joy and cheerfulness. These spirits appear near the stomach—sometimes to the left, sometimes to the right, above or below, or at varying distances depending on their specific nature. ## XXXIV.

### THE CONNECTION OF HEAVEN WITH HUMANITY THROUGH THE WORD.

**303.** Those who think using their deeper reason can see that there is a connection between all things, through intermediate steps, back to <term>the First</term> <note>The primary Source or Origin of all things; God.</note>. They can see that whatever is not part of this connection simply disappears. When they reflect on it, they know that nothing can continue to exist on its own; it must come from something that existed before it, and thus all things come from a First Source. This connection to what came before is like the relationship between an effect and the cause that produced it; when the cause is removed, the effect is dissolved and vanishes. Because scholars have thought this way, they have observed and stated that <term>existence is a perpetual springing forth</term> <note>original Latin: "subsistentia est perpetua existentia." This suggests that creation is not a one-time event in the past, but a continuous process of being sustained in every moment.</note>. This means that all things derive their continued existence from the First; as they originally emerged from that First, they perpetually emerge from it to remain in existence. 

However, the specific nature of the connection between every individual thing and what preceded it—and thus to the First who is the source of everything—cannot be explained in just a few words because it is so varied and complex. It can only be said in general terms that there is a connection between the natural world and the spiritual world. Consequently, there is a <term>correspondence</term> <note>A symbolic and functional relationship where physical things reflect spiritual realities.</note> of everything in the natural world with everything in the spiritual world (see sections 103–115). There is also a connection, and therefore a correspondence, between every part of a human being and every part of heaven (see sections 87–102).

**304.** Human beings are created in such a way that they have a <term>conjunction</term> <note>A deep, internal joining or spiritual union.</note> and connection with the Lord, but only a close association with the angels of heaven. We have this association with angels because, in terms of the inner reaches of the mind, a human being is created just like an angel, possessing a similar will and understanding. Consequently, if a person lives according to <term>Divine order</term> <note>The laws and structure of reality as established by God.</note>, they become an angel after death, possessing the same wisdom. Therefore, when we speak of the connection between humanity and heaven, we really mean a connection with the Lord and an association with the angels; for heaven is "heaven" because of the Lord’s Divine nature, not because of anything that belongs strictly to the angels’ own <term>self-nature</term> <note>original: *proprium*; the inherent sense of self that feels independent from God.</note>. That it is the Lord’s Divine nature that creates heaven was shown previously (sections 7-12).

**[2.]** However, humans possess something that angels do not: we do not only exist in the spiritual world through our inner minds, but we also exist simultaneously in the natural world through our outer lives. These "exteriors" in the natural world include everything in our natural or external memory, along with the thoughts and imagination that spring from it. Generally, this includes all knowledge and science—with their accompanying delights and pleasures—as well as the physical senses, speech, and actions. All of these are the "outmosts" or final points where the <term>Divine influx</term> <note>The spiritual life and influence flowing constantly from God into the universe.</note> comes to rest. This influence does not stop halfway; it continues until it reaches its final expression. This shows that the final point of Divine order is found within the human being; and because it is the final point, it serves as the base and foundation for everything else.

**[3.]** Since the Lord’s Divine influence does not stop midway but flows to its final points, as stated, and since the middle part it passes through is the angelic heaven while the final point is in humanity, it follows that they are interconnected. Nothing can exist in isolation. Therefore, the connection between heaven and the human race is so strong that one derives its continued existence from the other. Humanity without heaven would be like a chain without a hook to hold it up; and heaven without the human race would be like a house without a foundation.¹

**306.** I have been told from heaven that the most ancient people had direct revelation because their <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner levels of the human mind and spirit, which are designed to receive light and love from God.</note> were turned toward heaven. Because of this, there was a direct <term>conjunction</term> <note>A spiritual joining or union.</note> of the Lord with the human race at that time. After those times, however, such direct revelation ceased. In its place, there was a "mediate" or indirect revelation by means of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The relationship between a natural object and the spiritual reality it represents; for example, "water" corresponding to "natural truth."</note>. This was because all Divine worship at that time consisted of symbols, which is why the churches of that era were called <term>representative churches</term> <note>Early religious eras where every ritual and object was meant to symbolize a deeper spiritual truth.</note>. In those days, people understood what a correspondence was and what it represented. They knew that everything on earth corresponds to spiritual things in heaven and the church—or, to put it another way, represents them. Because of this, the physical objects used in their worship served as tools to help them think spiritually, which allowed them to think in harmony with the angels. 

Once the knowledge of correspondences and representations was lost, the Word was written. In this Word, every single term and its meaning is a correspondence; therefore, it contains a <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>Also called the "internal sense," this is the deeper meaning of the Bible that deals with the soul, heaven, and the Divine.</note> or internal sense, which is the level where the angels exist. Consequently, whenever a person reads the Word and understands it according to its literal or outer sense, the angels perceive it according to its internal or spiritual sense. This is because the thoughts of angels are entirely spiritual, while the thoughts of humans are natural. These two ways of thinking may appear different, but they are actually one because they correspond to each other. In this way, after man had separated himself from heaven and broken the bond, the Lord provided the Word as a medium to join heaven and man together again.

**307.** To show how heaven is joined to man by means of the Word, I will use some passages as examples. The "New Jerusalem" is described in the *Apocalypse* <note>original: *Apocalypsi*; The Book of Revelation.</note> in these words:

All this shows how heaven is conjoined with man by means of the Word.

### XXXVI.

## THE HEATHEN, OR PEOPLES OUTSIDE OF THE CHURCH, IN HEAVEN.

**318.** There is a common opinion that those born outside of the church—often called the "nations" or the **heathen** <note>original: "gentes". In Swedenborg’s time, this referred to anyone outside of the Christian world, including those we might today call "Gentiles" or "non-Christians."</note>—cannot be saved. This is because, lacking the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, they know nothing about the Lord, and it is believed that there is no salvation apart from the Lord. However, we can be certain that these people are also saved because the mercy of the Lord is **universal**—it extends to every single individual. People outside the church are born as human beings just as much as those within the church (who are actually few in comparison), and it is not their fault that they are ignorant of the Lord. 

Anyone who thinks with a bit of enlightened reason can see that no one is born for hell. The Lord is **love itself**, and His very nature is to will the salvation of all. Therefore, He has provided a religion for everyone, which allows for an acknowledgment of the Divine and the cultivation of an **interior life**. To live according to one's religion is to live interiorly; by doing so, a person looks toward the Divine. Insofar as a person looks toward the Divine, they look away from the world and separate themselves from the "life of the world," which is merely an exterior or superficial way of living.¹

---

¹ Both the heathen and Christians are saved (sections 932, 1032, 1059, 2284, 2589, 2590, 3778, 4190, 4197).

<summary>This page argues that salvation is available to all people, regardless of their religious upbringing, because God’s mercy is universal and no one is created for damnation. It emphasizes that living sincerely according to one's conscience and religion connects a person to the Divine.</summary>

**319.** Anyone can see that the **heathen** <note>original: "gentiles". Historically used to refer to non-Christians or those from other nations.</note> as well as Christians are saved if they understand what it is that creates "heaven" in a person. Heaven is not a place you go to, but something that exists within the human heart; those who have heaven within them are the ones who enter heaven. Heaven within a person consists of acknowledging the **Divine** <term>The "Divine" refers to God or the ultimate sacred reality</term> and being guided by that Divine presence. 

The first and most essential part of every religion is to acknowledge the Divine. A religion that does not recognize the Divine is not actually a religion at all. The rules of every religion focus on worship—that is, the way the Divine should be honored so that the person's service is pleasing to Him. When a person settles this in their mind—to the extent that they truly want to do this and love doing it—they are being led by the Lord. 

It is common knowledge that people of other nations live moral lives just as Christians do, and many of them live better lives than Christians. A moral life can be lived for two reasons: out of regard for the Divine, or out of regard for other people in the world. A moral life lived for the sake of the Divine is a **spiritual life**. On the outside, these two types of moral life look exactly the same, but on the inside, they are completely different. One saves a person; the other does not. This is because someone who lives morally for the sake of the Divine is being led by God; but someone who lives morally only for the sake of other people is being led by themselves.

**[2.]** This can be shown through an example. Imagine someone who refuses to do evil to their neighbor because it is against their religion—that is, against the Divine. That person is avoiding evil for a spiritual reason. However, imagine someone else who avoids doing evil to another person only because they are afraid of the law, or afraid of losing their reputation, honor, or money. That person is acting for the sake of themselves and their status in the world; they are avoiding evil for a "natural" reason and are leading themselves. 

The life of the second person is merely natural, while the life of the first is spiritual. A person whose moral life is spiritual has heaven within them. A person whose moral life is merely natural does not have heaven within them. The reason for this is that heaven flows in from above, opening up the inner levels of a person's soul, and through those inner levels...

**326.** It is a common thing for heathen that have worshipped any god under an image or statue, or any graven thing, to be introduced, when they come into the other life, to certain spirits in place of their gods or idols, that they may rid themselves of their <term>fantasies <note>In the language of the time, "fantasies" refers to deeply held mental illusions or false beliefs formed during earthly life.</note></term>. Among the heathen in heaven the Africans are most beloved, for they receive the goods and truths of heaven more readily than others. They especially wish to be called obedient, but not faithful. They say that as Christians possess the doctrine of faith they may be called faithful; but they themselves simply accept that doctrine, or as they say, have the ability to accept it.

**327.** I have talked with some who belonged to the **Ancient Church**. <note>Swedenborg categorizes human history into spiritual "churches" or eras; the "Ancient Church" refers to the era following the Great Flood (Noah's era) but preceding the Israelite Church.</note> This is the name given to the church established after the deluge, which spread through many kingdoms: namely, Assyria, Mesopotamia, Syria, Ethiopia, Arabia, Libya, Egypt, Philistia as far as Tyre and Zidon, and throughout the land of Canaan on both sides of the Jordan. $^1$ The people of this church knew of the Lord’s coming and were filled with the <term>goods of faith <note>Acts of kindness and spiritual truths lived out in daily life.</note></term>, yet they eventually fell away and became idolaters. In the spiritual world, these spirits were positioned in front toward the left, in a dark place and in a miserable condition. Their speech was like the sound of a pipe of a single tone, almost devoid of rational thought. They said they had been in that state for many centuries, and that they are occasionally taken out to serve others in various low-level tasks. This led me to reflect on many modern Christians—who are idolaters inwardly if not outwardly, being worshippers of themselves and the world while denying the Lord in their hearts—and what kind of fate awaits them in the afterlife.

**328.** The church of the Lord is spread over the entire globe and is therefore universal. It includes everyone who has lived in the <term>good of charity <note>The practice of genuine love and goodwill toward others.</note></term> according to their own religion. The "Church Proper"—where the <term>Word <note>The Holy Scriptures or Bible.</note></term> exists and the Lord is known through it—stands in relation to those outside the church as the **heart and lungs** do in a human being. Just as all the internal organs and limbs of the body derive their life from the heart and lungs (depending on their specific form and location), so do those outside the church receive spiritual life from the light of the Word maintained by the church. This can be seen in earlier sections (n. 308).

### XXXVII.

## LITTLE CHILDREN IN HEAVEN.

**329.** It is a belief of some that only such children as are born within the church go to heaven, and that those born out of the church do not, and for the reason that the children within the church are baptized and by baptism are initiated into the faith of the church. Such are not aware that no one receives heaven or faith through baptism; for baptism is merely for a sign and memorial that man should be <term>regenerated<note>A spiritual "rebirth" or the process of being made new by God, changing from a person focused on self to one focused on love and truth.</note></term>, and that those born within the church can be regenerated because the Word <note>The Bible or Divine Scripture.</note> is there, and in the Word are the Divine truths by means of which regeneration is effected, and there the Lord who regenerates is known. $^1$ Let them know therefore that every child, wherever he is born, whether within the church or outside of it, whether of pious parents or impious, is received when he dies by the Lord and trained up in heaven, and taught in accordance with Divine order, and imbued with affections for what is good, and through these with a knowledge of what is true; and afterwards as he is perfected in intelligence and wisdom is introduced into heaven and becomes an angel. Every one who thinks from reason can be sure that all are born for heaven and no one for hell, and if man comes into hell he himself is culpable; but little children cannot be held culpable.

**330.** When children die they are still children in the other life, having a like infantile mind, a like innocence in ignorance, and a like tenderness in all things. They are merely in the rudiments of a capacity to become angels, for children are not angels but become angels. Every one passing out of this world enters the other in the same state of life, a little child in the state of a little child, a boy in the state of a boy, a 

---

$^1$ Baptism signifies regeneration by the Lord by means of the truths of faith from the Word <note>original references: *Arcana Coelestia* n. 4255, 5120, 9088, 10239, 10386-10388, 10392</note>.

Baptism is a sign that the man baptized is of the church in which the Lord, who regenerates, is acknowledged, and where the Word is from which are the truths of faith, by means of which regeneration is effected <note>original references: n. 10386-10388</note>.

Baptism confers neither faith nor salvation, but it is a witness that those who are being regenerated will receive faith and salvation <note>original reference: n. 10391</note>.

**331.** The state of children in the other life far surpasses their state in the world, for they are not clothed with an earthly body, but with such a body as the angels have. The earthly body is in itself **gross**, <note>original: "crassum" — meaning heavy, material, or lacking the agility of spirit.</note> and receives its first sensations and first motions not from the inner or spiritual world, but from the outer or natural world; and in consequence in this world children must be taught to walk, to guide their motions, and to speak; and even their senses, as seeing and hearing, must be opened by use. It is not so with children in the other life. There are as many children in each one’s care as she desires from a spiritual parental affection. This heaven appears in front before the forehead, directly in the line or <term>radius<note>The direction of sight; in the spiritual world, "direction" is determined by one's focus on the Divine.</note></term> in which the angels look to the Lord. It is so situated because all children are under the immediate <term>auspices<note>Protection, guidance, or patronage.</note></term> of the Lord; and the heaven of innocence, which is the third heaven, flows into them.
