Other such scenes are provided there, acting like educational plays adapted for children, which guide them into the understanding of truth and the love of doing good.

**336.** I was also shown how sensitive and receptive a child's understanding is. While I was praying the Lord’s Prayer, the children’s perception flowed into my own thoughts. This <term>influx<note>The spiritual process where thoughts or feelings flow from the divine or the angelic realm into a person's mind.</note></term> was perceived as something incredibly tender and soft, felt almost entirely as a pure emotion or affection. At the same time, their understanding seemed to be opened directly by the Lord, as if the divine light were simply flowing through them without any obstacle. 

Furthermore, the Lord flows into the minds of children primarily from their innermost being. Unlike adults, children have nothing to block this flow: they have no "principles of falsity" <note>Deep-seated false beliefs or prejudices that a person adopts during their adult life.</note> to bar the way to truth, nor any life of habituated evil to prevent them from receiving what is good and wise. All of this makes it clear that children do not become angels immediately after death. Instead, they are gradually led into an angelic state through the learning of truth and good, following the natural order of heaven. The Lord knows every tiny detail of their nature and leads them, according to every slight movement of their personal inclination, to embrace spiritual wisdom.

**337.** I have also seen how all these qualities are planted within them through delightful and pleasant experiences suited to their youthful spirit. I was permitted to see children dressed in the most charming clothing, wearing garlands of flowers that shimmered with heavenly colors around their chests and arms. On another occasion, I saw children accompanied by their guardians and young women in a magnificent park. This park was decorated not just with trees, but with beautiful arbors and covered paths made of laurel, with walkways leading further inside. As the children entered, dressed in their fine clothing, the flowers above the entrance beamed with a joyous light. This illustrates the nature of their happiness: they are led through these beautiful and pleasant sights into the deeper states of **innocence** and **charity** <note>In this context, charity refers to an active, selfless love for others.</note>, which the Lord continually instills within them.

<summary>Swedenborg describes the gentle, symbolic methods used by angels to educate children in heaven and explains why children are more receptive to divine wisdom than adults. He illustrates the heavenly environment as a place of beauty where delight and play are used to instill deep spiritual virtues like innocence.</summary>

**338.** It was shown to me, through a method of communication common in the spiritual world, what children’s thoughts are like when they look at objects. To them, every single thing appears to be alive. Because of this, even the smallest detail of their thought is filled with life. I also perceived that children on earth have very similar ideas when they are playing; at that age, they do not yet have the adult habit of reflecting on things as being "inanimate" or "lifeless." <note>This suggests that the "magical thinking" of childhood, where dolls or toys are treated as living beings, is actually a reflection of the innate spiritual state of a child’s mind.</note>

**339.** It was mentioned earlier that children possess either a <term>celestial genius<note>A "celestial" nature is one driven primarily by the heart and a love for what is good.</note></term> or a <term>spiritual genius<note>A "spiritual" nature is one driven primarily by the intellect and a love for what is true.</note></term>. Those of a celestial nature are easily told apart from those of a spiritual nature. Their thoughts, speech, and actions are so gentle that they seem to flow directly from a love for the Lord and a love for their playmates. However, those of a spiritual nature are not quite as gentle; in everything they do, there is a certain "vibration," like the fluttering of wings. The difference between these two types is also visible in how they express frustration and in other behaviors.

**340.** Many people might assume that children in heaven remain children forever, staying as little ones among the angels. Those who do not understand what an angel truly is might have this idea confirmed by the paintings and statues in churches, where angels are always shown as small children. But the reality is completely different.

Intelligence and wisdom are what actually make an angel. As long as children do not yet possess these, they are with the angels, but they are not yet angels themselves. As soon as they become intelligent and wise, they become true angels. Surprisingly, they do not then appear as children, but as adults. They are no longer of an "infantile" nature, but have reached a mature angelic state. Intelligence and wisdom cause this change. The reason children appear more mature—eventually looking like youths or young men as their wisdom grows—is because intelligence and wisdom are the actual <term>spiritual nourishment<note>In the spiritual world, the mind's growth directly dictates the appearance of the body; as the mind "grows" in wisdom, the spiritual body "grows" in age.</note></term> for the soul. The things that feed their minds also nourish their spiritual bodies.

From them, I learned about the progress of their life from one age to another.

**341.** That innocence is a receptacle for all things of heaven—and thus the innocence of children is a <term>plane<note>A "plane" acts as a foundational level or a surface upon which something else can be built or received; similar to a canvas for a painting.</note></term> for all affections for good and truth—can be seen from what has been shown above (sections 276–283) regarding the innocence of angels in heaven. Namely, that innocence is a willingness to be led by the Lord and not by oneself; consequently, as far as a person is in innocence, they are separated from what is purely their own, and so far as one is separated from their own, they are in what is the Lord’s own. The Lord’s own is what is called His righteousness and merit. 

But the innocence of children is not "genuine" innocence, because as of yet it is without wisdom. Genuine innocence is wisdom, since so far as anyone is wise, they love to be led by the Lord; or what is the same, so far as anyone is led by the Lord, they are wise. [2.] Therefore, children are led from the external innocence in which they are at the beginning—which is called the innocence of childhood—to internal innocence, which is the innocence of wisdom. This innocence is the goal that directs all their instruction and progress; therefore, when they have attained to the innocence of wisdom, the innocence of childhood (which in the meanwhile has served them as a foundation) is joined to them. 

[3.] The innocence of children has been represented to me as something made of wood, almost devoid of life, which becomes vivified as they are perfected by knowledges of truth and affections for good. Afterwards, genuine innocence was represented by a most beautiful child, naked and full of life; for the really innocent, who are in the inmost heaven and thus nearest to the Lord, always appear before the eyes of other angels as children, and some of them naked. This is because innocence is represented by nakedness unaccompanied by shame, as is said of the first man and his wife in <term>Paradise<note>Referring to the Garden of Eden.</note></term> (*Genesis* 2:25); so when their state of innocence perished, they were ashamed of their nakedness and hid themselves (*Genesis* 3:7, 10, 11).

# LITTLE CHILDREN IN HEAVEN.

In a word, the wiser the angels are, the more innocent they are; and the more innocent they are, the more they appear to themselves as little children. This is why in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> "childhood" signifies innocence (see above, section 278).

**342.** I have talked with angels about children—specifically, whether they are free from evils, since they have not committed any <term>actual evil<note>Evil actions intentionally chosen and committed during one’s adult life, as opposed to natural tendencies.</note></term> as adults have. I was told that they are equally in evil; in fact, they are nothing but evil themselves. However, like the angels, they are withheld from their own evils and held in a state of "good" by the Lord so effectively that it seems to them as if they are good by their own power. 

For this reason, when children have become adults in heaven, they are occasionally allowed to slip back into the <term>inherited evils<note>The natural inclinations toward selfishness or pride that Swedenborg believes every human is born with, inherited from their ancestors.</note></term> they were born with. This is done so they do not develop the false idea that the goodness within them comes from themselves rather than from the Lord. They remain in this state until they realize, acknowledge, and believe the truth of the matter. 

**[2.]** There was once the son of a king who died in childhood and grew up in heaven who held this mistaken opinion. Consequently, he was let down into that life of evils into which he was born. He then perceived from the <term>sphere<note>A spiritual "aura" or atmosphere that emanates from a person’s true character.</note></term> of his life that he had a natural disposition to dominate others and viewed adultery as a matter of no importance—evils he had inherited from his parents. But after he was brought to recognize his real character, he was again received among the angels with whom he had previously lived. 

**[3.]** In the other life <note>The spiritual world or afterlife.</note>, a person never suffers punishment on account of inherited evil, because it is not his own fault that he was born with such tendencies. He suffers only for the actual evil that is his own—that is, the evils he intentionally made a part of his life through his own actions.

**343.** Several times when a number of children that were in a purely infantile state have been with me in <term>choirs<note>In this context, groups of spirits or angels who think and act in a coordinated, harmonious rhythmic unity.</note></term>, they were heard as a tender unarranged mass, that is, as not yet acting as one, as they do when they have become more mature. To my surprise the spirits with me could not refrain from inducing them to talk. This desire is innate in spirits. But I noticed, each time, that the children resisted, unwilling to talk in this way. This refusal and resistance, which were accompanied by a kind of indignation, I have often perceived; and when an opportunity to talk was given them they would say nothing except that "It is not so." I have been taught that little children have been so tempted in order that they may get accustomed to resisting, and may begin to resist **falsity and evil**, and also that they may learn not to think, speak, and act, from another, and in consequence may learn to permit themselves to be led by no one but the Lord.

**344.** From what has been said it can be seen what child education is in heaven, namely, that it is leading them by means of an understanding of truth and the wisdom of good into the **angelic life**, which is love to the Lord and mutual love, in which is **innocence**. But how different in many cases is the education of children on the earth can be seen from this example. I was in the street of a large city, and saw little boys fighting with each other; a crowd flocked around and looked on with much pleasure; and I was told that little boys are incited to such fights by their own parents. Good spirits and angels who saw this through my eyes so revolted at it that I felt their horror; and especially that parents should incite their children to such things, saying that in this way parents extinguish in the earliest age all the mutual love and all the innocence that children have from the Lord, and initiate them into the spirit of

**345.** What the difference is between those who die in childhood and those who die in mature life shall also be told. Those dying in mature life have a <term>plane<note>A foundational layer or "ground" in the mind upon which thoughts and feelings are built.</note></term> acquired from the earthly and material world, and this they carry with them. This plane is their memory and its bodily natural affection. This remains fixed and becomes <term>quiescent<note>Quiet or inactive; in this context, the physical memory becomes a dormant foundation rather than an active tool in the spiritual world.</note></term>, but still serves their thought after death as an outmost plane, since the thought flows into it. Consequently such as this plane is, and such as the <term>correspondence<note>The spiritual relationship and harmony between an internal reality (like a thought) and an external form (like an action or a physical object).</note></term> is between the things that are in it and the <term>rational faculty<note>The human ability to reason, understand truths, and make logical connections.</note></term>, such is the man after death. But the children who die in childhood and are educated in heaven have no such plane, since they derive nothing from the material world and the earthly body; but they have a spiritual-natural plane. For this reason they cannot be in such gross affections and consequent thoughts, since they derive all things from heaven. Moreover, these children do not know that they were born in the world, but believe that they were born in heaven. Neither do they know about any other than spiritual birth, which is effected through knowledge of good and truth and through intelligence and wisdom, from which man is a man; and as these are from the Lord they believe themselves to be the Lord's own, and love to be so. Nevertheless it is possible for the state of men who grow up on the earth to become as perfect as the state of children who grow up in heaven, provided they put away bodily and earthly loves, which are the loves of self and the world, and receive in their place spiritual loves.

But few know who are meant by the "intelligent" and by those that "turn many to righteousness." The common belief is that they are such as are called the accomplished and learned, especially such as have taught in the church and have surpassed others in acquirements and in preaching; and still more such among them as have converted many to the faith. In the world all such are regarded as the intelligent; nevertheless such are not the intelligent in heaven that are spoken of in these words, unless their intelligence is <term>heavenly intelligence<note>A deep, inner understanding that comes from a genuine love for what is true and good, rather than just factual knowledge.</note></term>. What this is will now be told.

**347.** Heavenly intelligence is interior intelligence, arising from a love for truth, not with any glory in the world nor any glory in heaven as an end, but with the truth itself as an end, by which they are inmostly affected and with which they are inmostly delighted. Those who are affected by and delighted with the truth itself are affected by and delighted with the light of heaven; and those who are affected by and delighted with the light of heaven are also affected by and delighted with Divine truth, and indeed with the Lord himself; for the light of heaven is Divine truth, and Divine truth is the Lord in heaven (see above, n. 126–140). This light enters only into the <term>interiors<note>The deeper levels of the human mind or soul that are capable of receiving spiritual influence.</note></term> of the mind; for the interiors of the mind are formed for the reception of that light, and are affected by and delighted with that light as it enters; for whatever flows in and is received from heaven has in it what is delightful and pleasant. From this comes a genuine affection for truth, which is an affection for truth for truth’s sake. Those who are in this affection, or what is the same thing, in this love, are in heavenly intelligence, and "shine in heaven as with the brightness of the <term>firmament<note>original: "firmamentum." Traditionally the sky or expanse of the heavens; here it symbolizes the clarity of the spiritual intellect.</note></term>." > “To him that hath it shall be given, that he may have more abundantly” (*Matthew* 13:12; 25:29).

To love truth and good for their own sake is to will them and to do them; for those who love are those who act, while those who do not act, do not truly love. Such people also love the Lord and are loved by Him, because good and truth originate from the Lord. Since good and truth come from the Lord, the Lord Himself is present within them; consequently, He is present in those who receive good and truth into their lives by willing and doing. 

Furthermore, when a person is viewed in their true essence, they are nothing other than their own good and truth, because good is the defining property of their <term>will<note>Latin: *voluntas*; the faculty of desiring and intending.</note></term> and truth is the property of their <term>understanding<note>Latin: *intellectus*; the faculty of thinking and perceiving.</note></term>. A person is defined by the nature of their will and understanding. It is evident, then, that a person is loved by the Lord exactly to the extent that their will is formed from what is good and their understanding from what is true. To be loved by the Lord is also to love the Lord, since love is reciprocal; for the Lord grants the ability to love to those whom He loves.

**351.** It is a common belief in the world that those who possess vast knowledge—whether of church teachings, the scriptures, or the sciences—possess a more internal and sharp vision of truth than others. Such people are often considered more intelligent and wise, and they often hold this opinion of themselves. However, the nature of true intelligence and wisdom, as well as the nature of false or superficial intelligence and wisdom, will be explained in the following sections. 

**[2.]** True intelligence and wisdom consist of seeing and perceiving what is true and good, and thereby identifying what is false and evil, clearly distinguishing between them through an internal intuition and perception. Within every person, there are interior faculties and exterior faculties; the interior faculties belong to the **internal or spiritual man**, while the exterior faculties belong to the **exterior or natural man**. A person’s ability to see and perceive depends on how their "interiors" (inner qualities) are formed and made to act as one with their "exteriors" (outer qualities). 

The inner self can only be formed in heaven, while the outer self is formed in the world. When the inner self has been formed in heaven, the heavenly qualities it contains flow into the outer self (which is derived from the world), shaping it so that it <term>corresponds<note>The concept of "correspondence" describes a functional relationship where the physical or outer action perfectly mirrors and expresses a spiritual or inner cause.</note></term> with the inner self—that is, they act as one. When this harmony is achieved, the person sees and perceives from an internal perspective. These inner qualities can be formed in only one way: by the person looking toward the **Divine** and toward heaven. As previously stated, the interiors are formed in heaven; a person looks toward the Divine when they believe in the Divine, and when they believe that all truth, good, and subsequent wisdom come from the Divine. A person truly believes in the Divine when they are willing to be led by the Divine. In this way and...

**352.** Spurious intelligence and wisdom is failing to see and perceive from within what is true and what is good, and thereby what is false and what is evil. Instead, it is merely believing that to be true and good (or false and evil) which is said to be so by others, and then "confirming" it. Because such people see truth from someone else, and not from the truth itself, they can seize upon and believe what is false as readily as what is true, and can confirm it until it appears to be true; for whatever is confirmed takes on the appearance of truth, and there is nothing that cannot be confirmed. The interiors of such people are opened only from beneath; but their exteriors are opened to the extent that they have confirmed their own views. For this reason, the light by which they see is not the light of heaven, but the light of the world, which is called **natural light** (<term>lumen<note>original: "lumen"; in this context, it refers to a lower, natural form of light or cognitive understanding, as opposed to "lux," the spiritual light of heaven.</note></term>). In that light, falsehoods can shine like truths; and when confirmed, they can even appear resplendent, though not in the light of heaven. Within this class, those who have most strongly confirmed themselves are the least intelligent and wise, while those who have confirmed themselves less strongly are more so. All this shows what spurious intelligence and wisdom are. **354.** It has been granted me to speak with many of the <term>learned<note>The "learned" (Latin: *eruditi*) refers to those who have acquired extensive academic or scientific information during their life on earth.</note></term> after their departure from the world; with some of distinguished reputation and celebrated in the literary world for their writings, and with some not so celebrated, although endowed with profound wisdom. I perceived and also saw that the <term>interiors<note>The deeper levels of the mind or soul that are capable of receiving light and love from heaven.</note></term> of their minds were so closed up as to appear black (for in the spiritual world such things become visible), and in consequence they were unable to endure any heavenly light or admit any influx from heaven. This blackness which their interiors presented was more intense and extended with those that had confirmed themselves against the Divine by the <term>knowledges<note>Here, "knowledges" refers to specific facts, data, or scientific theories used as evidence.</note></term> they had acquired. In the other life such people accept all falsity with delight, imbibing it as a sponge does water; and they repel all truth as an elastic bony substance repels what falls upon it. In fact, it is said that the interiors of those that have confirmed themselves against the Divine and in favor of nature become bony, and their heads down to the nose appear callous like ebony, which is a sign that they no longer have any perception. Those of this description are immersed in quagmires that appear like bogs; and there they are harassed by the <term>fantasies<note>Distorted or delusional mental images that feel real to the spirit experiencing them.</note></term> into which their falsities are turned. Their <term>infernal fire<note>This is not a literal physical fire, but a burning, selfish passion or "lust" that torments the soul from within.</note></term> is a lust for glory and reputation, which prompts them to assail one another, and from an infernal ardor to torment those about them who do not worship them as deities; and this they do one to another in turns. Into such things is all the learning of the world changed that has not received into itself light from heaven through acknowledgment of the Divine.

For man carries with him his entire natural memory, but its contents are not then under his view, and do not come into his thought as when he lives in the world. He can take nothing from that memory and bring it forth into spiritual light because its contents are not objects of that light. But those things of the reason and under-

### EXTRACTS FROM THE SECRETS OF HEAVEN <note>Original title: *Arcana Cælestia*</note> REGARDING KNOWLEDGES.*

A person ought to be fully instructed in knowledges, since by means of them they learn how to think, then how to understand what is true and good, and finally how to be wise (n. 129, 1450, 1451, 1453, 1548, 1802).
Knowledges are the first things on which a person's life—civil, moral, and spiritual—is built and founded; they are to be learned for the sake of being useful as an end goal (n. 1489, 3310).
Knowledges open the way to the <term>internal man<note>The spiritual part of the human being that lives on after death.</note></term>, and afterwards connect that internal part with the external self according to how they are used (n. 1563, 1616).
The rational faculty is born by means of knowledges (n. 1895, 1900, 3086).
However, it is not born from the knowledges themselves, but from an affection for the *uses* derived from them (n. 1895).

[2.] There are knowledges that provide an entrance to Divine truths, and there are knowledges that do not (n. 5213).
Empty knowledges are to be destroyed (n. 1489, 1492, 1499, 1581).
Empty knowledges are those that have the love of self and the world as their goal; they sustain those selfish loves and withdraw a person from love to God and love toward the neighbor. Such knowledges close up the internal man, even to the point where the person becomes unable to receive anything from heaven (n. 1563, 1600).
Knowledges are means to becoming wise and means to becoming insane; through them, the internal man is either opened or closed, and thus the rational mind is either enriched or destroyed (n. 4156, 8628, 9922).

[3.] The internal man is opened and gradually perfected by means—

<meta>This page continues the specific references to the "Secrets of Heaven" (Arcana Coelestia), specifically exploring how factual information gathered by our physical senses provides the raw material for our spiritual growth and eternal life.</meta>

->HEAVEN AND HELL<-

If a person puts their <term>knowledges<note>From the Latin *scientifica*, meaning factual information or data gathered through the senses and education.</note></term> to good use, especially use that focuses on eternal life, those facts become beneficial (reference: n. 3086).
The facts stored in the <term>natural man<note>The part of the human personality oriented toward the physical world and sensory experience.</note></term> are met by spiritual and heavenly influences from the <term>spiritual man<note>The deeper part of the human mind that is open to heaven and spiritual truths.</note></term>. The spiritual man then adopts whatever facts are suitable for its growth (n. 1495).
The Lord then draws out the useful elements of heavenly life and perfects them. These are raised out of the storehouse of facts in the natural man by means of the <term>internal man<note>The soul or the highest level of the human spirit.</note></term> (n. 1895, 1896, 1900, 1901, 1902, 5871, 5874, 5901).
Meanwhile, any facts that are inconsistent or opposing are pushed to the side and dismissed (n. 5871, 5886, 5889).

**[4.]** The "sight" of the internal man selects only those things from the external man’s knowledge that align with what it loves (n. 9394).
From the perspective of the internal man, things related to love are in the center and in bright light; things not related to love are pushed to the edges and remain in the dark (n. 6068, 6084).
Suitable facts are gradually planted into a person's affections and come to "live" within them (n. 6325).
If a person were born into love for their neighbor, they would be born into intelligence. However, because we are born into self-love and love of the world, we are born in total ignorance (n. 6323, 6325).
True knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom are the "children" of love for God and love for one's neighbor (n. 1226, 2049, 2116).

**[5.]** It is one thing to be wise, another to understand, another to know, and another to actually *do*. Nevertheless, in those who have a spiritual life, these stages follow a specific order and exist together within their actions or deeds (n. 10331).
Furthermore, there is a difference between simply knowing a fact, acknowledging it as true, and having actual faith in it (n. 896).

**[6.]** Facts, which belong to the external or natural man, exist in the "light of the world." However, truths that have become part of a person's faith and love—and have thus been given life—exist in the "light of heaven" (n. 5212).
Truths that have gained this spiritual life are understood through the lens of natural ideas (n. 5510).
<term>Spiritual influx<note>The concept that life and influence flow from the spiritual realm down into the natural realm, never the other way around.</note></term> moves from the internal or spiritual man into the facts stored in the external or natural man (n. 1940, 8005).
Facts act as "receptacles" or vessels for the truth and goodness belonging to the internal man (n. 1469, 1496, 3068, 5489, 6004, 6023, 6052, 6071, 6077, 7770, 9922).
Facts are like mirrors in which the truths and goodness of the internal man are reflected as an image (n. 5201).
In those facts, they exist together in their most external form (n. 5373, 5874, 5886, 5901, 6004, 6023, 6052, 6071).

**[7.]** This influence is not physical but spiritual. That is, the flow comes from the internal man into the external—specifically into the facts of the external—and never from the external into the internal. Therefore, faith does not originate from mere facts (n. 3219, 5119, 5259, 5427, 5428, 5478, 6322, 9110).
A person must first take a principle from the teachings of the church (which come from the Word of God) and acknowledge those truths. Only then is it helpful to look to facts for support (n. 6047).
Thus, it is helpful for those who already believe in spiritual truths to use facts to intellectually confirm them.

### EXTRACTS REGARDING KNOWLEDGES

<term>Knowledges<note>From the Latin *scientifica*, referring to factual information or data gathered through the physical senses and education.</note></term> are useful for some, but not for those who approach them with a negative or dismissive mindset (n. 2568, 2588, 4760, 6047).

A person who refuses to believe <term>Divine truths<note>The fundamental spiritual laws and realities originating from the Divine.</note></term> until they are first convinced by scientific evidence will never come to believe (n. 2094, 2832).

Attempting to enter into the truths of faith by starting with external knowledge is a reversal of the natural order (n. 10236).

Those who attempt this become confused and irrational regarding the things of heaven and the church (n. 128, 129, 130).

They eventually fall into the false ideas that come from a selfish or evil heart (n. 232, 233, 6047).

In the afterlife, when such people try to think about spiritual matters, they appear as if they are intoxicated or "drunken" (n. 1072).

Further details on the character of such individuals (n. 196).

Examples demonstrating that spiritual realities cannot be understood when one tries to approach them solely through external facts (n. 233, 2094, 2196, 2203, 2209).

In matters of the spirit, many of the highly educated are actually more confused than those with simple minds. This is because they start from a state of denial, which they then try to justify using the vast amount of data they have gathered (n. 4760, 8629).

**[8.]** Those who use their knowledge to argue against the truths of faith do so very sharply. This is because they argue from the <term>fallacies of the senses<note>Misleading appearances provided by the physical senses, such as the sun appearing to move around the earth.</note></term>, which are very persuasive and difficult to disprove (n. 5700).

Definitions of what these sensory fallacies are and how they function (n. 5084, 5094, 6400, 6948).

Those who lack a true understanding, and those who live selfishly, are able to argue about the truths and benefits of faith, but they are incapable of actually understanding them (n. 4214).

True intelligence does not consist in simply being able to defend a specific <term>dogma<note>A set of principles or beliefs laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.</note></term>; rather, it is the ability to see whether something is true or not *before* trying to prove it (n. 4741, 6047).

**[9.]** External facts are of no value after death. The only thing that remains useful is what a person has integrated into their understanding and their life through those facts (n. 2480).

Nevertheless, all knowledge remains in the memory after death, even if it stays in a quiet, inactive state (n. 2476-2479, 2481-2486).

**[10.]** For those who are evil, their knowledge turns into falsehood because it is twisted to serve selfish ends. For those who are good, the same knowledge becomes truth because it is applied to what is good (n. 6917).

Truthful information held by an evil person is not truly "true," no matter how accurate it sounds when spoken, because there is an evil intention behind it (n. 10331).

**[11.]** An example of the deep desire that spirits have to learn (n. 1974).

Angels have a limitless longing to learn and become wise, because learning, intelligence, and wisdom are their <term>spiritual food<note>Just as the body requires physical food to survive, the spirit or soul requires truth and wisdom to grow and find fulfillment.</note></term> (n. 3114, 4459, 4792, 4976, 5147, 5293, 5340, 5342, 5410, 5426, 5576, 5582, 5588, 5655, 6277, 8562, 9003).

The knowledge held by the ancient people was the knowledge of <term>correspondences<note>The relationship and connection between the natural world and the spiritual world.</note></term> and <term>representations<note>Physical objects or actions that mirror and express spiritual realities.</note></term>. Through these, they understood spiritual things. However, this type of knowledge is completely lost today (n. 4749, 4844, 4964, 4965).

**[12.]** To understand spiritual truths, the following universal principles must be known: 
(i.) Everything in the universe relates to "good" and "truth" and their partnership. For anything to truly exist, love and faith must work together. 
(ii.) Human beings possess both <term>understanding<note>The faculty of the mind that receives truth.</note></term> and <term>will<note>The faculty of the mind that receives love or "good."</note></term>. The understanding is designed to receive truth, and the will is designed to receive what is good. Everything in a human being relates to these two and their...

### XXXIX.

## THE RICH AND THE POOR IN HEAVEN.

**357.** People hold many different opinions about who is allowed into heaven. Some believe that the poor are welcomed while the rich are excluded; others believe that rich and poor are received equally; still others believe that the rich can only be accepted if they give away all their wealth and live like the poor. One can find passages in <term>the Word<note>A term for the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note></term> that seem to support all of these different views. However, those who make a distinction between the rich and the poor regarding their place in heaven do not truly understand the Scriptures. In its inner depths, the Word is **spiritual**, but in its literal text, it is **natural**. Consequently, those who see only the literal meaning of the Bible, and not its spiritual meaning, fall into many errors—especially regarding the rich and the poor. For example, they take literally the idea that it is as difficult for a rich person to enter heaven as it is for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, or that it is easy for the poor simply because they are poor, since it is written:

> “Blessed are the poor, . . . for theirs is the kingdom of heaven ” (*Matthew 5:3*; *Luke 6:20, 21*).

But those who know anything of the <term>spiritual sense<note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that Swedenborg claims to have been revealed to him.</note></term> of the Word think differently. They know that heaven is for everyone who lives a life of faith and love, whether they are rich or poor. I will explain in the following sections who is actually meant by "the rich" and "the poor" in the Bible. From my many conversations and interactions with angels, I have been allowed to know for certain that the rich enter heaven just as easily as the poor. No one is shut out of heaven because of their wealth, and no one is received into heaven simply because of their poverty.

<summary>This page explains that spiritual growth requires understanding the connection between our internal and external selves and clarifies that entry into heaven depends on a life of love and faith rather than one's earthly financial status.</summary>

**358.** It should be said to begin with that a man may acquire riches and accumulate wealth as far as opportunity is given, if it is not done by craft or fraud; that he may enjoy the delicacies of food and drink if he does not place his life therein; that he may have a palatial dwelling in accord with his condition, have intercourse with others in like condition, frequent places of amusement, talk about the affairs of the world, and need not go about like a devotee with a sad and sorrowful countenance and drooping head, but may be joyful and cheerful; nor need he give his goods to the poor except so far as affection leads him; in a word, he may live outwardly precisely like a man of the world; and all this will be no obstacle to his entering heaven, provided that inwardly in himself he thinks about God as he ought, and acts sincerely and justly in respect to his neighbor. For a man is such as his <term>affection<note>In this context, affection refers to the underlying desire or love that drives a person’s choices.</note></term> and thought are, or such as his love and faith are, and from these all his outward acts derive their life; since acting is willing, and speaking is thinking, acting being from the will, and speaking from the thought. So the declarations in the <term>Word<note>A term used by Swedenborg to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note></term> that man will be judged in accordance with his deeds, and will be rewarded in accordance with his works, mean that he will be judged and rewarded in accordance with his thought and affection, which are the source of his deeds, or which are in his deeds; for deeds are nothing apart from these, and are precisely such as these are.¹

---

¹ It is very frequently said in the Word that man will be judged and will be rewarded in accordance with his deeds and works (n. 3934).
By “deeds and works,” deeds and works in their internal form are meant, not in their external form, since good works in external form are likewise done by the wicked, but in internal and external form together only by the good (n. 3934, 6073).
Works, like all activities, have their **being and manifestation** <note>original: "esse et existere"</note> and their quality, from the <term>interiors<note>The internal psychological and spiritual states of a person, such as their true intentions and beliefs.</note></term> of man, which pertain to his thought and will, since they proceed from these; therefore such as the interiors are such are the works (n. 3934, 8911, 10331).
That is, such as the interiors are in regard to love and faith (n. 3934, 6073, 10331, 10332).
Thus works contain love and faith, and are love and faith in effect (n. 10331).
Therefore to be judged and rewarded in accordance with deeds and works, means in accordance with love and faith (n. 3147, 3934, 6073, 8911, 10331, 10332).
So far as works look to self and the world they are not good, and are good only so far as they look to the Lord and the neighbor (n. 3147).

->HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

All this shows that a person’s <term>external<note>The 'external' refers to outward behavior, speech, and social reputation—how one appears to the world.</note></term> accomplishes nothing on its own; only the <term>internal<note>The 'internal' refers to a person’s actual intentions, thoughts, and the 'why' behind their actions.</note></term>, which is the source of the external, truly matters. For example: if a man acts honestly and avoids cheating solely because he fears the law or losing his reputation, honor, or profit—and would defraud others the moment those fears were removed—his heart is still full of fraud, even if his deeds look honest. Because he is inwardly dishonest, he carries the state of <term>hell</term> within himself. However, the person who acts honestly and avoids fraud because it is a sin against God and his neighbor would have no desire to cheat even if he could get away with it. His thoughts and will are guided by <term>conscience</term>, and he carries <term>heaven</term> within himself. The outward actions of these two people look identical, but inwardly they are completely different.

**359.** Since a person can live outwardly just like anyone else—acquiring wealth, eating well, living in an elegant house, wearing fine clothes suited to their station, enjoying pleasures, and working in business for the sake of their physical and mental health—it is clear that finding the path to heaven is not as difficult as many believe. The only real difficulty is being able to resist the **love of self** and the **love of the world**, and preventing them from becoming the dominant forces in one's life; for these loves are the root of all evil. <note>original: "amor sui et mundi"</note> That this is not as hard as people think is shown by the words of the Lord:

> "Learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls; for My yoke is easy and My burden is light" (*Matthew* 11:29, 30).

The Lord’s yoke is easy and His burden light because a person is led by the Lord and not by their own ego, to the exact extent that they resist the evils arising from self-love and worldly-love. When a person makes that effort, the Lord Himself resists and removes those evils for them.

**360.** I have spoken with some after death who, while they lived in the world, renounced society and gave themselves up to a nearly solitary life. They did this in order to practice an **abstraction** <note>In this context, 'abstraction' refers to the spiritual practice of withdrawing one's thoughts from physical, worldly concerns to focus entirely on the divine.</note> of the...

<margin>2. These evils include contempt for others, enmity, hatred, revenge, cruelty, and deceit (references: n. 6667, 7370-7374, 9348, 10038, 10742).</margin>

[2.] A person can only be prepared for heaven by living in the world. It is in the world that our inner feelings find their "outmost effects"—the physical actions where every person’s affection must find its conclusion. Unless an affection expresses itself or flows out into actions (which happens through interacting with others), it eventually becomes so stifled that the person no longer cares for their **neighbor**, but only for themselves. All of this makes it clear that a life of **charity** toward one's neighbor—which means doing what is just and right in every task and every job—is what leads to heaven, and not a life of **piety** practiced apart from charity;¹ and from this, it follows that **charity** can only be practiced, and a life of **charity** can only grow, to the extent that a person is actively engaged in the business of life. This growth is impossible if a person separates themselves from such duties.

[3.] I will now speak on this subject from my own experience. Among those who were involved in trade and commerce in the world and became rich through those pursuits, many are now in heaven. However, there are not as many who held high-ranking positions and became rich through those roles. This is because those in high office were often led by their profits and honors to love themselves and the world. Through the very act of dispensing justice and managing lucrative, honorable posts, they were tempted to separate their thoughts and affections from heaven and turn them toward themselves. For as much as a person loves themselves and the world, and looks only to themselves and the world in everything they do, they distance themselves from <term>the Divine<note>original: "Divinum"</note></term> and separate themselves from heaven.

HEAVEN AND HELL.
224

**361.** As for the fate of the rich in heaven, they are wealthier than everyone else. Some of them live in palaces where every detail shines as if made of gold and silver. They possess an abundance of everything needed for life, yet they do not value these possessions for their own sake; instead, they focus entirely on <term>uses<note>In Swedenborg's writing, "uses" refers to performing beneficial services or productive work that helps society and other people.</note></term>. To them, these "uses" are seen clearly, as if bathed in light, while the gold and silver are seen only dimly, as if in the shadows. This is because, during their life in the world, they loved being useful, and valued gold and silver only as tools to achieve those ends. In heaven, it is these useful services that shine: the "good" of a service shines like gold, and the "truth" or wisdom behind a service shines like silver. Therefore, their wealth in heaven matches the quality of the service they provided in the world, and so does their delight and happiness. 

Providing for oneself and one’s family with the necessities of life is considered a good "use." So is desiring wealth for the sake of one's country and for the sake of one's neighbor; a wealthy person can help others in many more ways than a poor person can. These are considered good uses because they allow a person to avoid an idle life, which is harmful; in an idle life, a person’s thoughts naturally drift toward evil because of the selfish tendencies inherent in human nature. These uses are good to the extent that they contain a "Divine" quality—that is, as long as the person looks toward the Divine and heaven, finds their true happiness in spiritual things, and views wealth only as a secondary tool to do good.

**362.** However, the fate of the rich who did not believe in the Divine, and who rejected the things of heaven and the church from their minds, is the exact opposite. Such people end up in hell, a place of filth, misery, and poverty. In that state, the riches they loved for their own sake are transformed into these wretched conditions. This happens not only to their riches but also to the way they spent their time, which was focused either on living purely for their own pleasure or seeking the freedom to commit evil acts more easily, or seeking to rise—

***

¹ Every good action derives its joy from the service it performs and is defined by that service (sections 3049, 4984, 7038); the quality of the good is determined by the quality of the service (section 3049).
All the happiness and joy of life comes from performing useful services (section 997).
In a general sense, life itself is a life of being useful (section 1964).
The life of an angel consists of the goodness of love and charity—which means performing useful services (section 454).
The goals a person has in mind, which are their intended services, are the only things the Lord and the angels look at (sections 1317, 1645, 5844).
The kingdom of the Lord is a kingdom of useful services (sections 454, 696, 1103, 3645, 4054, 7038).
To perform a service is to serve the Lord (section 7038).
A person's true character is defined by the services they perform (sections 4054, 6815); this is further explained in section 7038.

**363.** Every man’s ruling affection or love remains with him after death, nor is it rooted out to eternity, since a man’s spirit is wholly what his love is, and—what is unknown—the body of every spirit and angel is the outward form of his love, exactly corresponding to his inward form, which is the form of his disposition and mind; consequently the quality of his spirit is known from his face, movements, and speech. While a man is living in the world the quality of the spirit would be known if he had not learned to counterfeit in his face, movements, and speech what is not his own. All this shows that man remains to eternity such as his ruling affection or love is. It has been granted me to talk with some who lived seventeen hundred years ago <note>Swedenborg often claimed to have the ability to speak with the spirits of people from the distant past, including biblical figures and famous philosophers.</note>, and whose lives are well known from writings of that time, and I found that the same love still rules them as when they were on the earth. This makes clear also that everyone’s love of riches, and of uses from riches, remains to eternity, and that it is exactly the same as the love acquired in the world, yet with the difference that in the case of those who devoted their riches to good uses riches are changed in the other world into delights which are in accord with the uses performed; while in the case of those who devoted their riches to evil uses riches are turned into mere filth, in which they take the same delight as they did in the world in their riches devoted to evil uses. Such then take delight in filth because filthy pleasures and iniquities, which had been the uses to which they had devoted their riches, and also avarice, which is a love of riches without regard to use, correspond to filth. Spiritual filth is nothing else.

There are many among the poor who are not content with their lot, who strive after many things, and believe riches to be blessings;¹ and when they do not gain them are much provoked, and harbor ill thoughts about the <term>Divine providence<note>The belief that God's government is constant and works for the eternal salvation of every person, even through worldly hardship.</note></term>; they also envy others the good things they possess, and are as ready as any one to defraud others whenever they have opportunity, and to indulge in filthy pleasures.

They were therefore told that charity is every thing that pertains to life, and faith everything that pertains to doctrine; consequently charity is willing and doing what is just and right in every work, and faith is thinking justly and rightly; and faith and charity are conjoined, the same as doctrine and a life in accordance with it, or the same as thought and will; and faith becomes charity when that which a man thinks justly and rightly he also wills and does, and then they are not two but one. This they well understood, and rejoiced, saying that in the world they did not understand believing to be anything else but living.

## XL.

### MARRIAGES IN HEAVEN.

**366.** As heaven is formed from the human race, and because angels are therefore human beings of both sexes, it follows that there are marriages in heaven just as there are on earth. From their very creation, woman is meant for man and man for woman; they belong to one another, and an innate love for the other exists in both. We shall now explore what these heavenly marriages are like, how they differ from earthly ones, and how they resemble them.

**367.** Marriage in heaven is the <term>conjunction<note>A term used by Swedenborg to describe a deep, spiritual union where two distinct things become a single functioning whole.</note></term> of two people into one mind. To understand this, we must first explain what the "mind" is. The mind consists of two parts: the **understanding** <note>The faculty of the mind that deals with thought, logic, and truth.</note> and the **will** <note>The faculty of the mind that deals with intention, desire, and love.</note>. When these two parts work together in harmony, they are called "one mind." In this heavenly union, the part called the understanding acts as the husband, and the part called the will acts as the wife. When this internal union of the spirit descends into the lower parts of the person and the body, it is felt as love, specifically "marriage love." <note>This is often translated from the Latin *amor conjugialis*, a specific term for the highest form of spiritual love between partners.</note> This shows that marriage love starts with the joining of two minds into one. In heaven, this is called "cohabitation," and the two are not called two, but one. Thus, a married pair in heaven is spoken of not as two separate individuals, but as one single angel.¹

**368.** Furthermore, this joining of husband and wife in the deepest parts of their minds is a result of their creation. Man is born to be **intellectual**—that is, to think from his understanding—while woman is born to be **affectional**—that is, to think from her will. This is clearly seen from the natural inclination or—

---

¹ In the present day, people do not know what marriage love truly is or where it comes from (*Secrets of Heaven* <note>original: "n." followed by numbers refers to paragraph sections in Swedenborg's *Arcana Coelestia*.</note> n. 2727). 
Marriage love consists of wanting what the other person wants—a mutual and shared desire (n. 2731). 
Those who experience marriage love are joined in the very core of their lives (n. 2732). 
It is such a union of two minds that, through love, they become one (n. 10168, 10169). 
For the love of minds is a spiritual love, and spiritual love is a union (n. 1594, 2057, 3939, 4018, 5807, 6195, 7081-7086, 7501, 10130).

Regarding their form, the man has a rougher and less beautiful face, a deeper voice, and a harder body; whereas the woman has a smoother and more beautiful face, a softer voice, and a more tender body. There is a similar difference between the **understanding** <note>The faculty of the mind that processes logic and thought.</note> and the **will** <note>The faculty of the mind that processes desire and love.</note>, or between thought and affection; so, too, between truth and good, and between faith and love; for truth and faith belong to the understanding, and good and love belong to the will. Because of this, in <term>the Word<note>Swedenborg's term for the Bible, specifically its deeper spiritual meaning.</note></term>, a "youth" or a "man" signifies, in the <term>spiritual sense<note>The inner, symbolic meaning of scripture that relates to the soul and the afterlife.</note></term>, the understanding of truth, while a "virgin" or a "woman" signifies the affection for what is good. It is also for this reason that the church—because of its affection for good and truth—is called a "woman" and a "virgin." Furthermore, all those who live in the affection for what is good are called "virgins" (as seen in *Revelation* xiv. 4).¹

**369.** Every person, whether man or woman, possesses both understanding and will; however, in the man, the understanding predominates, and in the woman, the will predominates. A person’s character is determined by which of these two is the primary influence. Yet, in heavenly marriages, there is no such thing as "dominance." This is because the will of the wife is also the husband's will, and the understanding of the husband is also the wife's understanding. The love of each is to will and to think exactly as the other does—that is, mutually and reciprocally. In this way, they are joined into one. This is a true and actual union, for the wife's will enters into the husband's understanding, and the husband's understanding enters into the wife's will. This is especially true when they look into one another's faces; for, as has been said many times before, in the heavens there is a constant sharing of thoughts and affections, particularly between a husband and wife, because they love each other.

**370.** I have been told by the angels that the more a married couple is so joined, the more they experience marriage love, and to that same extent, they also grow in intelligence, wisdom, and happiness. This is because **Divine truth** and **Divine good**—the sources of all intelligence, wisdom, and happiness—flow primarily into marriage love. Consequently, marriage love, since it is a union of good and truth, is the very foundation for <term>Divine influx<note>The spiritual process by which life, wisdom, and love flow from the Divine into the human soul.</note></term>. 

Because this love is a union of the **understanding** and the **will**, it is also a union of truth and good. The understanding receives Divine truth and is formed by it, while the will receives Divine good and is formed by it. To a person, whatever they "will" or desire is their "good," and whatever they "understand" or think is their "truth." Therefore, it is the same thing whether you call it a union of understanding and will or a union of truth and good. This union of truth and good is what makes an angel, and creates their intelligence, wisdom, and happiness. An angel is truly an angel only insofar as the "good" within them is joined with "truth," and truth with good—or, to put it another way, as much as their love is joined with their faith.

**371.** The Divine power that goes out from the Lord flows most directly into marriage love because that love descends from the union of good and truth. As has been said, the union of understanding and will is the same as the union of good and truth. This union of good and truth begins in the Lord's Divine love toward everyone in heaven and on earth. From Divine love, **Divine good** flows forth, and this good is received by angels and people through Divine truths. 

Because truth is the only "vessel" capable of holding good, no one can receive anything from the Lord or from heaven unless they live in truths. Therefore, to the exact extent that the truths in a person are joined to good, that person is joined to the Lord and to heaven. This is the very origin of marriage love, and for this reason, that love is the primary foundation for Divine influx. This shows why the union of good and truth in heaven is called the **heavenly marriage**, and why <term>the Word<note>Swedenborg's term for the Bible, specifically its inner spiritual meaning.</note></term> compares heaven to a marriage, and calls it a marriage; and the

**380.** The love of **dominion** <note>The desire to rule over or control another person.</note> of one over the other entirely takes away marriage love and its heavenly delight, for as has been said above, marriage love and its delight consists in the will of the one being that of the other, mutually and reciprocally. This is destroyed by love of dominion in marriage, since he that domineers wishes his will alone to be in the other, and nothing of the other's will to be reciprocally in himself, which destroys all mutuality, and thus all sharing of any love and its delight one with the other. And yet this sharing and consequent conjunction are the interior delight itself that is called **blessedness** in marriage. This blessedness, with everything that is heavenly and spiritual in marriage love, is so completely extinguished by love of dominion as to destroy even all knowledge of it; and if that love were referred to it would be held in such contempt that any mention of blessedness from that source would excite either laughter or anger. [2.] When one wills or loves what the other wills or loves each has freedom, since all freedom is from love; but where there is dominion no one has freedom; one is a servant, and the other who rules is also a servant, for he is led as a servant by the lust of domineering.

Because of this difference, heaven may be the portion of one and hell the portion of the other.

This is why spouses who are in marriage love enjoy heavenly delights together; these delights appear to their minds almost like the playful sports of innocence among little children. -># MARRIAGES IN HEAVEN<-

On earth, marriages occur because they involve both the spirit and the physical flesh. Since there are no physical marriages in heaven, the partners are not called "husband" and "wife." Instead, based on the angelic concept of two minds becoming one, each partner refers to the other by a name that expresses their mutual belonging. This explains how we should understand the Lord’s words in the Gospel of Luke regarding "marrying and giving in marriage" (Luke 20:35, 36) <note>In this Bible passage, Jesus explains that those in the resurrection neither marry nor are given in marriage, which Swedenborg interprets here not as the absence of companionship, but as the absence of earthly, physical procreation.</note>.

**383.** I have also been permitted to see how marriages are formed in the heavens. Just as everywhere in heaven those who are alike are united and those who are unlike are separated, every angelic society consists of people who share a similar character. These compatible spirits are brought together not by their own efforts, but by the Lord (as noted previously in sections 41, 43, and 44). In this same way, partners whose minds can truly be joined as one are drawn toward each other. At the very first sight, they feel a deep, internal love for one another and recognize themselves as a destined pair, subsequently entering into marriage. For this reason, all marriages in heaven are initiated by the Lord alone. They also hold marriage feasts, which are attended by many guests, though the festivities vary between different societies.

**384.** Earthly marriages are considered most holy in the sight of the angels because they are **seminaries** <term>Seminaries: Here used in the classical sense of a "nursery" or "seedbed" where the human race—and eventually the population of heaven—is grown.</term> of the human race. Since all angels were originally part of the human race, marriage is the source of heaven itself. Furthermore, these marriages have a spiritual origin—the union of **good and truth**—and the Lord’s Divine influence flows specifically into **marriage love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis." This refers to a holy, spiritual love between spouses that transcends mere physical attraction.</note>. On the other hand, the angels view adultery as profane because it is the direct opposite of marriage love. While the angels see marriage as the union of good and truth (which is heaven), they see adultery as the union of what is false and what is evil (which is hell). If angels even hear adultery mentioned, they turn away in distress. This is why heaven is closed off to a person who commits adultery for the sake of pleasure; once heaven is shut, that person no longer acknowledges the Divine or any aspect of the church's faith.<sup>1</sup> I have been allowed to perceive that everyone in hell is hostile to marriage love; I felt this from the atmosphere exhaling from hell, which acted as a constant pressure to dissolve and violate marriages. **391.** As all the societies in the heavens are distinct in accordance with their goods (as said above, n. 41, seq.) so they are distinct in accordance with their uses, goods being goods in act, that is, goods of charity which are uses. There are other societies that teach the **simple good** <note>The "simple good" refers to individuals from the Christian world who lived moral lives and possessed a good heart but lacked deep intellectual or theological understanding.</note> from the Christian world, and lead them into the way to heaven; there are others that do the same for the various Gentile nations.

There are some who look after spirits in the **lower earth** <term>lower earth: In this theology, a region in the spiritual world where individuals are prepared for heaven by being gradually cleared of worldly or incorrect ideas.</term>; and others who attend to spirits in the hells, restraining them from tormenting each other beyond certain set limits. They work to inspire people with good affections, doing so only as much as the person is willing to receive them in freedom. By these means, they guide the actions or works of humanity by removing, as far as possible, evil intentions. When angels are with people, they dwell, as it were, within the person's own feelings. They are close to a person only to the degree that the person lives in a way that is good and true; they are distant from those whose lives are far removed from goodness. <gloss>1</gloss> 

However, all these duties of the angels are actually the work of the Lord performed through them; for the angels carry them out from the Lord and not from themselves. For this reason, in the **Word** <term>the Word: The Sacred Scripture or Bible, which the author views as having multiple layers of meaning.</term>, when understood in its **internal sense** <note>Swedenborg teaches that the Bible contains a "spiritual sense" hidden beneath the literal text, which describes the inner workings of the soul and the Divine.</note>, "angels" do not refer to individual beings, but to something belonging to the Lord Himself. It is for this same reason that angels are sometimes called "gods" in the Bible. <gloss>2</gloss>

**392.** These duties of the angels are their general roles, but every single angel has their own specific task. Every "general use" is made up of countless smaller functions—which we might call intermediate, ministering, or supporting uses. All of these are organized and ranked according to **Divine order** <term>Divine order: The perfect, logical structure through which God governs the universe, where every part serves the whole.</term>. Taken together, they constitute and perfect the general use, which is the common good of all.

# EMPLOYMENTS IN HEAVEN.

->HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

**393.** Those in heaven who manage church-related matters are the ones who, during their time on earth, loved **the Word** <term>the Word: The Sacred Scripture or Bible, viewed here as containing deep, hidden layers of spiritual wisdom.</term> and searched it for truths. They did this not for fame or money, but to improve their own lives and the lives of others. In heaven, these people are filled with light and wisdom according to how much they desire to be helpful. They receive this wisdom from the spiritual version of **the Word**, which differs from the physical Bible we know on earth (as mentioned in section 259). These individuals serve as preachers; following the divine order, those who are the most enlightened and wise hold the higher positions.

[2.] Those who manage civil affairs are the ones who, while on earth, loved their country and prioritized the public good over their own interests, acting with justice and integrity. To the extent that these people studied the laws of justice out of a desire to help, they are given the ability to perform similar roles in heaven. They serve in positions that match their intelligence, which is always equal to their love for serving the community.

[3.] Furthermore, there are more jobs, services, and occupations in heaven than can be listed; the world has very few by comparison. No matter the job, everyone finds delight in their work because it comes from a **love of use** <term>love of use: The selfless desire to perform actions that are beneficial to others or to society as a whole.</term>, never from a love of self or money. Since all the necessities of life are provided for free, there is no need to work for a paycheck. They are given housing, clothing, and food at no cost. It is clear, then, that those who loved themselves and the world more than being helpful have no place in heaven; a person’s true love or inner motivation remains with them forever after death (as mentioned in section 363).

**394.** In heaven, everyone is assigned a role based on **correspondence** <term>correspondence: The fundamental relationship between the spiritual world and the natural world, where spiritual realities are reflected in physical forms or activities.</term>. This is not based on the specific job itself, but on the *use* or purpose that the job serves. When someone in heaven enters a role that corresponds to their inner nature, their life feels familiar, as if they were still on earth. This is because the spiritual and natural worlds are linked through these correspondences. The main difference is that the person experiences a deeper, more internal joy, as they have entered into a spiritual life that is more open to receiving heavenly happiness.

## XLII.

### HEAVENLY JOY AND HAPPINESS.

**395.** Hardly anyone today truly understands what heaven is or what "heavenly joy" entails. Most people who have thought about it have had such a vague and crude idea that it amounts to almost nothing. Through my interactions with spirits who have recently arrived in the afterlife from our world, I have been able to learn exactly what they imagined heaven to be. When these spirits are left to their own thoughts—as if they were still living in the world—they think exactly as they did before. This general ignorance exists because people usually base their opinions of joy on the outward pleasures of the **natural man** <term>natural man: The part of a person focused on the physical world, sensory experiences, and self-interest.</term>. They do not understand the **inner or spiritual man** <term>spiritual man: The internal part of a human being that is capable of receiving love and wisdom from the Divine.</term>, nor do they understand the nature of that inner self's happiness and blessedness. Even if someone who experiences spiritual joy tried to describe it to them, they would have no way to grasp it. Because the concept is so foreign to their experience, they would simply reject it. 

Yet, anyone can logically understand that when a person leaves their outer, physical body behind, they enter into their inner, spiritual self. Therefore, heavenly joy must be internal and spiritual, not external and physical. Because it is internal, it is more pure and intense, affecting the deepest parts of the soul. From this, we can conclude that a person's joy after death is simply a continuation of whatever joy their spirit felt while they were alive. Physical pleasures—which we might call "delights of the flesh"—are not heavenly by comparison. Whatever is in a person's spirit stays with them after death, because they then live as a **man-spirit** <term>man-spirit: The Swedenborgian term for a person who has died and is now living in the spiritual world in a complete, human-shaped spiritual body.</term>.

**396.** All joy and delight flow from love; whatever a person loves, they find delightful. There is no other source for happiness. From this, it follows that the nature of a person's joy depends entirely on the nature of their love. Physical or "fleshly" pleasures all flow from a **love of self** and a **love of the world**; consequently, these are essentially cravings and their satisfactions. In contrast, the joys of the soul or spirit all flow from **love for the Lord** <note>original: "amor in Dominum" — specifically, a love directed toward the Divine.</note> and **love toward the neighbor**. These are holy and unselfish affections...

It argues that because our inner spirit survives death, our experience of heaven is determined by the quality of the loves we cultivated during our physical life.</summary>

### HEAVENLY JOY AND HAPPINESS.

...physical pleasures are replaced by a deep affection **for good and truth and interior satisfactions.** These heavenly loves, along with the joy they bring, flow into a person from the Lord via an "inner way"—meaning they descend from a higher spiritual level and move into the innermost parts of the mind. In contrast, the loves of the world and their pleasures flow in from the body and the surrounding world via an "external way"—meaning they enter from below and affect only the outer senses. 

Therefore, to the degree that a person receives these two heavenly loves (love for the Lord and love for others), their **interiors** <term>interiors: The deeper levels of the human mind and soul that are capable of connecting with spiritual reality.</term> are opened. These inner levels belong to the soul or spirit and naturally look upward toward heaven. However, to the degree that a person focuses only on the loves of the world, their **exteriors** <term>exteriors: The outer layers of consciousness focused on physical survival, social status, and sensory gratification.</term> are opened, and they look away from heaven toward the physical world. Since all joy is a result of what a person loves, the delights of heaven flow into those whose inner minds are open, while the delights of the world remain only on the surface.

**397.** Heaven, in its very essence, is so filled with joy that it can be described as nothing other than pure blessedness and delight. This is because the **Divine Good** <note>In this context, "Good" refers to the active energy of love and kindness that flows from the Divine.</note> flowing from the Lord’s love is what creates heaven, both as a whole and within every individual angel. The Divine love is a constant, powerful longing for the salvation and happiness of everyone, stemming from the deepest core of being. Therefore, to speak of "heaven" or to speak of "heavenly joy" is essentially to speak of the same thing.

**398.** The joys of heaven are beyond description and too many to count. However, a person who finds pleasure only in the body or the flesh cannot understand—or even believe in—a single one of these countless spiritual joys. As mentioned before, their inner self is looking in the wrong direction: away from heaven and toward the world. A person who is entirely focused on physical pleasure, or what is effectively the same thing, **self-love and the love of worldly gain**, can only perceive joy in terms of status, profit, and sensory gratification. 

These worldly desires so thoroughly stifle and "suffocate" the inner joys of heaven that the person loses all capacity to believe they even exist. Such a person is usually shocked to hear that there are any joys other than those of status and wealth. They are even more surprised to learn that the joys of heaven, which replace these worldly ones, are so vast and profound that they cannot even be compared to physical pleasures. This fundamental misunderstanding is why so few people truly know what heavenly joy is.

Such sharing goes forth from the two **loves of heaven**, which are, as has been said, **love to the Lord** and **love towards the neighbor**; and to share their delights is the very nature of these loves. 

Love to the Lord is such because it is a love of sharing every thing it has with all, since it wills the happiness of all. There is a like love in every one of those who love the Lord, because the Lord is in them; and from this comes the mutual sharing of the delights of angels with one another. Love towards the neighbor is the same, as will be seen in what follows. All this shows that it is the nature of these loves to share their delights. 

It is otherwise with the **loves of self** and **of the world.** The love of self takes away from others and robs others of all delight, and directs it to itself, for it wishes well to itself alone; while the love of the world wishes to have as its own what belongs to the neighbor. Therefore these loves are destructive of the delights of others; or if there is any disposition to share, it is for the sake of themselves and not others. Thus in respect to others it is the nature of these loves not to share but to take away, except so far as the delights of others have some relation to self. 

That the loves of self and of the world, when they rule, are such I have often been permitted to perceive by living experience. Whenever the spirits that were in these loves during their life as men in the world drew near, my delight receded and vanished; and I was told that at the mere approach of such to any **heavenly society** <term>heavenly society: A community of angels grouped together by their shared character and specific type of love.</term> the delight of those in the society diminished just in the degree of their proximity; and what is wonderful, the evil spirits are then in their delight. All this indicates the state of the spirit of such a man while he is in the body, since it is the same as it is after it is separated from the body, namely, that it longs for or **lusts** <note>original: "cupiditas." In this context, it refers to a disordered, selfish craving that consumes the person's focus.</note> after the delights or goods of another, and finds delight so far as it secures them. All this makes clear that the loves of self and of the world tend to destroy the joys of heaven, and are thus direct opposites of heavenly loves, which desire to share.

The specific functions that each of our senses perform are well-known to those who study them, and even more so to those who understand **correspondences** <term>correspondences: the spiritual principle that physical things in the world reflect and respond to spiritual realities</term>. The sense of sight brings delight because of the service it provides to the **understanding** <term>understanding: the faculty of the mind that perceives truth and spiritual light</term>, which is the "inner sight" of the soul. These various pleasures exist within our sensory organs because of an **influx** <term>influx: the constant flow of life and energy from the spiritual world into the physical world</term> from heaven, where every joy is tied to a specific use and exists in proportion to that use.

Such a life would not be an active one, but a stagnant one that would eventually numb all the vital powers of the soul. Everyone should understand that there can be no happiness in life without activity; rest from such activity is meant only for recreation, so that a person can return to their active life with more energy. These spirits were then shown many proofs that the life of an angel consists in performing the good works of **charity** <term>charity: the act of doing what is good and just out of love for others</term>, which are called **uses** <term>uses: meaningful services or functions that benefit the community or the Lord’s kingdom</term>. Angels find all their happiness within these uses, because of these uses, and in accordance with the quality of those uses. To those who held the opinion that heavenly joy is simply sitting in idleness and breathing in eternal joy, a direct perception of what such a life is actually like was granted, so they might feel ashamed of the idea. They saw that such a life is actually profoundly sad, and that since all joy would vanish, they would very quickly feel only disgust for it.
