**405.** Almost all who enter the other life think that hell is the same to every one, and heaven the same; and yet in both there are infinite varieties and diversities, and in no case is hell or heaven wholly the same to one as to another; as it is impossible that any one man, spirit, or angel should ever be wholly like another even as to the face. At my mere thought of two being just alike or equal the angels expressed horror, saying that every one thing is formed out of the **harmonious concurrence** <term>harmonious concurrence: the way diverse and different parts fit together perfectly to create a single, unified whole</term> of many things, and that the one thing is such as that concurrence is; and that it is thus that a whole society in heaven becomes a one, and that all the societies of heaven together become a one, and this from the Lord alone by means of love.¹ **Uses** in the heavens are likewise in all variety and diversity, and in no case is the use of one wholly the same as and identical with the use of another; so neither is the happiness of one the same as and identical with the happiness of another. Furthermore, the delights of each use are innumerable, and these innumerable delights are likewise various, and yet conjoined in such order that they mutually regard each other, like the uses of each member, organ, and **viscus** <term>viscus: an internal organ of the body, such as the heart or lungs</term>, in the body, and still more like the uses of each vessel and fibre in each member, organ, and viscus; each and all of which are so affiliated as to have regard to another's good in their own good, and thus each in all, and all in each. From this universal and individual aspect they act as one.

# HEAVENLY JOY AND HAPPINESS.

**406.** I have talked at times with spirits <note>In this context, spirits refers to people who have recently died and are in the "world of spirits," an intermediate state of transition before entering heaven or hell.</note> that had recently come from the world about the state of eternal life. I told them that it is important to know who the **Lord** <note>original: "Dominus"; Swedenborg uses this term to refer specifically to Jesus Christ as the single God of heaven and earth.</note> of the kingdom is, and what kind and what form of government it has. Just as nothing is more important for those entering a new kingdom in the physical world than to know who the king is, what the government is like, and other details about the realm, so it is of even greater consequence in this kingdom where they are to live for eternity.

Therefore, they should know that it is the Lord who governs both heaven and the universe, for He who governs one must govern the other. Thus, the kingdom in which they now find themselves belongs to the Lord. The laws of this kingdom are eternal truths, all of which rest upon the law that the Lord must be loved above all things and the neighbor as themselves; and even more than this—if they wish to be like the angels, they must love the neighbor **more than themselves.**

On hearing this, they could make no reply, because although they had heard similar ideas during their physical life, they had not truly believed them. They wondered how there could be such love in heaven, and how it could be possible for anyone to love his neighbor more than himself. But they were told that every "good" <note>Here, "good" refers to a person’s capacity for love and kindness.</note> increases immeasurably in the other life. While people cannot go further in the life of the body than to love the neighbor as themselves—because they are immersed in concerns of the physical body—once those bodily concerns are set aside, their love becomes more pure. It eventually becomes **angelic love**, which is to love the neighbor more than oneself.

For in the heavens, there is joy in doing good to another, but no joy in doing good to oneself unless it is with the goal of that good eventually benefiting someone else. This is what it means to love the neighbor more than oneself. They were told that the possibility of such love is shown even in the world: in the **marriage love** <term>marriage love: often called "conjugial love" in older translations; it is the spiritual union of two people whose souls are joined in mutual love and wisdom</term> of those who have faced death to protect a consort <note>consort: a spouse or marriage partner.</note> from injury; in the love of parents for their children, such as a mother preferring to go hungry rather than see her child go hungry; in sincere friendship, where one friend will face danger for another; and even in the polite or pretended friendship of the world that tries to mimic the real thing by offering the best things to others and speaking well of them. Finally, it is seen in the very nature of love, which finds its joy in serving others, not for its own sake but for theirs.

However, all of this was incomprehensible to those who loved themselves more than—

...others, and in the life of the body had been greedy of gain; still more to the avaricious. <note>This continues a list of those who find the selflessness of heaven difficult to understand, specifically those who were obsessed with profit or material wealth during their earthly lives.</note>

**407.** There was one who, in the life of the body, had exercised power over others and had retained the desire to rule even in the next life. However, he was told that he was now in another kingdom, which is eternal, and that his earthly rule had perished. He was informed that he was now in a place where no one is esteemed except in accordance with their **goodness and truth** <term>Goodness and truth: These are the two fundamental components of spiritual life in this theology—goodness relates to the will and love, while truth relates to the intellect and wisdom.</term>, and according to that measure of the Lord's **mercy** <note>original: "misericordia"</note> which he enjoyed because of how he lived in the world. 

He was also told that the same principle applies in this kingdom as on earth, where men are esteemed for their wealth and for their favor with the prince; however, "wealth" here is goodness and truth, and "favor with the prince" is the mercy bestowed on a person by the **Lord** <note>Swedenborg consistently uses "the Lord" (Dominus) to refer to Jesus Christ as the God of heaven.</note> in accordance with his life in the world. Any wish to rule otherwise would make him a rebel, since he is now in another's kingdom. Upon hearing these things, he was ashamed.

**408.** I have talked with spirits who believed heaven and heavenly joy consisted in being "great." Such spirits were told that in heaven, he that is **least** is **greatest**. He is called "least" who has, and wishes to have, no power or wisdom from himself, but only from the Lord. Because the one who is "least" in that sense has the greatest happiness, it follows that they are the "greatest"; for by relying on the Lord, they possess all power and excel all others in wisdom. 

What does it mean to be the greatest, if not to be the most happy? For to be the most happy is what the powerful seek through power and the rich seek through riches. It was further said that heaven does not consist in a desire to be "least" for the specific purpose of being "greatest," for that would be a hidden longing for status; rather, it consists in desiring from the heart the good of others more than one's own, and in serving others for the sake of their happiness—not for reward, but out of love.

**409.** Heavenly joy itself, as it is in its essence, cannot be described. This is because it exists in the **inmost** <note>original: "intimis"; referring to the deepest levels of human consciousness and the soul's connection to the Divine.</note> of the life of angels and, from there, in every single one of their thoughts and affections, and subsequently in every detail of their speech and action. It is as if the **interiors** <term>Interiors: The internal spiritual faculties of a person which are fully opened only after the death of the physical body.</term> were fully opened and unloosed to receive delight and blessedness, which are distributed to every tiny fibre and thus throughout the whole person. Thus, the perception and sensation of this joy cannot be described, for that which starts from the very core flows into every detail derived from that core, always increasing as it moves toward the exterior parts of the being. Good spirits who are not yet in that joy—because they have not yet been raised...

...up into heaven, when they receive a sense of that joy from an angel from the sphere of his love, are filled with such delight that they come as it were into a delicious trance. This sometimes happens with those who desire to know what heavenly joy is.

**410.** When certain spirits wished to know what heavenly joy is, they were allowed to feel it to such a degree that they could no longer bear it; and yet it was not even true angelic joy. It was scarcely in the least degree angelic—as I was permitted to perceive by sharing the experience—and was so slight as to be almost cold by comparison. Nevertheless, they called it "most heavenly" because, to them, it was an inmost joy. From this it was evident not only that there are degrees of the joys of heaven, but also that the deepest joy of one person scarcely reaches the level of the middle or outermost joy of another. It also showed that when any person receives their own highest possible joy, they are in their "heavenly joy," and they cannot endure anything even more internal, for such an intense joy would become painful to them. <note>Swedenborg suggests that "heaven" is not a uniform experience, but is tailored to the specific capacity of each individual to feel love and wisdom.</note>

**411.** Certain spirits, who were not evil, fell into a state of stillness like sleep <term>Quiescence: A state of rest or inactivity where the external senses are calmed so the inner mind can be more perceptive.</term>. In this state, the inner levels of their minds were taken up into heaven; even before their inner selves are fully opened, spirits can be taken into heaven to be taught about the happiness of those who live there. I saw them in this peaceful state for about half an hour, and afterward, they returned to their external state and to a memory of what they had seen. 

They said that they had been among the angels in heaven and had seen and perceived amazing things, all of which were resplendent as if made of gold, silver, and precious stones, appearing in exquisite forms and wonderful variety. They also noted that angels are not delighted by these outward objects themselves, but by what they represented—which were Divine, beyond words, and full of infinite wisdom. This spiritual meaning was the source of their joy. They mentioned innumerable other things that could not be described in human language—not even a ten-thousandth part—nor could they even be understood by thoughts that are based on material things.

**412.** Scarcely anyone who enters the afterlife knows the nature of heavenly bliss and happiness, because they do not know what internal joy is. They base their understanding of joy solely on the pleasures of the body and the world. Because of this ignorance, they suppose that if a joy is not worldly, it must be nothing at all; in fact, bodily and worldly joys are of no account in comparison. In order, therefore, that well-intentioned people who do not know what heavenly joy is may come to realize it, they are...

**413.** But that I might learn the nature of heaven and heavenly joy I have frequently and for a long time been permitted by the Lord to perceive the delights of heavenly joys; but while I have been enabled to know by living experience what they are I am not at all able to describe them. Nevertheless, that some idea of them may be formed, something shall be said about them. Heavenly joy is an affection <note>In this context, "affection" refers to a deep, flowing state of love or emotion rather than a simple liking.</note> of innumerable delights and joys, which together present something general, and in this general, that is, this general affection, are harmonies of innumerable affections that come to perception obscurely, and not distinctly, because the perception is most general. Nevertheless I was permitted to perceive that there are innumerable things in it, in such order as cannot be at all described, those innumerable things being such as flow from the order of heaven. Such is the order in every particular of the affection even to the least, and these particulars are presented and perceived only as a most general whole, in accordance with the capacity of him who is the subject.

In a word, each general affection contains infinite joys arranged in a most orderly form, with nothing therein that is not living, and actuating all of them from the inmosts; for heavenly joys go forth from inmosts. I perceived also that the joy and satisfaction came as from the heart, diffusing most softly through all the inmost fibres, and from these into the bundles of fibres, with such an inmost sense of delight that the fibre seemed to be nothing but joy and satisfaction, and everything perceptive and sensitive therefrom seemed in like manner to be alive with happiness. <note>Swedenborg often uses anatomical language—like "fibers"—to describe how spiritual life flows into the human form.</note> Compared with these joys the joy of bodily pleasures is like a gross and pungent dust compared with a pure and most gentle aura. I have noticed that when I wished to transfer all my delight to another, a more interior and fuller delight continually flowed in in its place, and the more I wished this, the more it flowed in; and this, I perceived, was from the Lord.

**414.** Those who live in heaven are continually progressing toward the springtime of life. Women who have died old and worn out by age—if they have lived in faith in the Lord, in charity toward their neighbor, and in a happy marriage love <term>Marriage love: Also known as "conjugial love," this refers to a sacred, spiritual union of souls that Swedenborg describes as the highest form of human affection.</term> with a husband—move more and more into the flower of youth and early womanhood as the years pass. They attain a beauty that transcends any concept of beauty ever seen on earth. It is goodness and charity that forms and expresses its own likeness in them, causing the joy and beauty of that love to shine forth from every tiny detail of the face, until they become forms of charity itself. 

Some who have witnessed this were struck with amazement. In this form of charity seen vividly in heaven, it is charity itself that both creates the form and is the form; in such a way, the entire angel, and especially the face, is a personification of charity. This is both clearly seen and felt. When this form is beheld, it is a beauty beyond words, affecting the very inmost life of the mind with a sense of love. In a word, growing old in heaven is growing young. Those who have lived in love to the Lord and in charity toward their neighbor become such beauties in the next life. All angels are such forms in endless variety, and of these, heaven is composed.

**416.** The immensity of the Lord's heaven is also shown by the fact that all children—whether born within the church or outside of it—are adopted by the Lord and become angels. **417.** Furthermore, the immensity of the Lord's heaven can be seen from the fact that all the planets visible to the eye in our solar system are "earths" <note>Swedenborg uses the term "earths" to describe any inhabited planet.</note>, and beyond these, there are innumerable earths in the whole universe, all full of inhabitants. [A per]son ought to know from many things that he does know that there are many earths inhabited by men; for it may be reasonably inferred that immense bodies like the planets, some of which exceed this earth in magnitude, are not empty masses created merely to be borne through space around the sun, and to shine with their scanty light for the benefit of a single earth, but must have a more important use. He that believes, as any one must believe, that the **Divine** created the universe for no other end than that the human race might exist, and heaven therefrom—for the human race is a <term>seminary of heaven</term><note>A "seminary" here refers to a seedbed or nursery; Swedenborg views the physical world as the place where the "seeds" of future angels are grown and prepared.</note>—must needs believe that wherever there is an earth there are men. 

That the planets visible to us, because they are within the limits of our solar system, are earths is evident from their being bodies of earthy matters, which is known from their reflecting the sun's light, and from their not appearing, when viewed through telescopes, like stars, sparkling with flame, but like earths varied with darker portions; also from their passing like our earth around the sun and following in the path of the zodiac, thus making years and seasons of the year, spring, summer, autumn, and winter, also revolving on their axes like our earth, making days and times of the day, morning, mid-day, evening, and night; also from some of them having moons, called *satellites*, that revolve around their earth at stated times, as the moon does around ours; while the planet Saturn, being at a greater distance from the sun, has also a large luminous belt which gives much light, though reflected, to that earth. Who that knows all this and thinks rationally can ever say that the planets are empty bodies? 

Moreover, I have said to spirits that man might believe that there are more earths in the universe than one, from the fact that the starry heaven is so immense, and the stars there so innumerable, and each of them in its place or in its system a sun, resembling our sun, although of a different magnitude. Any one who duly weighs the subject must conclude that such an immense whole must needs be a means to an end that is the final end of creation; and this end must be a heavenly kingdom in which the **Divine** may dwell with angels and men. For the visible universe or the heaven illumined by stars so numberless, which are so many suns, must be simply a means for the existence of earths with men upon them from whom the heavenly kingdom is derived. 

From all this a rational man must needs conclude that so immense a means to so great an end could not have been provided merely for the human race on a single earth. What would this be for a **Divine** that is infinite, to which thousands and even myriads of earths, all of them full of inhabitants, would be little and scarcely anything? There are spirits whose sole pursuit is the acquisition of knowledges, because their delight is in this alone; and for this reason they are permitted to wander about, and even to pass out of our solar system into others, in acquiring knowledge. These spirits, who are from the planet **Mercury**, have told me that there are earths with men upon them not only in this solar system but also beyond it in the starry heaven in immense numbers.

# THE WORLD OF SPIRITS,

## *AND THE STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.*

### XLIV.

### WHAT THE WORLD OF SPIRITS IS.

**421.** The world of spirits is not heaven, nor is it hell, but it is the intermediate place or state between the two; for it is the place that a person first enters after death. From here, after a suitable length of time, they are either raised up into heaven or cast down into hell, in accordance with the life they acquired while living in the world.

**422.** The world of spirits is both an intermediate place between heaven and hell and an intermediate state for the human being after death. It has been shown to me not only that it is an intermediate place—having the hells below it and the heavens above it—but also that it is an intermediate state, since as long as a person is there, they are not yet fully in heaven or in hell. 

The "state of heaven" in a human spirit is the **conjunction** <term>Conjunction: A spiritual union or marriage of two different elements. Swedenborg uses this to describe how our thoughts and our intentions must eventually become one.</term> of **good and truth** within them; conversely, the "state of hell" is the conjunction of **evil and falsity** <note>In this context, "falsity" refers to false ideas or delusions that a person uses to justify selfish or harmful behavior.</note> within them. Whenever goodness in a human spirit is joined to truth, that person enters heaven, because that union, as just stated, is heaven within them. But whenever evil in a human spirit is joined with falsity, they enter hell, because that union is hell within them. This joining is brought about in the world of spirits while the person is in this intermediate state. It is the same thing whether you call it the conjunction of the **understanding and the will**, or the conjunction of good and truth.

**423.** Let us first say something about the conjunction of the understanding and the will, and how it is essentially the same as the conjunction of good and truth, as this is the union that is completed in the world of spirits. Every human being has an understanding and a will. The understanding receives truths and is shaped by them, and the will receives "goods" <gloss>Inherent qualities of love, kindness, and altruistic intent</gloss> and is shaped by them. Therefore, whatever a person understands and thinks from their understanding, they call "true," and whatever a person wills

**430.** With every man there are two gates; one that leads to hell and that is open to evils and their **falsities** <term>Falsities: In this spiritual context, these are not just simple lies, but systemic errors or distorted beliefs that support a person's selfish desires.</term>; while the other leads to heaven and is open to goods and their truths. Thus there are two ways that lead to the **rational mind** <term>Rational Mind: The faculty of the human soul that sits between the spiritual and natural worlds, acting as the decision-maker for an individual's character.</term> of man; a higher or internal way through which good and truth from the Lord enter, and a lower or external way through which evil and falsity enter from hell. The rational mind itself is at the middle point to which the ways tend. Consequently, so far as light from heaven is admitted man is rational; but so far as it is not admitted he is not rational, however rational he may seem to himself to be. 

This has been said to make known the nature of the **correspondence** <term>Correspondence: The spiritual law that every physical or mental state has a direct, matching reality in the spiritual world.</term> of man with heaven and with hell. While man’s rational mind is being formed it corresponds to the world of spirits, what is above it corresponding to heaven and what is below it to hell. With those preparing for heaven the regions above the rational mind are opened, but those below are closed to the **influx** <term>Influx: The constant spiritual "flow" of life, thought, and motivation from the spiritual world into the human mind.</term> of evil and falsity; while with those preparing for hell the parts below it are opened, and the parts above it are closed to the influx of good and truth. 

Thus the latter can look only to what is below themselves, that is, to hell; while the former can look only to what is above themselves, that is, to heaven. To look above themselves is to look to the Lord, because He is the common centre to which all things of heaven look; while to look below themselves is to look backwards from the Lord to the opposite centre, to which all things of hell look and tend (see above, n. 123, 124).

# HEAVEN AND HELL.

### XLV.

### IN REGARD TO THE INTERNAL SELF, EVERY PERSON IS A SPIRIT.

**432.** Anyone who carefully considers the matter can see that because the body is material, it is not the physical body that thinks, but the soul, which is spiritual. The human soul—the immortality of which many authors have discussed—is actually the person's spirit; for the spirit is immortal in every respect. It is the spirit that thinks within the body, for the spirit is of a spiritual nature, and that which is spiritual is capable of receiving spiritual things and living in a spiritual way (which means to think and to exercise the will). 

Consequently, all **rational life** <term>Rational Life: The faculty of the human soul that allows for conscious thought, reasoning, and the ability to make moral choices.</term> that appears in the body belongs to the soul, and none of it belongs to the body. As previously stated, the body is material; this material nature is a property of the physical body that is added—and seemingly joined—to the spirit so that the human spirit can live and perform useful actions in the **natural world** <note>The "natural world" refers to our physical, material universe.</note>. All things in this physical world are material and, in themselves, possess no life. Since only that which is spiritual possesses life, it is clear that the human spirit is the only thing in a person that truly lives, while the body merely serves it, just as a tool serves a living, moving force. It is common to say that an instrument acts, moves, or strikes; but to believe that these are the actions of the tool itself, rather than the person acting through the tool, is a **fallacy** <note>original: "fallacy" — a mistaken belief or a failure in reasoning.</note>.

**433.** Since everything in the body that lives—and everything that acts and feels because of that life—belongs exclusively to the spirit and not the body, it follows that the spirit is the person themselves. Or, to put it another way, a person viewed in their true essence is a spirit in human form. This is because everything that lives and feels within a person belongs to their spirit; from head to toe, every part of a person lives and feels. 

As a result, when the body is separated from its spirit (the event we call death), the person continues to be a person and continues to live. I have heard from heaven that some who die continue to think even while they are lying on the **bier** <note>original: "bier" — a stand on which a corpse or coffin is placed before burial.</note>, before they are **resuscitated** <note>original: "resuscitated" — here meaning the spiritual awakening or "rising again" that occurs shortly after physical death.</note>. Even in their cold body, they do not realize they are no longer physically alive, except for the fact that they find they are unable to move even the smallest particle of the body's matter.

**439.** To make clear that man, in respect to his **interiors** <term>Interiors: The internal spiritual components of a person—their mind, will, and soul—which exist within the physical body.</term>, is a spirit, I will relate from experience what happens when a person is withdrawn from the body, and what it is to be carried away by the spirit to another place.

**440.** First, as to **withdrawal from the body**, it happens thus: A person is brought into a certain state that is midway between sleeping and waking, and when in that state he seems to himself to be wide awake; all the senses are as perfectly awake as in the completest bodily wakefulness—not only the sight and the hearing, but what is wonderful, the sense of touch also, which is then more exquisite than is ever possible when the body is awake. In this state spirits and angels have been seen to the very life, and have been heard, and what is wonderful have been touched, with almost nothing of the physical body intervening. This is the state that is called "being withdrawn from the body" and not knowing whether one is in the body or out of it. I have been admitted into this state only three or four times, that I might learn what it is, and might know that spirits and angels enjoy every sense, and that man does also in respect to his spirit when he is withdrawn from the body.

**441.** As to being **carried away by the spirit** <note>A phenomenon where the consciousness is transported to a distant location in the spiritual world while the physical body remains stationary.</note> to another place, I have been shown by living experience what it is, and how it is done, but only two or three times. I will relate a single instance. Walking through the streets of a city and through fields, talking at the same time with spirits, I seemed to myself to be fully awake, and in possession of my usual sight. Thus I walked on knowing what I was doing, and all the while with clear vision, seeing groves, rivers, palaces, houses, men, and other objects. ### XLVI.

->THE **RESUSCITATION** <term>Resuscitation: Not a medical reviving of the physical body, but the process of the soul being "awakened" or "raised up" into the spiritual world after the body dies.</term> OF MAN FROM THE DEAD AND HIS ENTRANCE INTO ETERNAL LIFE.<-

**445.** When the body is no longer able to perform the bodily functions in the **natural world** <term>Natural world: The physical, material universe we inhabit during our earthly lives.</term> that correspond to the spirit's thoughts and affections, which the spirit has from the **spiritual world** <term>Spiritual world: The reality beyond the physical, where spirits and angels dwell and where thoughts and feelings take on visible form.</term>, man is said to die. This takes place when the respiration of the lungs and the beatings of the heart cease. But the man does not die; he is merely separated from the bodily part that was of use to him in the world, while the man himself continues to live. # RESUSCITATION OF MAN FROM THE DEAD.

The death of man is merely his passing from one world into another. And this is why in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures, or the Bible.</note> in its internal sense “death” signifies resurrection and continuation of life.¹

**446.** There is an inmost communication of the spirit with the breathing and with the beating of the heart, the spirit’s thought communicating with the breathing, and its affection of love <note>In this context, "affection" refers to the core desires or emotional drives of a person.</note> with the heart;² consequently when these two motions cease in the body there is at once a separation. These two motions, the respiration of the lungs and the beating of the heart, are the very bond on the sundering of which the spirit is left to itself, and the body being then deprived of the life of its spirit grows cold and begins to decay. This inmost communication of the spirit of man is with the respiration and with the heart, because on these all vital motions depend, not only in general but in every particular.³

**447.** After the separation the spirit of man continues in the body for a short time, but only until the heart’s action has wholly ceased, which happens variously in accord with the diseased condition that causes death, with some the motion of the heart continuing for some time, with others not so long. **448.** I have been both told and shown through a living experience how this resuscitation <note>Resuscitation here refers to the process of being "woken up" or drawn out of the physical body into spiritual consciousness.</note> is carried out. **449.** The senses of my body were brought into a state of insensibility, nearly the same as the state of the dying; but with the interior life and thought remaining unimpaired, which enabled me to perceive and retain in the memory the things that happened to me, and that happen to those who are resuscitated from the dead. I perceived that the respiration of the body was almost wholly taken away; but the interior respiration of the spirit went on in connection with a slight and silent respiration of the body. Then, first, a communication of the pulse of the heart with the celestial kingdom <note>The "celestial kingdom" is the highest of the three heavens, characterized by the quality of love.</note> was established, because that kingdom corresponds to the heart in man.¹ Angels from that kingdom were seen, some at a distance, and two sitting near my head. Thus all my own affection <note>In this context, "affection" refers to a person's underlying emotional state or will.</note> was taken away, although thought and perception continued. 

**[2.]** I was in this state for some hours. Then the spirits that were around me withdrew, thinking that I was dead; and an aromatic odor like that of an embalmed body was perceived. This is because when the celestial angels are present, everything pertaining to the corpse is perceived as aromatic, and when spirits perceive this they cannot approach; in this way, evil spirits are kept away from a man's spirit when he is being introduced into eternal life. The angels seated at my head were silent, merely sharing their thoughts with mine; and when their thoughts are received, the angels know that the spirit of man is in a state in which it can be drawn forth from the body. This sharing of their thoughts was effected by looking into my face, for in this way in heaven thoughts are shared.

They are surprised to find that they are alive, and are just as much men as before—that they see, hear, and speak, and that their body enjoys the sense of touch as before, with no difference whatever (see above, section 74). And when they cease to be astonished at themselves, they are astonished that the church should know nothing about this state of men after death, and nothing about heaven or hell, when in fact everyone who has ever lived in the world is now in the other life and living as a human being. 

As they also wondered why this had not been disclosed to mankind through visions—since it is an essential part of the church’s faith—they were told from heaven that although this could easily have been done if the Lord willed it, those who have firmly rooted themselves in opposing falsehoods would not believe even if they saw it with their own eyes. Furthermore, there is a danger in confirming any truth through visions when people are set in their false beliefs; they would believe at first and afterwards deny it. By doing so, they would <term>profane</term> <note>In this context, "profanation" is the act of first accepting a holy truth and then later rejecting it, which creates a deep spiritual conflict within the person.</note> the truth itself. To believe and then later deny is to commit profanation, and those who profane truths are cast down into the lowest and most grievous of all the hells.¹

[4.] This danger is what is meant by the Lord’s words:

> “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, lest they should see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and should turn, and I should heal them” (*John 12:40*).

---

¹ <note>These references (marked as "n.") refer to paragraph numbers in Swedenborg's multi-volume work, *Arcana Coelestia* (Heavenly Secrets).</note> Profanation is the mixing of good and evil and of truth and falsity within a person (n. 6348). 

Only those can profane truth and good, or the holy things of the Word and the church, who first acknowledge them, and even more so those who live according to them; if they afterwards turn away from that belief, reject it, and live only for themselves and the world, they commit profanation (n. 593, 1008, 1010, 1059, 3398, 3399, 3898, 4289, 4601, 10284, 10287). 

If a person, after a sincere repentance of heart, relapses into their former evils, they profane the truth, and their later state is then worse than their former one (n. 8394). 

Those who have not acknowledged holy things, and especially those who have no knowledge of them, cannot profane them (n. 1008, 1010, 1059, 9188, 10284). 

The <term>heathen</term> <note>Referring to those outside the Christian tradition who do not have access to the Bible.</note> who are outside the church and do not have the Word cannot profane it (n. 1327, 1328, 2051, 2284). 

For this reason, deeper internal truths were not disclosed to the Jews; for if they had been disclosed and acknowledged, that people would have profaned them (n. 3398, 4289, 6963). 

The fate of profaners in the other life is the worst of all, because not only the good and truth they once acknowledged remains, but also their evil and falsity; because these opposites are stuck together, their very life is torn asunder (n. 571, 582, 6348). 

Consequently, the Lord takes the most careful provision to prevent profanation (n. 2426, 10287).

And that those who are in false beliefs would not believe, even if visions were given to them, is meant by these words:

> Abraham said to the rich man in hell, “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” But he said, “No, father Abraham, but if someone came to them from the dead, they would be converted.” But Abraham said to him, “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe though one should rise from the dead.” (*Luke* 16:29–31).

### 457.
When a person's spirit first enters the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "world of spirits" is an intermediate state between heaven and hell where people arrive immediately after death.</note>—which happens shortly after their <term>resuscitation</term> <note>The process of being awakened or "raised up" into the spiritual world after the physical body dies.</note> as described before—their face and the tone of their voice are similar to what they had in the world. This is because they are still in their state of "exteriors," and their "interiors" are not yet uncovered. This is a person's first state after death.

But later, their face changes and becomes entirely different. It begins to resemble their <term>ruling affection</term> <note>The primary love or motivation that guided a person's life and choices while they were on Earth.</note> or ruling love, which is what the inner depths of their mind and spirit truly were while they lived in the body. For the face of a person’s spirit differs greatly from the face of their physical body. The physical face is inherited from one's parents, but the face of the spirit is formed by one's own affections and is a direct image of them. 

When the life of the spirit in the physical body ends, and the outer appearances are set aside to reveal the inner self, the person enters this true affection. This is the person's second state. I have seen people who recently arrived from the world and recognized them by their face and speech; but seeing them later, I did not recognize them. Those who were governed by good affections appeared with beautiful faces, while those who were governed by evil affections appeared with misshapen or ugly faces. This is because a person's spirit, when viewed in its true nature, is nothing but their affection, and the face is merely its outward form.

Another reason why faces change is that in the next life, no one is allowed to fake affections that are not their own, or to put on a "mask" that contradicts their true love. Everyone in the spiritual world is brought into a state where they speak exactly as they think and show their true intentions through their looks and gestures. Because of this, everyone's face becomes a perfect image of their inner character. As a result, those who knew each other in the world may recognize each other in the world of spirits, but they do not necessarily recognize each other once they reach heaven or hell (as mentioned above in section 427).¹

->HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

**458.** The faces of <term>hypocrites</term> <note>In this context, Swedenborg refers to those who outwardly mimic moral or religious behavior while inwardly harboring selfish or atheistic motives.</note> change more slowly than those of others. This is because, through long practice, they have formed a habit of controlling their <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner levels of the mind where true intentions and thoughts reside.</note> to mimic good intentions; as a result, they may appear quite beautiful for a long time. However, as the "mask" they assumed is gradually discarded and the inner mind is brought into alignment with their true feelings, they eventually become more misshapen than others. Hypocrites are those who were accustomed to talking like angels but inwardly acknowledged only nature and not the Divine, thereby denying everything related to heaven and the church.

**459.** It is important to understand that every person's human form after death is more beautiful the more deeply they have loved <term>Divine truths</term> <note>Spiritual laws or realities that originate from God.</note> and lived according to them. A person’s inner self is opened and shaped according to their love and their life; therefore, the more "interior" or deep their affection is, the more it resembles heaven, and consequently, the more beautiful their face becomes. This is why the angels in the <term>inmost heaven</term> <note>Also known as the Third Heaven, this is the highest level of heaven in Swedenborg's cosmology, characterized by direct love for the Lord.</note> are the most beautiful, for they are the very forms of celestial love. 

On the other hand, those who have loved Divine truths more superficially, and lived by them only in an external way, are less beautiful. In their case, only surface-level feelings shine from their faces; no inner heavenly love—and thus nothing of the true form of heaven—shines through them. One sees in their faces something relatively dim, lacking the spark of an inner life shining through. In short, all perfection increases as one moves toward the "interiors" and decreases toward the "exteriors"; as perfection increases or decreases, so does beauty. I have seen the faces of angels from the third heaven with such a radiance that no painter, despite all his skill, could possibly use his colors to capture even a thousandth part of the brightness and life that shone from their countenances. However, the faces of angels in the <term>lowest heaven</term> <note>The first or most external level of heaven.</note> can be somewhat imitated by human art.

**460.** In conclusion, I will mention a certain <term>arcanum</term> <note>original: "arcanum"; a Latin term for a hidden spiritual secret or mystery that is not obvious to the natural mind.</note> that has been unknown until now: namely, that every "good" and "truth" that radiates from the Lord and creates heaven is in the <term>human form</term> <note>Swedenborg teaches that the "Human Form" is the fundamental design of the universe because God (the Lord) is the Divine Human. Therefore, all spiritual things—like love and wisdom—naturally organize themselves into this shape.</note>. This is true not only for heaven as a whole and in its greatest aspects, but also in every individual part and its smallest details. Furthermore, this form affects everyone who receives goodness and truth from the Lord; it causes everyone in heaven to exist in the human form in proportion to how much they receive those divine qualities. It is because of this that heaven is consistent with itself, both in general and in particular, and that the human form is the shape of the entire heaven, of every community of angels, and of every individual angel (as shown in chapters 59 through 86). To this, let it be added that this is also the form of every thought born from heavenly love within the angels. No person on earth can easily grasp this truth, but it is clearly understood by the angels because they live in the <term>light of heaven</term> <note>A spiritual light that carries divine wisdom, allowing those in heaven to understand truths that seem impossible to those in the physical world.</note>.

### XLVIII.

### AFTER DEATH MAN IS POSSESSED OF EVERY SENSE, AND OF ALL THE MEMORY, THOUGHT, AND AFFECTION, THAT HE HAD IN THE WORLD, LEAVING NOTHING BEHIND EXCEPT HIS EARTHLY BODY.

**461.** It has been proven to me by vast experience that when a person passes from the <term>natural world</term> into the <term>spiritual world</term> <note>The "natural world" refers to our physical universe, while the "spiritual world" is the realm of the afterlife where spirits and angels dwell.</note>—which happens when they die—they carry with them all their possessions. By this, I mean everything that belongs to them as a human being, except for their physical, earthly body. When a person enters the spiritual world or the life after death, they inhabit a body just as they did in the world. To the person, there is no apparent difference, as they can neither see nor feel any change. However, their body is now a <term>spiritual body</term> <note>A body made of spiritual substance rather than matter; it is the "inner person" that inhabited the physical shell during life on earth.</note>, and is thus separated or purified from everything earthly. When spiritual substance touches or sees other spiritual substance, the experience is exactly the same as when natural substance touches or sees natural substance. Consequently, when a person has become a spirit, they do not realize they have died; they believe they are still in the same body they had in the world. 

**[2.]** Moreover, a person’s spirit enjoys every sense, both outer and inner, that they enjoyed in the world. They see as before, they hear and speak as before, they smell and taste, and when touched, they feel the sensation of touch.

<summary>Swedenborg reveals that the Divine essence of heaven is organized in a "human form" and explains that upon death, individuals transition into a spiritual body that feels entirely physical and retains all senses and memories.</summary>

**462[*a*].** And yet there is a great difference between man’s life in the spiritual world and his life in the natural world, in regard both to his outer senses and their affections <note>In this context, "affections" refers to the underlying feelings or desires that drive our sensory experiences.</note> and his inner senses and their affections. Those that are in heaven have more exquisite senses—that is, a keener sight and hearing—and also think more wisely than when they were in the world; for they see in the <term>light of heaven</term> <note>A spiritual light that carries divine wisdom, allowing those in heaven to see both physical beauty and inner truths with perfect clarity.</note>, which surpasses by many degrees the light of the world (see above, section 126); and they hear by means of a spiritual atmosphere, which likewise surpasses by many degrees the earthly atmosphere (section 235). This difference in respect to the outward senses is like the difference between clear sunshine and dark cloudiness in the world, or between noonday light and evening shade. For the light of heaven, since it is Divine truth, enables the eyes of angels to perceive and distinguish most minute things. **[2.]** Moreover, their outer sight corresponds to their inner sight or understanding; for with angels one sight so flows into the other as to act as one with it; and this gives them their great keenness of vision. In like manner, their hearing corresponds to their perception...

That memory is the <term>book of his life</term> <note>The "book of life" is not a physical book, but the totality of a person's inner memory and character.</note> (n. 2474, 9386, 9841, 10505).

**466.** The nature of these two memories—the outer and the inner—is sometimes shown visually in the afterlife through forms not seen in our world; for in that realm, many things that exist in a person as abstract ideas are made visible to the sight. *   For those who tried to force their way into **Divine mysteries** <term>Divine arcana: profound spiritual truths that are beyond the reach of mere human logic or worldly science.</term> using only human philosophy, refusing to believe anything until proven by such means, their memory looks like a dark substance that swallows up rays of light and turns them into darkness.
*   For those who practiced deceit and hypocrisy, it appears hard and bony like ebony, which reflects the light away.

But for those who lived in the "good of love" and the "truths of faith," no such hardened layer is seen. Their inner memory transmits the rays of spiritual light directly into the outer memory. In the ideas and objects stored there—as if in a foundation or fertile soil—the light finds a beautiful and delightful home. The outer memory is the final boundary of order; when it is filled with goodness and truth, spiritual and heavenly things find their resting place there and feel at home.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the transformation of human consciousness after death. **468.** How the **rational faculty** <term>rational faculty: the human capacity to think clearly and perceive what is true, which Swedenborg defines as a spiritual tool for understanding rather than just logical argumentation.</term> may be cultivated shall also be told in a few words. The genuine rational faculty consists of truths and not of falsities; whatever consists of falsities is not rational. There are three kinds of truths: **civil, moral, and spiritual**. 

*   **Civil truths** relate to matters of judgment and of government in kingdoms, and in general to what is just and equitable in them. 
*   **Moral truths** relate to matters of individual life in regard to companionships and social relations, in general to what is honest and right, and in particular to virtues of every kind. 
*   **Spiritual truths** relate to matters of heaven and of the church, and in general to the good of love and the truth of faith. 

**[2.]** In every man there are three degrees of life <note>original: "n. 267" — refers to section 267 of this work, where the author details the structure of the human soul in three layers.</note>. The rational faculty is opened to the **first degree** by civil truths, to the **second degree** by moral truths, and to the **third degree** by spiritual truths. 

But it must be understood that the rational faculty that consists of these truths is not formed and opened by man's merely knowing them, but by his living according to them. Living according to them means loving them from **spiritual affection** <term>spiritual affection: a selfless love for a principle (like justice or honesty) for its own sake, rather than for personal gain.</term>. To love truths from spiritual affection is to love what is just and equitable because it is just and equitable, what is honest and right because it is honest and right, and what is good and true because it is good and true. 

In contrast, living according to them and loving them from **bodily affection** is loving them for the sake of self and for the sake of one's reputation, honor, or gain. Consequently, so far as man loves these truths from a bodily affection he fails to become rational, for he loves, not the truths, but himself; and the truths are made to serve him as servants serve their Lord. When truths become servants, they do not enter the man and open any degree of his life—not even the first—but merely rest in the memory as knowledge under a material form, where they join themselves with the love of self, which is a bodily love. 

**[3.]** All this shows how a person becomes truly rational: they reach the **third degree** through a spiritual love of good and truth (pertaining to heaven and the church); they reach the **second degree** through a love of what is honest and right; and the **first degree** through a love of what is just and equitable. These two latter loves also become spiritual when they are influenced by the spiritual love of good and truth, because that higher love flows into them, joins with them, and forms within them its own likeness.

<summary>This page defines the "rational faculty" as a three-tiered structure developed not through memory alone, but by living according to civil, moral, and spiritual truths. It emphasizes that true rationality is only achieved when these truths are loved for their own sake (spiritual affection) rather than for selfish reputation (bodily affection).</summary>

Whatever quality and amount of affection a spirit or angel had in the world remains with them. This affection is later perfected by being "filled out," a process that continues forever. Everything is capable of being filled out for eternity because everything is capable of infinite variation—it can be enriched, multiplied, and undergo **fructification** <term>fructification: the process of bearing fruit; spiritually, this refers to the continuous production of new insights and good deeds from a single seed of truth.</term>. There is no limit to anything good because it originates from the **Infinite** <note>original: "Infinito" — referring to the Divine or God as the source of all growth.</note>.

*   On the non-Christians or people outside the church in heaven (sections 318-328);
*   And on little children in heaven (sections 329-345).

**472.** But by deeds and works, what they are inwardly is here meant, and not the way they outwardly appear; for every one knows that every deed and work goes forth from the man's **will** and **thought** <term>will and thought: In Swedenborg’s psychology, the "will" is the seat of a person's desires and loves, while "thought" is the intellectual faculty. Together, they constitute the "internal man."</term>; otherwise it would be nothing but a movement like that of an **automaton** <note>original: "automati." An automaton is a self-operating machine. Swedenborg uses this to describe actions performed without conscious intent or spiritual life.</note> or image. Consequently, a deed or work viewed in itself is merely an effect that derives its soul and life from will and thought, even to the extent that it is nothing but will and thought in effect, and thus is will and thought in outward form. From this it follows that a deed or work is the same in quality as the will and thought that produce it. If the thought and will are good the deeds and works are good; but if the thought and will are evil the deeds and works are evil, although in outward appearance they are the same. A thousand men may act in the same way, that is, may do like deeds, so alike in outward form as to be almost indistinguishable, and yet each one regarded in itself be different, because from a different will. 

**[2.]** For example, when one acts honestly and justly with a companion, one person may do it for the purpose of appearing to be honest and just out of regard to himself and his own honor; another out of regard to the world and gain; a third out of regard to reward and merit; a fourth out of regard to friendship; a fifth from fear of the law and the loss of reputation or employment; a sixth that he may draw some one to his own side, even when he is in the wrong; a seventh that he may deceive; and others from other motives. In all these instances although the deeds are good in appearance, since it is a good thing to act honestly and justly with a companion, they are nevertheless evil, because they are done, not out of regard to honesty and justice and for the love of these, but out of regard to love of self and the world which are loved; and honesty and justice are made to serve that love as servants serve a lord, whom the lord despises and dismisses when they fail to serve him. 

**[3.]** In outward appearance those act in the same way who act honestly and justly with a companion because they love what is honest and just. **473.** Just as deeds and works originate from the will and the thought, so too do they originate from love and faith. Consequently, they are only as good or as true as the love and faith behind them. It is essentially the same whether you speak of a person’s **love** or their **will**, and it is the same whether you speak of a person’s **faith** or their **established thought**. This is because whatever a person loves, they also will; and whatever a person believes, they also think. When a person loves what they believe, they also will it and, as far as possible, do it. Everyone can recognize that love and faith reside within a person’s will and thought, not outside of them; for love is what sets the will on fire, and thought is what is enlightened in matters of faith. Therefore, only those who are able to think wisely are truly enlightened, and in the measure of their enlightenment, they think what is true and will it—or, to put it another way, they believe what is true and love it.¹

**474.** However, it must be understood that it is the **will** that makes the person, while thought only makes the person in so far as it...

---

¹ All things that exist according to order in the universe relate to **good** and **truth**; similarly, in man, all things relate to **will** and **understanding** <note>n. 803, 10122. These "n." citations refer to paragraph numbers in Swedenborg's multi-volume work, *Arcana Coelestia* (Heavenly Secrets).</note>.

The reason for this is that the will is a recipient of good and the understanding is a recipient of truth <note>n. 3332, 3623, 5232, 6065, 6125, 7503, 9300, 9995</note>.

It amounts to the same thing whether you say "truth" or "faith," for faith belongs to truth and truth belongs to faith; and it amounts to the same whether you say "good" or "love," for love belongs to good and good belongs to love <note>n. 4353, 4997, 7179, 10122, 10367</note>.

From this it follows that the understanding is a recipient of faith, and the will is a recipient of love <note>n. 7179, 10122, 10367</note>.

And since a person's understanding is capable of receiving faith in God, and the will is capable of receiving love for God, a person is capable of being joined with God in faith and love; and whoever is capable of being joined with God in love and faith can never die <note>n. 4525, 6323, 9321</note>.

...goes forth from the will; and deeds and works go forth from both; or what is the same, it is love that makes the man, and faith only so far as it goes forth from love; and deeds or works go forth from both. Consequently, the will or love is the man himself, for whatever goes forth belongs to that from which it goes forth. To go forth is to be brought forth and presented in suitable form for being perceived and seen.¹ All this makes clear what faith is when separated from love, namely, that it is no faith, but mere knowledge, which has no spiritual life in it; likewise what a deed or work is apart from love, namely, that it is not a deed or work of life, but a deed or work of death, which possesses an appearance of life from an evil love and a belief in what is false. This appearance of life is what is called **spiritual death** <term>spiritual death: A state where a person's inner life is disconnected from divine goodness and truth, though they may still appear active or "alive" in a worldly sense.</term>.

**475.** Again, it must be understood that in deeds or works the whole man is exhibited, and that his will and thought or his love and faith, which are his **interiors** <term>interiors: The internal aspects of a person, such as their private intentions, desires, and thoughts.</term>, are not complete until they exist in deeds or works, which are his **exteriors** <term>exteriors: The outward expressions of a person, including their speech and physical actions.</term>, for these are the outmosts in which the will and thought terminate, and without such terminations they are **interminate** <note>In this context, "interminate" means "without boundaries" or "unfinished"—like a project that never reaches a final result.</note>, and have as yet no existence, that is, are not as yet in the man. To think and to will without doing, when there is opportunity, is like a flame enclosed in a vessel which goes out; also like seed cast upon the sand, which fails to grow, and so perishes with its power of germination. But to think and will and from that...

---

¹ The will of man is the very **essential being** <note>original: "esse." In philosophy, *esse* refers to the fundamental nature or "to be" of a thing.</note> of his life, because it is the receptacle of love or good, and the understanding is the **resulting manifestation** <note>original: "existere." Swedenborg uses *existere* to describe how a thing’s inner essence (esse) takes form and becomes visible.</note> of life therefrom, because it is the receptacle of faith or truth (n. 3619, 5002, 9282).

Thus the life of the will is the chief life of man, and the life of the understanding is derived therefrom (n. 585, 590, 3619, 7342, 8885, 9282, 10076, 10109, 10110).

In the same way as light is derived from fire or flame (n. 6032, 6314).

From this it follows that man is man by virtue of his will and his understanding therefrom (n. 8911, 9069, 9071, 10076, 10109, 10110).

Every man is loved and esteemed by others in accordance with the good of his will and of his understanding therefrom, for he that wills well and understands well is loved and esteemed; and he that understands well and does not will well is set aside and despised (n. 8911, 10076).

After death man continues to be such as his will is, and his understanding therefrom (n. 9069, 9071, 9386, 10153).

Consequently after death man continues to be such as his love is, and his faith therefrom; and whatever belongs to his faith and not also to his love then vanishes, because it is not in the man, thus not of the man (n. 553, 2364, 10153).

# HEAVEN AND HELL.

to do is like a flame that gives heat and light all around, or like a seed in the ground that grows up into a tree or flower and continues to live. Every one can know that willing and not doing, when there is opportunity, is not willing; also that loving and not doing good, when there is opportunity, is not loving, but mere thought about willing and loving; and this is thought separate, which vanishes or is dissipated. Love and will constitute the soul itself of a deed or work, and give form to its body in the honest and just things that the man does. This is the sole source of man's **spiritual body** <term>spiritual body: The internal form of a person that exists after the physical body dies, shaped by their character and actions.</term>, or the body of his spirit; that is, it is formed solely out of the things that the man does from his love or will (see above, n. 463). In a word, all things of man and his spirit are contained in his deeds or works.¹

**476.** All this makes clear what the life is that man continues to have after death, namely, that it is his love and his faith therefrom, not only in **potency** <term>potency: The latent capacity or possibility for action, as opposed to the action itself.</term>, but also in act; thus that it is his deeds or works, because in this all things of man's love and faith are contained.

**477.** It is man's **ruling love** <term>ruling love: The fundamental, dominant desire that directs a person’s life and priorities.</term> that continues after death, and this is in no way changed to eternity. Everyone has many loves; but they are all related to his ruling love, and make one with it or together compose it. All things of the will that are in harmony with the ruling love are called loves, because they are loved. These loves are both inner and outer; some directly connected and some **mediately** <note>Meaning "indirectly" or acting as a middle step.</note>; some nearer and some more remote; all subservient in various ways. Taken together they constitute a kingdom, as it were, such being the order in which they are arranged in man, although man knows nothing about that arrangement. And yet something of it is made man-

Deeds or works are these "outmosts" which contain all the internal qualities of a person (n. 10331).

**479.** (i.) *Man after death is his own love or his own will.* This has been proved to me by manifold experience. The entire heaven is divided into societies according to differences of the "good of love"; and every spirit who is taken up into heaven and becomes an angel is taken to the society where his love is. When he arrives there he is, as it were, at home, and in the house where he was born; this the angel perceives, and is affiliated with those there that are like himself. When he goes away to another place he feels constantly a kind of resistance, and a longing to return to his like, thus to his ruling love. This is how affiliations are brought about in heaven; and in the same way in hell, where they are formed in accord with loves that are the opposites of heavenly loves. It has been shown above (sections 41-50 and 200-212) that both heaven and hell are composed of societies, and that they are all distinguished by differences of love. [**2.**] That man after death is his own love might also be seen from the fact that whatever does not make one with his ruling love is then separated and as it were taken away from him. All of this shows that "heaven" within a person is heavenly and spiritual love, because all the qualities of heaven are written into that love. Likewise, "hell" in a person is corporeal and worldly love when it is separated from heavenly love, because all the qualities of hell are inscribed upon it. It is evident, then, that the person whose love is heavenly and spiritual enters heaven, and the person whose love is merely corporeal and worldly enters hell.

Some of those who claimed that they had faith were brought to those who truly had faith, and when they communicated with them they found that they had no faith at all; and afterwards they confessed that merely believing what is true and believing the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> is not faith, but that faith is loving truth from heavenly love, and willing and doing it from interior affection. <note>This "interior affection" refers to a person's deepest motivations and feelings, rather than just intellectual agreement.</note> Moreover, they were shown that their persuasion which they called faith was merely like the **light of winter**, in which light, because it has no heat in it, all things on the earth are bound up in frost, become torpid, and lie buried under the snow. As soon, therefore, as the light of persuasive faith in them is touched by the rays of the light of heaven, it is not only extinguished but is turned into a dense darkness, in which no one can see himself; and at the same time their inner minds are so obscured that they can understand nothing at all, and at length become insane from **falsities**. <term>falsities: Beliefs that are not just factually wrong, but are distorted or "fake" truths used to justify selfish or evil behavior.</term> 

Consequently with such, all the truths that they have learned from the Word and from the doctrine of the church, and have called the truths of their faith, are taken away; and they soak up in their place every falsity that is in agreement with the evil of their life. For they are all let down into their loves and into the falsities agreeing with them; and they then hate and abhor and therefore reject truths, because they are repugnant to the falsities of evil in which they are. From all my experience in what pertains to heaven and hell I can bear witness that all those that from their doctrine have professed "faith alone," and whose life has been evil, are in hell. I have seen many thousands of them cast down to hell. (Respecting these see the treatise on *The Last Judgment and the Destruction of Babylon* <note>original Latin: "De Ultimo Judicio et de Babylonia destructa." This is a reference to another work by Swedenborg published in 1758.</note>).

**483.** (v.) *Love in act, that is, the life of man, is what endures.*—This follows as a conclusion from what has just been shown from experience, and from what has been said about deeds and works. Love in act is work and deed.

**484.** It must be understood that all works and deeds pertain to **moral** and **civil life**, and therefore have regard to what is honest and right, and what is just and equitable. <term>moral life: Actions involving personal integrity, honesty, and right behavior toward others.</term> <term>civil life: Actions involving legal justice, fairness, and the laws of society.</term> Honest and right behavior pertains to moral life, while just and equitable behavior pertains to civil life. The love from which deeds are done is either heavenly or infernal. Works and deeds of moral and civil life, when they are done from heavenly love, are heavenly; for what is done from heavenly love is done from the Lord, and everything done from the Lord is good. ### L.

## THE DELIGHTS OF EVERY ONE’S LIFE ARE CHANGED AFTER DEATH INTO CORRESPONDING DELIGHTS.

**485.** It has been shown in the preceding chapter that the **ruling affection** or dominant love in every one continues to eternity. It shall now be explained how the delights of that affection or love are changed into **corresponding delights**. <note>The concept of "correspondence" suggests that the internal feelings and thoughts of a person's spirit take on an outward form in the spiritual world that perfectly matches their inner nature.</note> Being changed into corresponding delights means into spiritual delights that correspond to the natural delights. That they are changed into spiritual delights can be seen from this, that so long as man is in his earthly body he is in the natural world, but when he leaves that body he enters the **spiritual world** and is clothed with a **spiritual body**. It has already been shown that angels, and men after death, are in a complete human form, and that the bodies with which they are clothed are spiritual.

¹ Man’s **own** <term>man’s own: The Latin "proprium" refers to the human ego or self-identity that feels it lives and acts independently of God.</term> consists in loving himself more than God, and the world more than heaven, and in making nothing of his neighbor in comparison with himself, thus it consists in the love of self and of the world. <note>Original references: Arcana Coelestia, nos. 694, 731, 4317.</note>
Man is born into this "own," and it is dense evil. <note>Original references: Arcana Coelestia, nos. 210, 215, 731, 874-876, 987, 1047, 2307, 2308, 3518, 3701, 3812, 8480, 8550, 10283, 10284, 10286, 10732.</note>
From what is man’s own not only every evil but also every **falsity** <term>falsity: A concept that is not just factually incorrect, but is a distortion of truth used to justify selfish or evil desires.</term> is derived. <note>Original references: Arcana Coelestia, nos. 1047, 10283, 10284, 10286.</note>
The evils that are from what is man’s own are contempt for others, enmity, hatred, revenge, cruelty, deceit. <note>Original references: Arcana Coelestia, nos. 6667, 7370, 7373, 7374, 9348, 10038, 10742.</note>

**486.** All the delights that a person has are the delights of their **ruling love**, <term>ruling love: The fundamental obsession or primary motivation that directs a person’s life and choices.</term> for we feel nothing to be delightful except what we love; therefore, we especially delight in that which we love above all else. It means the same whether you say the "ruling love" or "that which is loved above all things." 

These delights are diverse. In general, there are as many varieties as there are ruling loves—consequently, as many as there are people, spirits, and angels; for no one’s ruling love is exactly like another's. For this reason, no one has a face exactly like that of any other; for each person's face is an image of their mind, and in the **spiritual world** it becomes a direct image of their ruling love. <note>In this context, the author suggests that in the afterlife, our outward appearance is no longer a mask but a perfect reflection of our true character.</note> 

In particular, every individual's delights are of infinite variety. It is impossible for any one delight to be exactly like another, or the same as another, whether they follow one after another or exist at the same time; no one delight is ever identical to another. Nevertheless, these particular delights in every person are connected to their one primary love, which is their ruling love; they compose that love and thus become one with it. Likewise, all delights in general refer back to one universally ruling love: which in **heaven** is love to the Lord, and in **hell** is the **love of self**. <term>love of self: A state where a person's own ego and desires are placed above the well-being of others or the divine.</term>

**487.** Only from a knowledge of **correspondences** <term>correspondences: The ancient spiritual science explaining how every physical object or feeling in the natural world is a direct "reflection" of a spiritual reality.</term> can it be known what spiritual delights a person's natural delights are changed into after death, and what kind of delights they are. 

In general, this knowledge teaches that nothing natural can exist without something spiritual corresponding to it. In particular, it teaches what it is that corresponds, and what kind of a thing it is. Therefore, anyone who has this knowledge can determine and know what their own state after death will be, if they only know what their love is, and what its relation is to the "universally ruling loves" spoken of above. 

However, it is impossible for those who are in the **love of self** to know what their ruling love is, because they love what is "their own," <note>original: "proprium"</note> and they call their own evils "goods." The false ideas they incline toward—and use to justify their evils—they call "truths." And yet, if they were willing, they might learn the truth from others who are wise and who see what they themselves do not. This, however, is impossible for those who are so filled with self-love that they reject all teaching from the wise.

From truth (which comes from good), anyone can see evil and its **falsity**; but from evil, no one can see what is good and true. This is because the falsehoods born of evil are essentially darkness and correspond to darkness; consequently, those who live in falsehoods from evil are like the blind—they cannot see the things that exist in the light, but instead shun them like birds of night.¹ 

**[3.]** But as truths from good are light, and correspond to light (see above, sections 126–134), those who are in truths from good see with open eyes and can discern the differences between light and shade. Such spirits have no comprehension of the good of heavenly love, of conscience, of honesty, or of justice—except when such things are done for the sake of self-interest. They do not understand what it means to be led by the Lord. They claim that such things do not exist and are therefore of no account. 

All this has been said so that a person may examine themselves and recognize their true love by identifying what they find most delightful. In this way, so far as they can understand it through a knowledge of **correspondences**, <term>correspondences: The spiritual law stating that every natural object or feeling reflects a specific spiritual reality or "truth."</term> they may know the state of their life after death.

**488.** How the delights of every person's life are changed after death into corresponding delights can be known from the science of correspondences; but as that science is not yet generally known, I will try to throw some light on the subject by providing certain examples from experience. 

All those who are in evil and who have confirmed themselves in **falsities** <note>original: "falsis" – This refers to persistent false beliefs that a person uses to justify their own selfish or harmful behavior.</note> in opposition to the truths of the church—especially those who have rejected **the Word** <note>original: "Verbum" – Referring to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>—flee from the light of heaven. They take refuge in caves that appear at their openings to be densely dark, and they hide there.

### LI.

## THE FIRST STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.

**491.** There are three states <note>Stages or conditions of being.</note> that a person passes through after death before they enter either heaven or hell. The first state is the state of their **exteriors** <note>The outward personality, manners, and social self that a person presented to the world.</note>, the second is the state of their **interiors** <note>The hidden, inner intentions and true character of the person.</note>, and the third is their state of **preparation**. A person passes through these stages in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>An intermediate realm between heaven and hell where everyone first arrives after dying.</note>. 

There are some, however, who do not pass through these stages, but are instead taken up into heaven or cast into hell immediately after death. Those who are taken up to heaven immediately are those who have been **regenerated** <note>Spiritual rebirth; the process of becoming a new person through a life of faith and charity.</note> while in the world and were thus already prepared for heaven. Those who have been so transformed and prepared that they only need to shed their natural impurities along with the physical body are at once carried up by the angels into heaven. I have seen people raised up in this way shortly after the hour of death. 

On the other hand, those who have been inwardly wicked while maintaining an outward appearance of goodness—filling up the measure of their malice through trickery and using "goodness" as a tool to deceive others—are cast into hell immediately. I have seen some such individuals cast into hell right after death: one of the most deceitful was cast in head-downward and feet-upward, and others in various ways. There are also some who are cast into caverns immediately after death and are thus separated from those in the world of spirits; they are eventually taken out of these 

<summary>This page explains that earthly joys are transformed into spiritual correspondences after death and introduces the three-stage transition process (outward self, inward self, and preparation) that most souls undergo in the world of spirits.</summary>
