and put back again by turns. They are such as have dealt wickedly with the neighbor under civil pretences <note>Using the rules of polite society or the law as a "mask" to hide harmful intentions toward others.</note>. But all these are few in comparison with those that are retained in the **world of spirits** <note>The intermediate realm where the soul is prepared for its final destination.</note>, and are there prepared in accordance with Divine order for heaven or for hell.

**492.** In regard to the **first state**, which is the state of the **exteriors** <note>The outward personality, social manners, and physical appearance that a person presented to the world.</note>, it is that which man comes into immediately after death. Every man, as regards his spirit, has **exteriors** and **interiors** <note>The inner, true character consisting of one's deepest desires and thoughts.</note>. The exteriors of the spirit are the means by which it adapts the man’s body in the world—especially the face, speech, and movements—to fellowship with others; while the interiors of the spirit are what belong to its own will and thought; and these are rarely manifested in face, speech, and movement. For man is accustomed from childhood to maintain a semblance of friendship, benevolence, and sincerity, and to conceal the thoughts of his own will, thereby living from habit a moral and civil life in externals, whatever he may be internally. As a result of this habit man scarcely knows what his interiors are, and gives little thought to them.

**493.** The first state of man after death resembles his state in the world, for he is then likewise in externals, having a like face, like speech, and a like disposition, thus a like moral and civil life; and in consequence he is made aware that he is not still in the world only by giving attention to what he encounters, and from his having been told by the angels when he was raised up that he had become a spirit (n. 450). Thus is one life continued into the other, and death is merely the passing from one to the other.

**494.** The state of man’s spirit that immediately follows his life in the world being such, he is then recognized by his friends and by those he had known in the world; for this is something that spirits perceive not only from one’s face and speech but also from the **sphere of his life** <note>An invisible spiritual "aura" that radiates a person's true character and feelings to those around them.</note> when they draw near. Whenever any one in the other life thinks about another he brings his face before him in thought, and at the same time many things of his life; and when he does this the other becomes present, as if he had been sent for or called. This is so in the spiritual world because thoughts there are shared, and there is no such space there as in the natural world (see above, n. 191-199). So all, as soon as they enter the other life, are recognized by their friends, their relatives, and those in any way known to them; and they talk with one another, and afterward associate in accordance with their friendships in the world.

# FIRST STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.

I have often heard that those that have come from the world were rejoiced at seeing their friends again, and that their friends in turn were rejoiced that they had come. Very commonly husband and wife come together and congratulate each other, and continue together, and this for a longer or shorter time in accord with their delight in living together in the world. If they had not been united by a **true marriage love** <note>A spiritual union where two minds are joined by heavenly love, rather than just social or legal obligation.</note>, which is a conjunction of minds by heavenly love, after remaining together for a while they separate. Or if their minds had been discordant and were inwardly adverse, they break forth into open enmity, and sometimes into combat; nevertheless they are not separated until they enter the **second state** <note>The state of "interiors," where a person's outward social mask is removed and their true inner character is revealed.</note>, which will be treated of presently.

**495.** As the life of spirits recently from the world is not unlike their former life, and as they know nothing about the state of life after death and nothing about heaven and hell except what they have learned from the **sense of the letter of the Word** <note>The literal, surface-level meaning of the Bible.</note> and preaching from it, they are at first surprised to find themselves in a body and in every sense that they had in the world, and seeing the same things; and they become eager to know what heaven is, what hell is, and where they are. 

Therefore their friends tell them about the conditions of eternal life, and take them about to various places and into various companies, and sometimes into cities, and into gardens and parks, showing them chiefly such magnificent things as delight the **external senses** and faculties, which are then active. They are then brought in turn into those notions about the state of their soul after death, and about heaven and hell, that they had acquired in the life of the body, even until they feel indignant at their total ignorance of such things, and at the ignorance of the church also. 

Nearly all are anxious to know whether they will get to heaven. Most of them believe that they will, because of their having lived in the world a **moral and civil life** <note>Living according to the laws of the state and the requirements of social etiquette or "polite society."</note>, never considering that the bad and the good live a like life outwardly, alike doing good to others, attending public worship, hearing sermons, and praying; and wholly ignorant that **external deeds** and **external acts of worship** are of no avail, but only the **internals** <note>The inner motivations, intentions, and heart-felt beliefs that drive outward behavior.</note> from which the externals proceed. There is hardly one out of thousands who knows what internals are, and that it is in them that man must find heaven and the church. Still less is it known that outward acts are such as the intentions and thoughts are, and the love and faith in these from which they spring. And even when taught they fail to comprehend that

**496.** Such, however, are explored by good spirits to discover what they are, and this in various ways; since in this **first state** the evil equally with the good utter truths and do good acts, and for the reason mentioned above, that like the good they have lived morally in outward respects, since they have lived under governments, and subject to laws, and have thereby acquired a reputation for justice and honesty, and have gained favor, and thus been raised to honors, and have acquired wealth. But afterwards, when they come into the **second state**, their evils become manifest, because their interiors are then opened and their exteriors laid asleep.

**498.** This first state of man after death continues with some for days, with some for months, and with some for a year; but seldom with any one beyond a year; for a shorter or longer time with each one according to the agreement or disagreement of his interiors with his exteriors. For with every one the exteriors and interiors must make one and **correspond** <note>The principle of "correspondence" dictates that in the spirit world, the outer appearance must eventually become a perfect reflection of the inner soul.</note>. In the spiritual world no one is permitted to think and will in one way and speak and act in another. Every one there must be an image of his own affection or his own love, and therefore such as he is inwardly such he must be outwardly; and for this reason a spirit's exteriors are first disclosed and reduced to order that they may serve the interiors as a corresponding plane.

# SECOND STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.

## LII.

### THE SECOND STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.

**499.** The second state of man after death is called the state of his <term>interiors</term> <note>In this context, "interiors" refers to a person's authentic inner self—their true motives, hidden desires, and private thoughts—as opposed to the "exteriors" or the polite social mask used in the world.</note>, because he is then let into the interiors of his mind, that is, of his **will** and **thought**; while his <term>exteriors</term>, which he has been in during his first state, are laid asleep. Whoever gives any thought to man's life and speech and action can see that every one has exteriors and interiors, that is, exterior and interior thoughts and intentions. This is shown by the fact that in society one thinks about others in accordance with what he has heard and learned of them by intercourse or conversation; but he does not talk with them in accordance with his thought; and if they are evil he nevertheless treats them with civility. That this is so is seen especially in the case of pretenders and flatterers, who speak and act in one way and think and will in a wholly different way; also in the case of hypocrites, who talk about God and heaven and the salvation of souls and the truths of the church and their country's good and their neighbor as if from faith and love, although in heart they believe otherwise and love themselves alone. 

**[2.]** All this makes clear that there are two kinds of thought, one exterior and the other interior; and that there are those who speak from exterior thought, while from their interior thought they have other sentiments, and that these two kinds of thought are kept separate, and the interior is carefully prevented from flowing into the exterior and becoming manifest in any way. By creation man is so formed as to have his interior and exterior thought make one by <term>correspondence</term> <note>A central concept in the author's work where the physical or outward expression perfectly mirrors and matches the spiritual or inward reality.</note>; and these do make one in those that are in good, for such both think and speak what is good only. But in those that are in evil interior and exterior thought do not make one, for such think what is evil and say what is good. This is an <term>inversion of order</term> <note>A state where the natural hierarchy of the soul is flipped; instead of the "good" soul directing the "external" body, the selfish desires of the body use "goodness" as a tool for personal gain.</note>, for good with such is on the outside and evil within; and in consequence evil has dominion over good, and subjects it to itself as a servant, that it may serve it as a means for gaining its ends, and the ends of such are of the same nature as their love. With such an end contained in the good that they seek and do, their good is evidently not good, but is infected with evil, however good it may

With such, order is not inverted; but good from interior thought flows into exterior thought, and thus into word and act. Into this order man was created; and in heaven, and in the light of heaven, his interiors are in this order. This form is made apparent through various rational analyses, which have their origin in the spiritual world and belong properly to the spirit of man.

**501.** Let it be understood that man is wholly such as his interiors are, and not such as his exteriors are separate from his interiors. This is because his interiors belong to his spirit, and the life of his spirit is the life of man, for from it his body lives; and because of this, such as a man’s interiors are, such he continues to be to eternity. But as the exteriors pertain to the body, they are separated after death, and those of them that adhere to the spirit are <term>laid asleep</term> <note>This means the social masks, physical habits, and polite pretenses used during earthly life become inactive, serving only as a quiet foundation for the true inner self to express itself.</note>, and serve purely as a plane for the interiors, as has been shown above in treating of the memory of man which continues after death. This makes evident what is man’s own and what is not his own, namely, that with the evil man nothing that belongs to his exterior thought from which he speaks, or to the exterior will from which he acts, is his own, but only that which belongs to his interior thought and will.

But these are shown what they would be if they were to continue in that state, namely, that they would attempt to accomplish in secret ways the same evil ends, and by semblances of goodness, honesty, and justice, would mislead the simple in heart and faith, and would utterly destroy themselves; for their exteriors would at length burn with the same fire as their interiors, and their whole life would be consumed.

**508.** The nature of the <term>wicked</term> <note>In this context, those who have internally rejected divine love and truth in favor of their own ego.</note> in this state cannot be described in a few words, for each one is insane in accord with his own lusts, and these are various; therefore I will merely mention some special instances from which conclusions may be formed respecting the rest. Those that have loved themselves above everything, and in their occupations and employments have looked to their own honor, and have performed uses and found delight in them not for the use’s sake but for the sake of reputation, that they might because of them be esteemed more worthy than others, and have thus been fascinated by their reputation for honor, are more stupid in this second state than others; for so far as one loves himself he is separated from heaven, and so far as he is separated from heaven he is separated from wisdom. 

**[2.]** But those that have not only been in **self-love** but have been crafty also, and have raised themselves to honors by means of crafty practices, affiliate themselves with the worst of spirits, and learn <term>magic arts</term> <note>original: "artes magicas"; here referring to the perversion of spiritual laws to manipulate or dominate others.</note>, which are abuses of **Divine order**, and by means of these they assail and infest all who do not honor them, laying snares, fomenting hatred, burning with revenge, and are eager to vent their rage on all who do not yield to them; and they rush into all these enormities so far as their fiendish companions favor them; and at length they meditate upon how they can climb up into heaven to destroy it, or be worshipped there as gods. To such length does their madness carry them. 

**[3.]** <term>Papists</term> <note>A historical term used by the author to refer to Roman Catholics who focused on the temporal power and authority of the Church hierarchy over the spiritual well-being of the individual.</note> of this character are more insane than the rest, for they cherish the notion that heaven and hell are subject to their power, and that they can remit sins at pleasure, claiming to themselves all that is Divine, and calling themselves Christ. This persuasion is such with them that wherever it flows in it disturbs the mind and induces darkness even to pain. Such are nearly the same in both the first and the second state; but in the second they are without <term>rationality</term> <note>In Swedenborg's system, "rationality" is the ability to see truth, which is lost when a person completely embraces evil.</note>. Of their insanities and their lot after this state some

# SECOND STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.

Further details on this subject will be provided in the treatise on *The Last Judgment and the Destruction of Babylon* <note>original: "De Ultimo Judicio et de Babylonia destructa," a work published by Swedenborg in 1758.</note>. **[4.]** Those who have credited creation to nature—and have therefore in their hearts, if not with their lips, denied the **Divine**—consequently deny all things of the church and of heaven. In this second state, they associate with others like themselves. They regard anyone who excels in craftiness as a god, even worshipping such a person with divine honors. I have seen such individuals in a gathering adoring a magician and debating about nature; they behaved so irrationally they seemed like wild beasts in human form. Among them were some who had held high positions of dignity in the world, and others who had been considered learned and wise. The same happens with others in various states.

**[5.]** From these few examples, it can be inferred what happens to those whose <term>interiors</term> <note>The "interiors" refers to the inner levels of the mind or soul that are capable of receiving light from heaven.</note> are closed toward heaven. This is the case for all who have received no <term>influx</term> <note>Spiritual "influx" is the concept of life, heat, and light flowing from the Divine into the created world and the human spirit.</note> from heaven because they did not acknowledge the Divine or lead a life of faith. Anyone can judge for themselves how they would act if they were left entirely free—with no fear of the law, no fear for their life, and no outward restraints like the fear of losing their reputation, honor, or profit.

**[6.]** Nevertheless, the Lord restrains the insanity of such spirits so that it does not break out beyond the limits of **use** <note>In this context, "use" refers to the functional purpose or benefit that even an evil thing might serve within the grand design of the universe.</note>; for even these spirits serve a purpose. Through them, good spirits can see the nature of evil and what a human being becomes when they are not led by the Lord. Another use they serve is to gather other evil spirits like themselves together, thereby separating them from the good. Furthermore, the truths and "goods" <note>In this philosophy, "goods" are the practical expressions of love and kindness.</note> that these evil people had outwardly performed or faked while in the world are taken away from them. Once stripped of these, they are brought into the actual evils of their life and the falsities that stem from those evils, and are thus prepared for hell.

**[7.]** For no one enters hell until they are fully settled in their own evil and the falsities that support it. In that realm, no one is permitted to have a **divided mind**—that is, to think and speak one thing while willing another. Every evil spirit there must think what is false based on their evil, and speak from that falsity. Both their thoughts and speech must come from their **will**, and thus from their own essential love and its inherent delights. They act exactly as they did in the world when they were "in their spirit"—that is, how they thought to themselves when moved by their deepest affections. The reason for this is that the **will** is the man himself. Thought only belongs to the man in as much as it comes from the will; the will is the very nature or disposition of the person. Therefore, for a man to be let into his will is to be let into his true nature and his true life, for a person acquires their nature through the life they lead. After death, a person remains exactly as that nature which they formed...

This process serves a divine "use" by separating evil from good and ensuring that every spirit's outward expression matches their internal will before they enter hell.</summary>

**509.** When evil spirits are in this second state—as they rush into every kind of evil—they are subjected to frequent and severe punishments. In the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>The "world of spirits" is a transitional, intermediate realm where everyone goes immediately after death before being prepared for either heaven or hell.</note>, there are many kinds of punishment; and there is no respect for a person's status, whether they were a king or a servant in the world. Every evil carries its own punishment within it; the two are inseparable. Therefore, whoever is in evil is also in the punishment of that evil. 

And yet, no one in the other world suffers punishment for the evils they did in this world, but only for the evils they do *at that time*. However, it amounts to the same thing, whether one says they are punished for their earthly evils or for their current ones, because everyone returns to their own life after death and thus into the same patterns of evil. The person continues to be the same as they were during their physical life (see sections 470-484). People are punished because the fear of punishment is the only way to control evils in this state. Encouragement is no longer effective, nor is instruction or the fear of the law and loss of reputation, since everyone then acts according to their true nature; and that nature can only be restrained and broken by punishments. 

On the other hand, good spirits are not punished, even if they had done wrong in the world, because their evils do not return. I have also learned that the evils they committed were of a different nature—they were not done intentionally to oppose the truth, nor from a bad heart, but rather were inherited from their parents or performed out of a blind impulse while they were focused on external matters rather than their inner spiritual life.

**510.** Every person goes to their own society—the one their spirit belonged to while in the world. Regarding their spirit, every human is connected to a specific group, either **infernal** or **heavenly**. The evil person belongs to an infernal society and the good person to a heavenly one, and they are brought to that society after death (see section 438). The spirit is led to their society gradually and eventually enters it. When an evil spirit is in the state of their <term>interiors</term> <note>The "interiors" refer to the deeper levels of the mind where a person's true intentions, loves, and character reside, stripped of social masks.</note>, they are turned by degrees toward their own society. Finally, before that state ends, they turn directly toward it and cast themselves into the hell where others like them dwell. To an observer, this act of "casting down" looks like someone falling headfirst, with their feet in the air. This appearance happens because the spirit himself is in an...

In this second state some evil spirits enter the hells and come out again by turns; but these do not appear to fall headlong as those do that are fully <term>vastated</term> <note>original: "vastati." This refers to a process of "emptying" or stripping away all external traits that do not match a spirit's true inner self.</note>. Moreover, the society itself in which they had been as regards their spirit while in the world is shown to them when they are in the state of their exteriors, that they may thus learn that even while in the life of the body they were in hell, although not in the same state as those that are in hell itself, but in the same state as those who are in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>The "world of spirits" is an intermediate, transitional realm between heaven and hell.</note>. Of this state, as compared with those that are in hell, more will be said hereafter.

**511.** In this second state the separation of evil spirits from good spirits takes place. In the first state they are together, for while a spirit is in his exteriors <note>The "exteriors" are the social masks, manners, and outward behaviors a person used while living on Earth.</note> he is as he was in the world, thus the evil with the good and the good with the evil; but it is otherwise when he has been brought into his interiors and left to his own nature or will. The separation of evil spirits from good spirits is effected by various means; in general by their being taken about to those societies with which in their first state they had communication by means of their good thoughts and affections, thus to those societies that they had induced to believe by outward appearances that they were not evil. Usually they are led about through a wide circle, and everywhere what they really are is made manifest to good spirits. At the sight of them the good spirits turn away; and at the same time the evil spirits who are being led about turn their faces away from the good towards that quarter where their infernal society is, into which they are about to come. Other methods of separation, which are many, will not now be mentioned.

## THIRD STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH, WHICH IS A STATE OF INSTRUCTION FOR THOSE WHO ENTER HEAVEN.

**512.** The third state of man after death, that is, of his spirit, is a state of instruction. This state is for those who enter heaven and become angels. It is not for those who enter hell, because such are incapable of being taught, and therefore their second state is also their third, ending in this, that they are wholly turned to their own love, thus to that infernal society <note>An "infernal society" is a community in hell made up of spirits who share the same specific evil desires or "loves."</note>...

...who is in a similar love. When this has been done, they will and think from that love; and as that love is infernal <note>In this context, "infernal" refers to anything originating from or belonging to hell.</note>, they will nothing but what is evil and think nothing but what is false. In such thinking and willing they find their delights, because these belong to their love; and in consequence of this, they reject everything good and true which they had previously adopted as serviceable to their love as means.

[2.] Good spirits, on the other hand, are led from the second state into the third, which is the state of their preparation for heaven by means of instruction. For one can be prepared for heaven only by means of <term>knowledges</term> <note>original: "cognitiones." This refers to specific facts or intellectual understandings of spiritual truths.</note> of good and truth—that is, only by means of instruction—since one can know what spiritual good and truth are, and what evil and falsity are (which are their opposites), only by being taught. 

One can learn from the world what civil and moral good and truth are, which are called justice and honesty, because there are civil laws in the world that teach what is just, and there is intercourse with others whereby man learns to live in accordance with moral laws, all of which have relation to what is honest and right. But spiritual good and truth are learned from heaven, not from the world. They can be learned from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> and from the doctrine of the church that is drawn from the Word; and yet, unless man in respect to his interiors <note>The "interiors" are the deeper levels of the human mind and soul that connect directly to the spiritual world.</note> which belong to his mind is in heaven, spiritual good and truth cannot flow into his life. A person is "in heaven" when he both acknowledges the Divine and acts justly and honestly for the reason that he ought so to act because the Word requires it. This is living justly and honestly for the sake of the Divine, and not for the sake of self and the world, as ends.

[3.] But no one can so act until he has been taught—for example, that there is a God, that there is a heaven and a hell, that there is a life after death, that God ought to be loved supremely and the neighbor as oneself, and that what is taught in the Word ought to be believed because the Word is Divine. Without a knowledge and acknowledgment of these things, man is unable to think spiritually; and if he has no thought about them, he does not <term>will</term> <note>In Swedenborg's philosophy, to "will" something is to deeply desire and intend it with the heart.</note> them; for what a man does not know he cannot think, and what he does not think he cannot will. So it is when man wills these things that heaven flows into his life—that is, the Lord through heaven—for the Lord flows into the will and through the will into the thought, and through both into the life, and the whole life of man is from these. All this makes clear that spiritual good and truth are learned not from the world but from heaven, and that one can be prepared for heaven only by means of instruction.

...the Lord flows into the life of anyone He instructs, for He kindles the will with the love of knowing truths and enlightens the thought to know them; and so far as this is done, the <term>interiors</term> <note>The "interiors" refer to the inner levels of a person’s mind and spirit that connect directly to the divine.</note> of man are opened and heaven is implanted in them. Furthermore, what is Divine and heavenly flows into the honest things pertaining to moral life and into the just things pertaining to civil life in man, and makes them spiritual. This is because the person then acts from a Divine source—doing these things for the sake of the Divine. For the honest and just actions of moral and civil life that a person performs from that source are the essential effects of spiritual life; and any effect derives its entire nature from its cause, since the effect is exactly like the cause that produced it.

**513.** Instruction is given by the angels of many societies, especially those in the northern and southern quarters, because those angelic societies are in intelligence and wisdom from a knowledge of good and truth. The places of instruction are toward the north and are various, arranged and distinguished according to the kinds and varieties of heavenly goods, so that everyone may be instructed according to their particular disposition and ability to receive. These places extend around for a great distance. 

The good spirits who are to be instructed are brought by the Lord to these places when they have completed their second state in the world of spirits. Yet, not all are brought here; for there are some who have been instructed in the world and have been prepared there by the Lord for heaven. These are taken up into heaven by another way—some immediately after death, and others after a short stay with good spirits. During this stay, the coarser elements of their thoughts and affections, which they had acquired from seeking honors and riches in the world, are removed, and in that way they are purified. 

Some first endure <term>vastations</term> <note>original: "vastationes." In this context, it refers to a process of spiritual "clearing" or "stripping away." It is a purification process where false beliefs are removed so that they no longer block the reception of truth.</note>. This is carried out in places under the soles of the feet, called the <term>lower earth</term> <note>A specific region in the spiritual world used for the purification of spirits before they can enter heaven.</note>, where some suffer severely. These are people who had confirmed themselves in falsities; for when false ideas have been firmly established, they cling with great force. Until they have been dispersed, truths cannot be seen and therefore cannot be accepted. The nature of these vastations and how they are carried out has been discussed in the *Arcana Caelestia* <note>original: "Heavenly Secrets," Swedenborg's primary theological work.</note>, from which the following notes have been collected:¹

**514.** All who are in places of instruction dwell apart; for each one is connected in regard to his <term>interiors</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s writing, "interiors" refers to the inner levels of a person’s spirit and mind, which must be aligned with a specific heavenly community.</note> with that society of heaven which he is about to enter. Thus, just as the societies of heaven are arranged according to the **heavenly form** (as discussed previously in sections 200–212), so too are the places where instruction is given. For this reason, when these areas are viewed from heaven, they appear like a miniature version of heaven itself. They are spread out in length from east to west, and in breadth from south to north; however, the breadth appears to be less than the length. ---

*   Those with good intentions undergo <term>vastations</term> <note>From the Latin *vastatio*; in this context, it refers to a process of spiritual purification or "emptying out" of worldly habits and false ideas to make room for heavenly truths.</note> so that they may be stripped of earthly and worldly attachments contracted during their life in the world (Sections 7186, 9763).
*   This also allows evils and "falsities" <note>False beliefs or distorted perspectives.</note> to be removed, creating space for the **influx** of goodness and truth from the Lord out of heaven, and granting the ability to accept them (Sections 7122, 9330).
*   Rising into heaven is impossible until such things have been removed, because they obstruct heavenly influences and are not in harmony with them (Sections 6928, 7122, 7186, 7541, 7542, 9763).
*   Those destined for heaven are prepared in this way (Sections 4728, 7090).
*   It is actually dangerous to enter heaven before being fully prepared (Sections 537, 538).
*   The state of enlightenment and the joy of those who emerge from this purification and are raised into heaven, as well as their reception there, is described (Sections 2699, 2701, 2704).
*   The region where these purifications take place is called the **lower earth** (Sections 4728, 7090).
*   That region is located "under the soles of the feet," surrounded by the <term>hells</term>; its nature is described based on experience (Sections 4940–4951, 7090, 699).
*   The specific hells that most frequently harass and "vastate" these spirits are described (Sections 7317, 7502, 7545).
*   Those spirits who have harassed the well-disposed eventually become afraid of them, shunning them and turning away (Section 7768).
*   These infestations and purifications happen in different ways depending on how deeply the person’s evils and false beliefs have taken root, and they continue according to their quality and quantity (Sections 1106–1113).
*   Some spirits are quite willing to undergo this purification (Section 1107).
*   Some are purified through fears (Section 4942).
*   Some are purified by facing the evils they committed and the false thoughts they held in the world, which causes them anxiety and pangs of conscience (Section 1106).
*   Some experience a form of **spiritual captivity**, which is an ignorance of truth and a feeling of being cut off from it, combined with a deep longing to know the truth (Sections 1109, 2694).
*   Some are purified through sleep; others through a state between wakefulness and sleep (Section 1108).
*   Those who believed they earned heaven through their own "merit" or good works often appear to themselves to be **cutting wood** <note>This is a symbolic representation of those who believe their own labor—rather than divine grace—is what saves them; the labor feels tedious until they realize the true source of goodness.</note> (Section 1110).
*   Others are prepared in various other ways, with great variety (Section 699).

**517.** Instruction in the heavens differs from instruction on earth in that <term>knowledges</term> <note>original: "cognitiones." In this context, it refers to specific spiritual truths or facts about the divine.</note> are not committed to memory, but to life; for the memory of spirits is in their life, for they receive and imbibe everything that is in harmony with their life, and do not receive, still less imbibe, what is not in harmony with it; for spirits are <term>affections</term> <note>A term describing the core desires or loves that make up a person's inner nature.</note>, and are therefore in a human form that is in accord with their affections. [2.] Being such they are constantly animated by an affection for truth that looks to the <term>uses</term> <note>"Uses" (Latin: "usus") is a central concept here, referring to the practical, helpful service or function a person performs for the benefit of others.</note> of life; for the Lord provides for every one's loving the uses suited to his <term>genius</term> <note>Referring to one's unique natural disposition or inherent talent.</note>; and that love is exalted by the hope of becoming an angel. And as all the uses of heaven have relation to the general use, which is the good of the Lord's kingdom, which in heaven is the <term>father-land</term> <note>original: "patria." Swedenborg views heaven as the true homeland or native country of the soul.</note>, and as all special and particular uses are to be valued in proportion as they more closely and fully have regard to that general use, so all of these special and particular uses, which are innumerable, are good and heavenly; and in every one an affection for truth is so conjoined with an affection for use that the two make one; and thereby truth is so implanted in use that the truths they acquire are truths of use. In this way are angelic spirits taught and prepared for heaven. [3.] An affection for truth that is suited to the use is <term>insinuated</term> <note>To be introduced or instilled gradually and gently.</note> by various means, most of which are unknown in the world; chiefly by representatives of uses which in the spiritual world are exhibited in a thousand ways, and with delights and pleasures that permeate the spirit from the interiors of its mind to the exteriors of its body, and thus affect the whole; and in consequence the spirit becomes as it were his use; and therefore when he comes into his society, into which he is initiated by instruction, he is in his life by being in his use.¹

<header>THIRD STATE OF MAN AFTER DEATH.</header>

From all this it is clear that <term>knowledges</term> <note>original: "cognitiones." These are specific items of information or intellectual facts about spiritual things, rather than a lived understanding.</note>, which are external truths, do not bring any one into heaven, but the life itself, which is a life of <term>uses</term> <note>original: "usus." In this philosophy, a "use" is any helpful service or practical function performed out of love for others.</note> implanted by means of knowledges.

**518.** There were some <term>spirits</term> <note>In this context, people who have recently died and are in the intermediate state between heaven and hell.</note> who had convinced themselves, by thinking about it in the world, that they would go to heaven and be received before others because of their learning and their great knowledge of the Word and of the doctrines of their churches, believing that they were wise in consequence, and were such as are meant by those of whom it is said that

> ->"They shall shine as the brightness of the firmament," and "as the stars" (*Daniel* xii. 3).<-

These were examined to see whether their knowledges resided in the memory or in the life. Such of them as had a genuine <term>affection</term> for truth—that is, who had uses separated from what pertains to the body and the world as their end, which are essentially spiritual uses—these, when they had been instructed, were received into heaven; and it was then given them to know what it is that shines in heaven, namely, Divine truth (which is the light of heaven) in use, which is a <term>plane</term> <note>A foundation or surface that can reflect light; here, a metaphor for how a person’s practical actions allow God's truth to shine through them.</note> that receives the rays of that light and turns them into various splendors. 

But those in whom knowledges resided merely in the memory, and who had acquired therefrom an ability to reason about truths and to prove what they had already accepted as principles, seeing such principles, after they had confirmed them, as truths, although they were <term>falsities</term> <note>Ideas that are fundamentally untrue, even if they can be made to sound logical through clever reasoning.</note>—these, as they were in no heavenly light, and yet were in a belief derived from the <term>conceit</term> <note>Intellectual pride or the belief that one is superior due to their education.</note> that usually adheres to such intelligence that they were more learned than others, and would for that reason enter heaven and be served by the angels, in order that they might be withdrawn from their delusive faith, were taken up to the first or <term>outmost heaven</term> <note>The "lowest" or most external level of the three heavens.</note> to be introduced into an angelic society. 

But at the very threshold their eyes began to be darkened by the inflowing of the light of heaven, and their understanding to be disturbed, and at length they began to gasp as if at the point of death; and as soon as they felt the heat of heaven, which is heavenly love, they began to be inwardly tormented. They were therefore cast out, and afterwards were taught that knowledges do not make an angel, but the life itself, which is gained by means of knowledges, for knowledges regarded in themselves are outside of heaven; but life acquired by means of knowledges is within heaven.

<header>HEAVEN AND HELL.</header>

**519.** When <term>spirits</term> <note>In this context, people who have died and are currently in the intermediate world between heaven and hell.</note> have been prepared for heaven through instruction in the places described above—a process that happens quickly because they now think in <term>spiritual ideas</term> <note>In the afterlife, thoughts are not limited by words but encompass complex concepts all at once.</note>—they are clothed in angelic garments. These are mostly a glowing white, appearing as if made of fine linen. They are then led to the path that climbs toward heaven and are entrusted to the care of angel guards. Afterward, they are welcomed by other angels and introduced into various communities and the many joys found there. Following this, the Lord leads each person to their own specific community. This journey happens in various ways, sometimes following winding paths. No angel knows these paths; they are known to the Lord alone. When they arrive at their own community, their <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner levels of the mind and heart where a person’s true character and loves reside.</note> are opened. Because these inner qualities are in harmony with those of the angels in that community, they are immediately recognized and welcomed with great joy.

**520.** I will add a remarkable fact regarding the paths that lead from these places of instruction to heaven, by which new angels are introduced. There are eight paths in total, two from each place of instruction: one going up toward the east and the other toward the west. Those entering the Lord’s <term>celestial kingdom</term> <note>The higher of the two heavens, characterized by a primary love for the Lord.</note> are brought in by the eastern path, while those entering the <term>spiritual kingdom</term> <note>The second heaven, characterized by a primary love for one's neighbor and for truth.</note> travel the western path. The four paths leading to the celestial kingdom appear decorated with olive trees and various fruit trees. However, the paths leading to the spiritual kingdom appear adorned with vines and laurels. This is due to <term>correspondence</term> <note>The spiritual law that causes the environment of the afterlife to perfectly mirror the internal state of its inhabitants; for example, a love for truth "looks" like a vine.</note>, because vines and laurels correspond to an affection for truth and its usefulness, while olives and fruits correspond to an affection for good and its usefulness.

But those who think this way know nothing about the nature of a human being: that a person is exactly what their life is, and their life is determined by what they love. This applies to the <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner levels of the mind, heart, and soul where true character resides.</note> belonging to their will and understanding, as well as the <term>exteriors</term> <note>The outward actions and the physical body.</note> belonging to their body. As long as someone remains ignorant of these facts, they may be led to believe that salvation involves nothing more than God’s good pleasure, which is commonly called mercy and grace.

**522.** First, let us consider what the **Divine mercy** is. The Divine mercy is pure mercy toward the whole human race, intended to save it; it is unceasing toward every person and is never withdrawn from anyone. Thus, everyone is saved who can be saved. And yet, no one can be saved except by <term>Divine means</term> <note>The spiritual tools and laws for living that allow a person to be shaped for heaven.</note>, which the Lord reveals in the <term>Word</term> <note>The Sacred Scriptures.</note>. These Divine means are what are called **Divine truths**; they teach us how we must live in order to be saved. Through these truths, the Lord leads us toward heaven and implants the "life of heaven" within us. The Lord does this for everyone. However, the life of heaven can be established in no one unless they abstain from evil, for evil acts as a blockage. Therefore, to the extent that a person abstains from evil, they are led by the Lord out of pure mercy through His Divine means—from infancy to the end of their life in this world, and thereafter for eternity. This is what is meant by the Divine mercy. From this, it is evident that the mercy of the Lord is pure mercy, but not "mercy apart from means"; that is, it does not involve saving everyone out of mere good pleasure, regardless of how they have lived.

**523.** The Lord never does anything contrary to **order**, because He Himself *is* Order. The Divine truth that proceeds from the Lord is what constitutes order, and Divine truths are the laws of order. It is in accord with these laws that the Lord leads humanity. Consequently, to save a person by mercy "apart from means" would be contrary to **Divine order** <note>The inherent structure and laws of reality established by God. Because God is Order itself, He cannot act against these laws without acting against His own nature.</note>; and what is contrary to Divine order is contrary to the Divine Himself. Divine order is...

**527.** I can testify from much experience that it is impossible to implant the life of heaven in those who in the world have lived a life opposite to the life of heaven. There were some who had believed that when after death they should hear Divine truths from the angels they would readily accept them and believe them, and live a different life, and thus be received into heaven. But the experiment was made with great numbers, although it was confined to those who held this belief, and was permitted in their case to teach them that repentance is not possible after death. 

Some of those with whom the experiment was made understood truths and seemed to accept them; but as soon as they turned to the life of their love <note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, "love" refers to the core motivation or ruling passion that defines a person's character.</note> they rejected them, and even spoke against them. Others were unwilling to hear them, and at once rejected them. Others wished to have the life of love that they had contracted from the world taken away from them, and to have the angelic life, or the life of heaven, infused in its place. This, too, was permitted to be done; but as soon as the life of their love was taken away they lay as if dead, with their mental powers gone. 

By these and other experiments the simple good were taught that no one's life can by any means be changed after death; that an evil life can in no way be converted into a good life, or an infernal life into an angelic life, for every spirit from head to heel is just such as his love is, and therefore just such as his life is; and to convert this life into its opposite is to destroy the spirit completely. ### LV.
## IT IS NOT SO DIFFICULT TO LIVE THE LIFE THAT LEADS TO HEAVEN AS SOME BELIEVE.

**528.** There are some who believe that to live the life that leads to heaven, which is called the **spiritual life**, is difficult. This is because they have been told that man must **renounce the world**, must strip himself of the cravings called the <term>lusts of the flesh (strong, selfish desires or instincts that focus only on physical or worldly gratification)</term>, and must live spiritually. They understand this to mean that they must discard worldly things, which consist chiefly in riches and honors; that they must walk continually in pious <note>devout or religious</note> meditation on God, salvation, and eternal life; and must spend their life in prayers and in reading the Word <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture</note> and religious books. 

Such is their idea of "renouncing the world" and living in the spirit rather than the flesh. But that this is not at all true has been shown to me by much experience and from conversation with the angels. I have learned, in fact, that those who renounce the world and live "in the spirit" in this ascetic manner acquire a sorrowful life that is not receptive of **heavenly joy**, since every person's life continues the same after death. 

On the contrary, to receive the life of heaven, a person must live in the world and engage in its business and employments. By means of a **moral** and **civil life** <note>"Civil life" refers to acting as a responsible, law-abiding citizen; "moral life" refers to acting with integrity and honesty.</note> there, they receive the spiritual life. In no other way can the spiritual life be formed in man, or his spirit prepared for heaven; for to live an internal life and not at the same time an external life is like dwelling in a house that has no foundation, that gradually sinks or becomes cracked and torn apart, or wobbles until it falls.

For there are men who live a civil life and not as yet a moral and spiritual life; and there are men who live a moral life and not as yet a spiritual life; and there are those who live a civil life, a moral life, and a spiritual life at the same time. These live the life of heaven; but the former live the life of the world separated from the life of heaven. This shows, in the first place, that the spiritual life is not a life separated from natural life or the life of the world, but is joined with it as the soul is joined with its body, and if it were separated it would be, as just said, like living in a house that has no foundation. For moral and civil life is the active plane of the spiritual life, since to will well is the province of the spiritual life, and to act well of the moral and civil life, and if the latter is separated from the former the spiritual life consists solely of thought and speech, and the will, left with no support, recedes; and yet the will is the very spiritual part of man.

**530.** That it is not so difficult as some believe to live the life that leads to heaven will now be shown. Any one can live a civil and moral life; for every one from his childhood is initiated into that life, and learns what it is by living in the world. Moreover, every one, whether evil or good, lives that life; for who does not wish to be called honest, and who does not wish to be called just? Almost every one practices honesty and justice outwardly, so far as to seem to be honest and just at heart, or to seem to act from real honesty and justice. The spiritual man ought to live in like manner, and can do so as easily as the natural man can, with this difference only, that the spiritual man believes in the Divine, and acts honestly and justly, not solely because to so act is in accord with civil and moral laws, but also because it is in accord with Divine laws. As the spiritual man, in whatever he is doing, thinks about Divine things, he has communication with the angels of heaven; and so far as this takes place he is conjoined with them; and thereby his <term>internal man (the deepest part of the human spirit that is capable of receiving love and wisdom from God)</term>, which regarded in itself is the spiritual man, is opened. When man comes into this state he is adopted and led by the Lord, although himself unconscious of it, and then whatever he does that is honest and just pertaining to moral and civil life, is done from a spiritual motive; and doing what is honest and just from a spiritual motive is doing it from honesty and justice itself, or doing it from the heart. That inwardly they are such can be clearly seen from those of the same character in the other life <note>original: "in altera vita" — Swedenborg's term for the afterlife or the world of spirits</note>, where every one's externals are taken away, and his internals in which he there lives to eternity are opened (see above, n. 499-511). **531.** Furthermore, the laws of spiritual life, the laws of civil life, and the laws of moral life are set forth in the ten commandments of the <term>Decalogue (The Ten Commandments)</term>; in the first three the laws of spiritual life, in the four that follow the laws of civil life, and in the last three the laws of moral life. Outwardly the merely natural man lives in accordance with the same commandments in the same way as the spiritual man does, for in like manner he worships the Divine, goes to church, listens to preachings, and assumes a devout countenance, refrains from committing murder, adultery, and theft, from bearing false witness, and from defrauding his companions of their goods. 

But all this he does merely for the sake of himself and the world, to keep up appearances; while inwardly such a person is the direct opposite of what he appears outwardly, since in heart he denies the Divine, in worship acts the hypocrite, and when left to himself and his own thoughts laughs at the holy things of the church, believing that they merely serve as a restraint for the simple multitude. **[2.]** Consequently he is wholly disjoined from heaven, and not being a spiritual man he is neither a moral <note>Here, Swedenborg suggests that true morality requires a spiritual foundation; without it, "morality" is just social acting.</note>

This has been said to make known what the one kind of man is and what the other is, although they have both lived the same external life.

**532.** Every one may know that thoughts are led or tend in accord with the intentions—that is, in the same directions that one intends. **533.** That it is not so difficult to live the life of heaven as some believe can now be seen from this, that when any thing presents itself to a man that he knows to be dishonest and unjust, but to which he is inclined, it is simply necessary for him to think that it ought not to be done because it is opposed to the <term>Divine precepts (spiritual laws or commandments from God)</term>. If a man accustoms himself so to think, and from so doing establishes a habit of so thinking, he is gradually <term>conjoined to heaven (spiritually linked or connected to the heavenly realm)</term>; and so far as he is conjoined to heaven the higher regions of his mind are opened; and so far as these are opened he sees whatever is dishonest and unjust, and so far as he sees these evils they can be dispersed, for no evil can be dispersed until it is seen. Into this state man is able to enter because of his <term>freedom (the God-given capacity to choose one’s thoughts and actions)</term>, for is not any one able from his freedom to so think? And when man has made a beginning the Lord quickens all that is good in him, and causes him not only to see evils to be evils, but also to refrain from <term>willing (the act of the heart desiring or intending)</term> them, and finally to turn away from them. This is meant by the Lord’s words,

> “My yoke is easy and My burden is light” <note>original citation: *Matt. xi. 30*; Matthew 11:30</note>.

But it must be understood that the difficulty of so thinking and of resisting evils increases so far as man from his will does evils, for in the same measure he becomes accustomed to them until he no longer sees them, and at length loves them and from the delight of his love excuses them, and confirms them by every kind of fallacy, and declares them to be allowable and good. This is the fate of those who in early youth plunge into evils without restraint, and also reject <term>Divine things (truths and realities originating from God)</term> from the heart.

All at first seemed to be going the same way until they came to the large stone at the head of the two ways. **535.** I have been permitted to talk with some in the other life who had withdrawn from worldly affairs that they might live in a pious and holy manner, also with some who had afflicted themselves in various ways, believing that they were thereby renouncing the world and subduing the lusts of the flesh. But as most of these had thus acquired a sorrowful life and had withdrawn from the life of <term>charity (active love and service to others)</term>, which life can be lived only in the midst of the world, they are incapable of being affiliated with angels, because the life of angels is a life of joy resulting from a state of blessedness, and consists in performing good deeds, which are works of charity. Moreover, those who have lived a life withdrawn from worldly employments are inflamed with the idea of their own <term>merit (the belief that one has earned a reward from God)</term>, and are continually desiring heaven on that account, and thinking of heavenly joy as a reward, utterly ignorant of what heavenly joy is. When such are admitted into the company of angels and into their joy, which discards merit and consists in active labors and practical services, and in a blessedness resulting from the good thereby accomplished, they are astonished like one who has found out something quite foreign to his belief; and since they are not receptive of that joy they go away and ally themselves with spirits of their own kind that have lived in the world a life like their own. [**2.**] But those who have lived an outwardly holy life, constantly attending church and praying and afflicting their souls, and at the same time have thought constantly of themselves that they would be esteemed and honored for all this above others, and finally after death would be accounted <term>saints (those set apart as holy)</term>—such in the other life are not in heaven because they have done all this for the sake of themselves. And as they have defiled Divine truths by the self-love in which they have immersed them, some of them are so insane as to think themselves gods; and are consequently in hell among those like themselves. # HELL.

## LVI.

### THE LORD RULES THE HELLS.

**536.** In the previous discussion concerning heaven, it has been shown throughout (especially in sections 2-6) that the <term>Lord (referring to Jesus Christ as the manifest God of heaven)</term> is the God of heaven, and thus that the entire government of the heavens belongs to Him. Because the relationship between heaven and hell is like that of two opposites acting against one another, they exist in an <term>equilibrium (a state of balance where opposing forces neutralize each other)</term> that allows all things to remain stable through their action and reaction. Therefore, so that every single thing may be kept in this balance, it is necessary that the same Being who rules one must also rule the other. If the same Lord did not restrain the outbursts from the hells and keep the <note>original: "insanities" — here referring to the chaotic and irrational impulses of those in a state of spiritual evil</note> there in check, the equilibrium would be destroyed, and everything else would perish with it.

**537.** First, however, we must explain what this equilibrium is. It is well known that when two things act against each other, and one resists as much as the other pushes—since there is equal power on both sides—neither side has any effect. In this state, both can be moved easily by a third force. When the strength of two opposing forces is neutralized by their conflict, the force of a third has full effect, acting as easily as if no opposition existed at all. **[2.]** This is the nature of the equilibrium between heaven and hell. It is not, however, like a physical struggle between two combatants of equal strength; it is a spiritual equilibrium—that is, a balance of <term>falsity from evil (errors and delusions that spring from a selfish heart)</term> against <term>truth from good (wisdom and reality that spring from a loving heart)</term>. From hell, there is a constant "exhalation" or spiritual influence of falsity rooted in evil, while from heaven, there is a constant influence of truth rooted in good. This spiritual balance is what ensures that human beings have the <term>freedom (the spiritual capacity to choose one's own character and destiny)</term> to think and to will. This is because everything a person thinks or intends relates either to evil (and the false ideas it creates) or to good (and the truths it creates). **[3.]** Consequently, when a person is held in this balance, they are in freedom to either admit and accept evil and its falsity from hell, or to admit and...

<summary>This page introduces the concept of Divine governance over hell, explaining that the Lord must rule both heaven and hell to maintain a spiritual equilibrium. This balance between good and evil forces is what provides human beings with the freedom of choice.</summary>

...accept good and its truth from heaven. Every person is held in this state of <term>equilibrium (a state of spiritual balance where opposing forces of good and evil neutralize each other)</term> by the Lord, because the Lord rules both heaven and hell. Why man is held in this freedom by such a balance, and why evil and falsehood are not simply taken away from him and replaced with goodness and truth by Divine power, will be explained later in its own chapter.

**538.** I have often been granted a sensory perception of the <term>sphere (a spiritual atmosphere or field of influence radiating from a person or place)</term> of falsehood and evil that breathes out of hell. It was a constant, driving effort to destroy everything that is good and true, combined with a kind of blind fury at being unable to do so. Specifically, it was an effort to annihilate and destroy the <term>Divine (the essential nature and presence of God)</term> of the Lord, because He is the source of all goodness and truth. At the same time, I perceived a sphere of truth and goodness flowing out of heaven, which restrained the fury of the effort rising from hell. The result of these two opposing forces was a perfect balance. This sphere from heaven was perceived to come from the Lord alone, even though it appeared to come through the angels. It comes from the Lord alone because every angel in heaven acknowledges that nothing of goodness or truth originates within themselves, but all of it comes from the Lord.

**539.** In the spiritual world, <term>truth from good (spiritual reality that is motivated by love and kindness)</term> is the source of all power, while falsehood rooted in evil has no power at all. This is because the very nature of heaven is Divine Good and Divine Truth, and all power belongs to the Divine. Falsehood from evil is powerless because it contains nothing of truth or goodness. Consequently, all power resides in heaven, and none in hell; for everyone in heaven lives in truths that come from goodness, while everyone in hell lives in lies that come from evil. Indeed, no one is admitted into heaven until they are established in goodness and truth, and no one is cast down into hell until they are settled in evil and falsehood. <note>original: "n. 491-520" and "n. 228-233" — these refer to earlier sections of the manuscript discussing the states after death and the power of angels.</note>

**540.** Such, then, is the equilibrium between heaven and hell. Those who are in the <term>world of spirits (the intermediate realm where souls go immediately after death before transitioning to heaven or hell)</term> exist in that balance, for the world of spirits is situated midway between heaven and hell. For the same reason, all people living in the natural world are kept in a similar balance, since the Lord governs people in the world by means of spirits who are in the world of spirits. This will be shown in a later chapter. No such equilibrium would be possible—

-># THE LORD RULES THE HELLS.<-

...unless the Lord ruled both heaven and hell and regulated both sides. Otherwise, <term>falsehoods (distortions of spiritual reality)</term> arising from evil would become too powerful and would overwhelm the <term>simple good (those who are naturally kind and well-meaning but lack deep intellectual or spiritual insight)</term> who live in the outer regions of heaven. These individuals are less equipped to resist such influences than the angels themselves. If this happened, the spiritual <term>equilibrium (the state of perfect balance between good and evil forces)</term> would be destroyed, and with it, the spiritual freedom of all human beings.

**541.** Hell, just like heaven, is organized into societies. In fact, there are exactly as many societies in hell as there are in heaven. This is because every heavenly community has a corresponding community in hell that acts as its opposite, maintaining a necessary balance. What distinguishes these hellish societies are the specific types of evil and the resulting falsehoods they embrace, just as heavenly societies are defined by their specific forms of goodness and truth. It is a fundamental law that for every good there is an opposite evil, and for every truth there is an opposite falsehood. We can recognize this in our own experience: nothing can truly be understood except in relation to its opposite. The nature and quality of a thing are only revealed through contrast; this is the source of all <term>perception (the mental grasp of truth)</term> and <term>sensation (the feeling of spiritual or physical reality)</term>. For this reason, the Lord continually ensures that every society in heaven is balanced by a specific society in hell.

**542.** Since hell is divided into the same number of societies as heaven, there are as many individual hells as there are heavenly communities. Just as each community in heaven is a "heaven in miniature" (as discussed previously in sections 51-58), so each community in hell is a "hell in miniature." Generally speaking, there are three heavens, and so there are three corresponding levels of hell: a lowest hell, which is opposite to the highest or third heaven; a middle hell, which is opposite to the middle or second heaven; and an upper hell, which is opposite to the lowest or first heaven.

**543.** How the hells are ruled by the Lord will be briefly explained. Generally, the hells are controlled by a broad outflow of <term>Divine Good and Divine Truth (the essential spiritual energies of love and wisdom)</term> from the heavens. This influence acts as a restraint, checking the collective impulse toward chaos that rises from the hells. There is also a more specific influence flowing from each individual heaven and its societies. More directly, the hells are overseen by angels who are granted the ability to look into those realms to calm their "insanities" and disturbances; occasionally, angels are even sent to these places to moderate the chaos by their very presence. However, for the most part, the inhabitants of the hells are ruled through <term>fear (the primary motivation for those who have rejected love)</term>. Some are governed by fears they brought with them from their life in the world, but as these earthly fears eventually fade, they are primarily controlled by the fear of punishment.

**544.** It has been believed heretofore in the world that there is one single <term>devil (a supposed personification of all evil)</term> that presides over the hells; that he was created an angel of light; but having become rebellious he was cast down with his crew into hell. This belief has prevailed because the names Devil and Satan, and also Lucifer, are found in <term>the Word (the Holy Scriptures or Bible)</term>, and the Word in those places has been understood only according to the <term>sense of the letter (the literal, surface-level meaning of the text)</term>. 

But by "the devil" and "Satan," hell itself is meant. Specifically, "the devil" refers to the hell that is "behind," where the worst dwell, who are called <term>evil genii (spirits who act maliciously upon the human will and emotions)</term>; and "Satan" refers to the hell that is "in front," where the less wicked dwell, who are called <term>evil spirits (spirits who act maliciously upon the human intellect)</term>. "Lucifer" refers to those that belong to <term>Babel or Babylon (symbolizing those who use religious appearances to claim power over others' souls)</term>, who are such as claim dominion even over heaven. 

That there is no one "devil" to whom the hells are subject is evident also from this: all who are in the hells, like all who are in the heavens, are from the human race (see sections 311-317). Those who have gone there from the beginning of creation to this time amount to myriads of myriads, and every one of them is a "devil" in accord with his opposition to the <term>Divine (the presence and order of God)</term> while he lived in the world (see above, sections 311, 312).

## LVII.

### NO ONE IS CAST INTO HELL BY THE LORD; THE SPIRIT DOES THIS TO HIMSELF.

**545.** A common opinion has long prevailed among some people that God turns His face away from humanity, casts people away from Himself, and throws them into hell, being angry with them on account of their evils. Some even believe that God punishes people and inflicts evil upon them. They confirm themselves in this opinion by the <term>sense of the letter (the literal, surface-level meaning of the text)</term> of <term>the Word (the Holy Scriptures or Bible)</term>, where such things are stated. They do not realize that the <term>spiritual sense (the deeper, symbolic meaning that reveals divine truths)</term> of the Word, which makes the literal meaning clear, is entirely different. Consequently, the genuine doctrine of the church—which is derived from the spiritual sense—teaches otherwise: that God never turns His face away from anyone and never casts anyone away from Himself; He casts no one into hell and is never angry with anyone. <note>original: "quod Dominus neminem in infernum deiciat, sed quod spiritus ipse se deiciat"</note> Everyone whose mind is <term>enlightened (spiritually opened to perceive truth)</term> perceives this to be true when they read the Word, based on the simple truth that God is goodness itself, love itself, and mercy itself. Goodness itself cannot do evil to anyone; love and mercy itself cannot cast a person away, for this would be contrary to the very essence of mercy and love, and thus contrary to the Divine nature itself. Therefore, those who think from an enlightened mind clearly perceive that God never turns away; and because He never turns away, He deals with everyone from a state of goodness, love, and mercy—meaning He wills good for them, loves them, and is merciful toward them. From this perspective, they can see that the literal sense of the Word, which contains such harsh expressions, actually conceals...

...possesses within itself a <term>spiritual sense (the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Word)</term>. **546.** Those who are <term>enlightened (those whose spiritual perception has been opened)</term> see further that good and evil are opposites. They are as opposed to one another as heaven is to hell. All good comes from heaven and all evil comes from hell. Since it is the <term>Divine of the Lord (the Lord’s divine essence)</term> that creates heaven (see sections 7–12), nothing but good can flow into a person from the Lord, just as nothing but evil can flow from hell. Therefore, the Lord is constantly pulling a person away from evil and leading them toward good, while hell is constantly leading them into evil. 

Unless a person stood between these two forces, they would have no capacity for thought or will, and certainly no <term>freedom (the spiritual ability to choose)</term> or choice. A person possesses these abilities only because of the <term>equilibrium (the state of perfect balance)</term> between good and evil. Consequently, if the Lord were to turn away and leave a person to evil alone, that person would cease to be human. All of this demonstrates that goodness flows from the Lord into every person—the evil as well as the good. The difference is that the Lord is constantly trying to pull the evil person away from their wrongdoing, while constantly leading the good person toward further good. This difference in outcome lies within the person themselves, because they are the <term>recipient (one who receives and processes spiritual influence)</term>.

**547.** From this, it is clear that when a person does evil, it comes from hell, and when they do good, it comes from the Lord. However, a person often believes that whatever they do, they do by their own power. Because of this belief, the evil they do clings to them as if it were their own. For this reason, the individual is the cause of their own evil; the Lord is in no way the cause of it. 

Evil within a person is essentially "hell" within them, for "evil" and "hell" are the same thing. Since the person is the cause of their own evil, they are led into hell by themselves, not by the Lord. In fact, the Lord is so far from leading anyone into hell that He is the one who delivers them from it—at least as far as the person does not intentionally will and love to remain in their own evil. A person’s will and love remain the same after death as they were before (see sections 470–484). Someone who wills and loves evil in this world will love that same evil in the <term>other life (the spiritual world after death)</term>, but there they no longer allow themselves to be pulled away from it. Therefore, if a person is rooted in evil, they are tied to hell. In terms of their <term>spirit (the internal, eternal self)</term>, they are actually already there. After death, they desire nothing more than to be where their evil is. Consequently, it is the person who casts themselves into hell after death, not the Lord.

**Key Terms:**
*   **Spiritual sense:** the inner meaning of scripture.
*   **Good and evil:** the two fundamental opposing forces of the universe.
*   **Heaven and hell:** the spiritual states and places resulting from those forces.
*   **Divine of the Lord:** God's own essence and influence.
*   **Equilibrium:** the balance between heaven and hell that allows for human free will.
*   **Freedom:** the ability to choose one's spiritual path.
*   **Recipient:** the human mind as a vessel for spiritual influence.
*   **Cause of evil:** the human choice to claim evil as one's own.
*   **Spirit:** the immortal part of a human being.
*   **Death:** the transition from the natural world to the spiritual world.

**548.** We will now explain how this process actually occurs. When a person enters the <term>other life (the afterlife or spiritual world)</term>, they are first received by angels. These angels perform every kind of service for them, speaking with them about the Lord, heaven, and the life of the angels, while instructing them in what is true and good. However, if the person—now a <term>spirit (the form of a human after the death of the physical body)</term>—is someone who knew about these things in the world but in their heart denied or looked down upon them, they will soon feel uncomfortable. After some conversation, they will desire and seek to move away from these angels. As soon as the angels sense this desire, they leave the spirit. 

After interacting with various others, the spirit eventually connects with those who are in the same kind of evil as themselves (as mentioned in sections 445-452). When this happens, the spirit turns away from the Lord and turns their face toward the hell they had already joined themselves to while living in the world—a place where others who share the same love of evil reside. 

All of this makes it clear that the Lord draws every spirit toward Himself through the help of angels and through <term>influx (the constant outward flow of divine life and energy)</term> from heaven. However, spirits who are grounded in evil resist this pull completely. They essentially tear themselves away from the Lord, pulled by their own evil—and thus by hell—as if by a rope. Because they are drawn this way and are eager to follow because of their love for evil, it is obvious that they cast themselves into hell by their own <term>free choice (the spiritual liberty to follow one's own love)</term>. 

People in the world, because of their preconceived ideas about hell, find it hard to believe this is the case. In fact, to those looking on from outside hell in the spiritual world, it does not always appear this way; it only seems so to those who are actually casting themselves in, for they enter of their own accord. Those who enter out of a burning, intense love for evil often appear to be thrown headlong, with their head down and their feet up. <note>In the spiritual world, your orientation reflects your values; those in hell have inverted their priorities, putting their own "feet" or worldly desires above "head" or divine wisdom.</note> It is because of this visual appearance that people assume they are being cast into hell by Divine power. (This will be discussed further in section 574.) Ultimately, the Lord casts no one into hell; every person casts themselves there, both while living in the world and after death when they join the world of spirits.

**549.** The Lord, by His very <term>Divine Essence (the fundamental nature of God)</term>—which is goodness, love, and mercy—cannot treat every person in the same way. This is not because of a lack of will on His part, but because evils and <term>falsities (false beliefs or distorted truths)</term> stand in the way. These evils do not just dim the Divine influx; they actively reject it. Evils and falsities are like thick, black clouds that move between the sun and the human eye, stripping away the sunshine and the clarity of light. Even so, the sun never stops trying to break through those opposing clouds, for it is constantly working
