## LVIII.

### ALL WHO ARE IN THE HELLS ARE IN EVILS AND IN FALSITIES DERIVED FROM THEM, STEMMING FROM THE LOVE OF SELF AND THE LOVE OF THE WORLD.

**551.** Everyone who dwells in the hells is rooted in evil and the <term>falsities (falsehoods or distorted perspectives)</term> that grow out of that evil. In the hells, there is not a single person who is in evil while also holding onto truths. In the physical world, however, evil people often have some knowledge of spiritual truths—the teachings of the church—because they were taught them in childhood, heard them in sermons, or read them in the **Word** <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible.</note>; and later in life, they may have even discussed these truths. Some have even convinced others that they are Christians at heart because they knew how to speak with a faked affection for the truth and how to act honestly, appearing to be motivated by a spiritual faith.

But people of this type, whose inner thoughts were actually hostile to these truths and who only avoided doing evil because of civil laws or to protect their reputation, status, and income, are all evil in their hearts. They hold truths and goodness only in their bodies (their outward behavior) and not in their spirits (their true selves). Consequently, when their external masks are removed in the afterlife and their <term>internals (the true nature of their spirit)</term> are revealed, they are found to be entirely in evil and falsity, possessing no truth or goodness at all. 

It then becomes clear that truths and goodness lived only in their memories as mere facts, which they pulled out when talking to put on a show of being good. When such people are allowed into their "internals"—and thus into their true, evil nature—they can no longer speak what is true. They can only speak what is false because they are speaking from the evil within them. It is impossible to speak truth from a heart of evil, for the spirit is then nothing but its own evil, and only falsehood can come from that source. Every evil spirit is brought to this state before being cast into hell. <note>See paragraphs 499-512 for the author's earlier explanation of this transition.</note> This process is called being <term>vastated</term> <note>From the Latin *vastatio*, meaning a process of "emptying" or "desolation." 555. This being so I will first describe what the love of self is, and then will show that all evils and their falsities spring from that love as their fountain.

Therefore so far as any one is in love of self he separates himself from heaven, because he separates himself from heavenly love.

**558[a].** Furthermore, so far as any one is in heavenly love, which consists in loving uses and goods and being moved by delight of heart when doing them for the sake of the church, country, human society, and one's fellow-citizens, he is so far led by the Lord, because that love is the love in which the Lord is, and which is from Him. But so far as any one is in love of self, which consists in performing uses and goods for the sake of himself, so far he is led by himself; and so far as any one is led by himself he is not led by the Lord. And from this it also follows that so far as any one loves himself he separates himself from the **Divine** <note>original: "Divino"; the essential nature of God.</note>, thus also from heaven. This bond decreases according to how much others are separated from their personal interests. Anyone outside this circle is considered worthless. Furthermore, anyone who opposes those within the circle or their specific evils is treated as an enemy—no matter how wise, upright, honest, or just that person might actually be.

The end for the sake of which wealth is sought is called its use; and it is the end or use that gives to love its quality; for the love is such as is the end in view, and all other things merely serve it as means.

### LIX.

## WHAT HELL FIRE IS AND WHAT THE GNASHING OF TEETH IS.

**566.** What eternal fire is, and what the gnashing of teeth is, which are mentioned in the **Word** <note>the Word: a term used to refer to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible</note> in reference to those who are in hell, scarcely any one as yet has known, because the contents of the Word have been thought about only in a material way, and nothing has been known about its **spiritual sense** <note>spiritual sense: the deeper, symbolic meaning of scripture that exists beyond the literal or physical interpretation</note>. So fire has been understood by some to mean material fire, by others to mean torment in general, by others remorse of conscience, and others have held that it is pictured merely to excite terror in the wicked. Likewise some have supposed the gnashing of teeth to mean actual gnashing, and some only a horror, such as is excited by such a sound. But any one who is acquainted with the spiritual meaning of the Word knows what eternal fire is, and what the gnashing of teeth is; for every expression and every meaning of the expressions in the Word contains a spiritual meaning, since the Word in its bosom is spiritual; and what is spiritual can be set before man only in natural forms of expression, because man is in the natural world and thinks from the things of that world. Therefore it shall now be told what is meant by "eternal fire" and "the gnashing of teeth" into which the spirits of evil men enter after death, or which their spirits, then in the spiritual world, endure.

**567.** There are two origins of heat, one the sun of heaven which is **the Lord** <note>the Lord: the central Divine figure, identified here as the source of all spiritual light and warmth</note>, and the other the sun of the world. The heat that is from the sun of heaven, that is, the Lord, is **spiritual heat** <term>spiritual heat: the essence of divine love as it is felt and experienced by the human spirit</term>; and this in its essence is love (see above, n. 126-140); but the heat from the sun of the world is natural heat, and this in its essence is not love, but serves spiritual heat or love as a receptacle. Evidently love in its essence is heat, since it is love,

That the natural heat that springs from the sun of the world serves spiritual heat as a receptacle <note>receptacle: a physical vessel or container that receives and holds spiritual energy</note> is evident from the heat of the body, which is excited by the heat of its spirit, and is a kind of substitute for that heat in the body. It is especially evident from the spring and summer heat in animals of every kind, which then annually renew their loves. [2.] It is not the natural heat that produces this effect, but it disposes their bodies to receive the heat that flows into them from the spiritual world; for the spiritual world flows into the natural as cause into effect. Whoever believes that natural heat produces these loves is much deceived, for **influx** <term>influx: the spiritual process where life and energy flow from the divine or spiritual realm into the physical world</term> is from the spiritual world into the natural world, and not from the natural world into the spiritual; and as all love belongs to the life itself it is spiritual. [3.] Again, he who believes that any thing comes forth in the natural world without influx from the spiritual world is deceived, for what is natural comes forth and continues to exist only from what is spiritual. Furthermore, the subjects of the **vegetable kingdom** <note>vegetable kingdom: a historical term for the world of plants and trees</note> derive their germinations <term>germinations: the beginning of growth in seeds or sprouts, here described as a spiritual process</term> from influx out of the spiritual world. The natural heat of spring time and summer merely disposes the seeds into their natural forms by expanding and opening them so that influx from the spiritual world can there act as a cause. These things are mentioned to make clear that there are two kinds of heat, spiritual heat and natural heat; and that spiritual heat is from the sun of heaven and natural heat from the sun of the world, and that influx and consequent co-operation produce the effects that appear before the eyes in the world.¹

**568.** Spiritual heat in man is the heat of his life, because, as was said above, it is in its essence love. This heat is what is meant in the **Word** <note>the Word: a term referring to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible</note> by "fire," love to the Lord and love towards the neighbor by "heavenly fire," and love of self and love of the world by "infernal fire."

**570.** As infernal fire is the love of self and of the world it is also every lust of those loves, since love is lust in its continuity, for what a man loves he continually lusts after. Infernal fire, therefore, is the lust and delight that spring from these two loves as their origins. The evils flowing from these loves are contempt of others, enmity, and hostility against those who do not favor them, envy, hatred, and revenge, and from these fierceness and cruelty; and in respect to the Divine they are denial and consequent contempt, derision, and detraction of the holy things of the church; and after death, when man becomes a spirit, these evils are changed into anger and hatred against these holy things (see above, n. 562). And as these evils breathe forth continually the destruction and murder of those whom they account as enemies, and against whom they burn with hatred and revenge, so it is the delight of their life to will to destroy and kill, and so far as they are unable to do this, to will to do mischief, to injure, and to exercise cruelty.

To the extent that a person prevails, they subjugate the others and bring them under their dominion, venting their rage with delight upon those who do not submit. This delight is so closely united with the delight of "bearing rule" <note>The desire to dominate others for one's own sake.</note> that they exist in the same measure, since the delight of doing harm is contained in all enmity, envy, hatred, and revenge.

-># THE MALICE OF INFERNAL SPIRITS<-

Under these outward appearances, evil has remained so hidden and obscured that the individual hardly knew their own spirit contained so much malice and craftiness. In other words, they did not realize that in their inner self, they were already the same kind of "devil" that they become after death, when the spirit returns to itself and its own true nature. **[3.]** At that point, a level of malice manifests that exceeds all belief. Thousands of evils then burst forth from the core of evil itself, including things that cannot be described by the words of any human language. I have been permitted to know and perceive what these are through extensive experience, since the Lord has granted me the ability to be in the spiritual world as a spirit while simultaneously being in the natural world in my physical body. 

I can testify that their malice is so great that it is hardly possible to describe even a thousandth part of it. It is so intense that if a person were not protected by the Lord, they could never be rescued from hell. This is because every person is surrounded by spirits from hell as well as angels from heaven (as seen above in points 292 and 293). Yet, the Lord cannot protect a person unless they acknowledge the Divine <note>The "Divine" refers to the presence and power of God.</note> and live a life of faith and charity <note>In Swedenborg's vocabulary, "charity" refers to active goodwill and useful service to others, not just giving money.</note>. Otherwise, the person turns themselves away from the Lord and toward hellish spirits, and thus their spirit becomes saturated with a malice just like theirs. 

**[4.]** Nevertheless, the Lord continually pulls man away from the evils that he attaches and attracts to himself through his connection with hellish spirits. If a person is not pulled back by the internal bonds of conscience—which they cannot receive if they deny the Divine—they are instead pulled back by external bonds. As mentioned before, these are fears regarding the law and its penalties, and the fear of losing profit, status, or reputation. In fact, such a person may be kept away from evil actions by their own desire for pleasure or the fear of losing that pleasure; however, they cannot be led into true spiritual "goods" <note>In this context, "goods" are the positive, selfless intentions and actions that come from a spiritual source.</note> by these fears. As soon as such a person is led toward spiritual things, they begin to focus on pretenses and schemes—faking or counterfeiting what is good, honest, and just for the sake of deceiving others. This cunning then joins itself to the evil of their spirit and gives it a specific form, making their inner evil identical to that deceitful nature.

**578.** The worst of all are those who have lived in evil out of a love for self while being inwardly governed by deceit. Deceit penetrates more deeply into a person's thoughts and intentions than other evils do, infecting them with a poison that completely destroys their spiritual life. Most of these spirits dwell in the hells located "behind the back" <note>Swedenborg often uses spatial directions (behind the back, under the feet) to describe the specific spiritual "neighborhoods" or states of being in the afterlife.</note>...

When the deceit and craftiness of these spirits are clearly seen, they appear as vipers.

### 583.

All of the gates to the hells open from the world of spirits, and none of them from heaven.

**585.** The openings or gates to the hells that are situated beneath the plains and valleys look different to the sight. Into these desert places those are cast out from the hells who have suffered every extremity of punishment, especially those who in the world have been more cunning than others in undertaking and contriving intrigues and deceits. Such a life is their final lot.

**587.** As to the positions of the hells in detail, it is something wholly unknown even to the angels in heaven; it is known to the **Lord** <note>The author's term for Jesus Christ, viewed as the sole God and ruler of both heaven and hell.</note> alone. In the spiritual world, these are not fixed map points but directions of the heart and mind.</note> in which they are. For the hells, like the heavens, are distinguished by their quarters; and in the spiritual world quarters are determined in accordance with what one loves. In heaven, all the quarters begin from the Lord as the sun, who is the **East** <note>In this theology, the "East" represents the source of all divine love.</note>; and as the hells are opposite to the heavens, their quarters begin from the opposite point, that is, from the **West**. (On this see the chapter on the four quarters in heaven, n. 141-153.) **[2.]** For this reason, the hells in the western quarter are the worst of all and the most horrible, becoming gradually worse and more horrible by degrees the more remote they are from the east. In the western hells are those who in the world were in the **love of self** <note>Considered the root of all spiritual ruin—the desire to put oneself above all others and to dominate them.</note>, and in consequent contempt of others, and in enmity against those who did not favor them.

## THE EQUILIBRIUM BETWEEN HEAVEN AND HELL.

**589.** For any thing to have existence there must be an <term>equilibrium</term> <note>original: "aequilibrium"; a fundamental concept in this work, referring to a state of balance between opposing forces (good and evil) that allows for human free will.</note> of all things. Without equilibrium there is neither action nor reaction; for equilibrium is between two forces, one acting and the other reacting, and the state of rest resulting from like action and reaction is called equilibrium. In the natural world there is an equilibrium in all things and in each thing. It exists in a general way even in the atmospheres, wherein the

<meta>This page transitions from the discussion of the vast and organized societies of hell (concluding section 588) into a new chapter regarding the spiritual "equilibrium" or balance between heaven and hell. ->### EQUILIBRIUM BETWEEN HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

lower parts react and resist in proportion as the higher parts act and press down. Again, in the natural world there is an **equilibrium** <term>equilibrium</term> <note>original: "aequilibrium"; a state of balance between opposing forces. Swedenborg views this balance as the essential condition for any action, movement, or existence to occur.</note> between heat and cold, between light and shade, and between dryness and moisture, the middle condition being the equilibrium. There is also an equilibrium in all the subjects of the three kingdoms of nature, the mineral, the vegetable, and the animal; for without equilibrium in them nothing can come forth and have permanent existence. Everywhere there is a sort of effort acting on the one side and reacting on the other.

[2.] All existence or all effect is produced in equilibrium, that is, by one force acting and another suffering itself to be acted upon, or when one force by acting flows in, the other receives and harmoniously submits. In the natural world that which acts and reacts is called **force**, and also **endeavor** <term>endeavor</term> <note>original: "conatus"; in the science of Swedenborg's time, this referred to a directed pressure or a "striving" toward movement that exists even in stationary objects.</note>; but in the spiritual world that which acts and reacts is called **life** and **will**. Life in that world is living force, and will is living effort; and the equilibrium itself is called **freedom**. Thus spiritual equilibrium or freedom has its outcome and permanence in the balance between good acting on the one side and evil reacting on the other side; or between evil acting on the one side and good reacting on the other side. 

[3.] With the good the equilibrium is between good acting and evil reacting; but with the evil the equilibrium is between evil acting and good reacting. Spiritual equilibrium is the balance between good and evil, because the whole life of man has reference to good and to evil, and the will is the receptacle. There is also an equilibrium between truth and falsity, but this depends on the equilibrium between good and evil. The equilibrium between truth and falsity is like that between light and shade, in that light and shade affect the objects of the vegetable kingdom only so far as heat and cold are in them. That light and shade themselves have no effect, but only the heat that acts through them, is evident from the fact that light and shade are the same in winter time and in spring time. This comparison of truth and falsity with light and shade is in accord with **correspondence** <term>correspondence</term> <note>The central theme of Swedenborg’s work, suggesting that every physical thing in the natural world has a direct spiritual counterpart or meaning.</note>, for truth corresponds to light, falsity to shade, and heat to the good of love; in fact, spiritual light is truth, spiritual shade is falsity, and spiritual heat is good of love (see the chapter where light and heat in heaven are treated of, n. 126-140).

**590.** There is a **perpetual equilibrium** between heaven and hell. From hell there continually breathes forth and ascends an endeavor to do evil, and from heaven there continually...

->## EQUILIBRIUM BETWEEN HEAVEN AND HELL.<-

...quently from all together—that is, from the whole of heaven and the whole of hell. Goodness flows out from heaven because everyone there lives in a state of good; and evil flows out from hell because everyone there lives in a state of evil. The goodness that comes from heaven is entirely from the **Lord**; for the angels in the heavens are all held back from what is **their own** <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium"; a central concept in Swedenborg's thought referring to the "self" or "selfhood"—the inherent nature of a person or angel which is naturally inclined toward self-interest rather than God.</note>, and are kept in what is the Lord’s, which is goodness itself. But the spirits in the hells are all in what is their own, and a person's own is nothing but evil; and because it is nothing but evil, it is hell.^1^ Clearly, then, the equilibrium in which angels are kept in the heavens and spirits in the hells is not the same as the equilibrium in the **world of spirits** <note>The intermediate state between heaven and hell where people go immediately after death.</note>. The equilibrium of angels in the heavens exists to the degree that they have been willing to be in good, or the degree to which they lived in good while in the world and thus felt a natural turning away from evil. However, the equilibrium of spirits in hell exists to the degree that they have been willing to be in evil, or have lived in evil in the world, and thus in heart and spirit have been opposed to good.

**592.** Unless the Lord ruled both the heavens and the hells, there would be no equilibrium; and if there were no equilibrium, neither heaven nor hell would exist. For everything in the universe—both in the natural world and in the spiritual world—survives by means of equilibrium. Every rational person can see that this is true. If there were a greater weight on one side and no resistance on the other, would not both sides be destroyed? This is exactly how it would be in the spiritual world if good did not react against evil and constantly restrain its upward surge. Unless this were done by the **Divine** itself, both heaven and hell would perish, and with them the entire human race. I say "unless the Divine itself did this," because the self of every individual—whether angel, spirit, or human—is nothing but evil (see above, section 591); consequently, neither angels nor spirits are able in the slightest to resist the evils constantly exhaling from the hells, since...

Only the Divine power—which comes solely from the Lord—is strong enough to resist the countless hells, which are beyond numbering and which act together against heaven and against everyone who dwells there.

**593.** The equilibrium between the heavens and the hells is either weakened or made more perfect depending on the number of people who enter heaven and those who enter hell—a number that amounts to several thousands every day. The Lord alone, and no angel, can know and perceive this shift in order to regulate and balance it with precision. This is because the Divine power that goes forth from the Lord is omnipresent <note>present everywhere at once</note>; He sees everywhere whether there is any wavering in the balance. An angel, by contrast, sees only what is near to them and has no internal perception of what is happening even within their own spiritual society.

**594.** We can see to some extent how all things in the heavens and the hells are arranged so that every single inhabitant remains in a state of equilibrium. This is understood from what was shown previously regarding the organization of these realms: all the societies of heaven are distinctly arranged according to the specific types and varieties of goodness they possess, and all the societies of hell are arranged according to their specific types and varieties of evil. Beneath every society of heaven, there is a <term>corresponding</term> <note>original: "correspondens"; a fundamental principle in Swedenborg's theology where the lower (hell) mirrors or reacts to the higher (heaven) in direct opposition.</note> society of hell that opposes it. It is from this "opposing correspondence" that equilibrium results. Because of this, the Lord constantly ensures that no hellish society beneath a heavenly one gains the upper hand. As soon as one begins to dominate, it is restrained by various means and brought back to an exact measure of balance.

There are many such means, but I will mention only a few. Some involve a stronger manifestation of the Lord’s presence; some involve creating a closer connection and joining of one or more societies with others; some involve casting an excess of hellish spirits into "deserts" <note>Spiritual regions of isolation or lack of influence.</note>; some involve transferring certain spirits from one hell to another; some involve bringing those in the hells into a stricter order through various methods; and some involve shielding certain hells under denser and thicker coverings, or letting them sink to even greater depths. There are many other means as well, including those employed within the heavens themselves...

It is obvious, then, that love for the Lord and the love of self are opposites, just as love toward the neighbor and the love of the world are opposites. ## LXIII.

### BY MEANS OF THE BALANCE BETWEEN HEAVEN AND HELL, HUMANITY LIVES IN FREEDOM.

**597.** I have now described the balance between heaven and hell. It has been shown that this is a balance between the good that comes from heaven and the evil that comes from hell; therefore, it is a spiritual balance, which in its very essence is freedom. A spiritual balance is essentially freedom because it is a balance between good and evil, and between truth and falsity—and these are spiritual things. Therefore, the ability to will either what is good or what is evil, to think either what is true or what is false, and to choose one over the other, is the "freedom" we are discussing here. 

This freedom is granted to every person by the Lord and is never taken away. In fact, because of its origin, this freedom is not truly the person's own but belongs to the Lord, since it flows from Him. Nevertheless, it is given to a person along with their life as if it were their own property. This is done so that a person can have the ability to be reformed <term>spiritually transformed or reshaped</term> and saved; for without freedom, there can be no reformation or salvation. 

With a little rational insight, anyone can see that it is a part of human freedom to be able to think about what is wrong or what is right, what is honest or what is dishonest, and what is just or what is unjust. A person is also free to speak and act rightly, honestly, and justly. However, they are often restrained from speaking and acting wrongly, dishonestly, or unjustly by the spiritual, moral, and civil laws that keep their external behavior in check. Clearly, then, it is the human spirit—the part that thinks and wills—that exists in freedom, rather than the external body which speaks and acts, except when those actions agree with the laws mentioned above.

**598.** A person cannot be reformed unless they have freedom, because we are born into evils of every kind <note>In Swedenborg’s view, "being born into evils" refers to inherited tendencies toward self-centeredness rather than an inherent "sinfulness" that deserves punishment from birth.</note>. These evils must be removed if a person is to be saved, and they cannot be removed unless the person sees them in themselves, acknowledges them, and afterwards stops willing them, eventually feeling a natural distaste <note>Original Latin: *aversionem*. This implies a turning away or a deep-seated desire to avoid something.</note> for them. Only then are they removed. And...

<summary>This page explains that human free will is a direct result of the spiritual balance maintained between heaven and hell, allowing individuals to choose between good and evil. This freedom is essential for spiritual reformation, as a person must freely recognize and reject their own negative tendencies to be saved.</summary>

The spiritual goods that a person is capable of thinking about are learned from childhood by reading the Word <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture</note> and from preaching; one learns moral and civil good from their life in the world. This is the first reason why a person must be kept in freedom. 

[2.] Another reason is that nothing is <term>appropriated</term> <note>In this context, to make something a permanent part of one's own character or spirit</note> to a person except what is done from an <term>affection</term> <note>The underlying feeling, desire, or love that motivates a person</note> of their love. Other things may gain entrance, but only as far as the thought and not reaching the <term>will</term> <note>The seat of a person's actual intentions and desires, as opposed to just their intellectual thoughts</note>; and whatever does not enter the will does not become the person's own. This is because thought derives its contents from the memory, while the will derives its contents from the life itself. Only what comes from the will—or what is the same thing, from the affection of love—can be called free, for whatever a person wills or loves, they do freely. Consequently, a person’s freedom and the affection of their love or will are one and the same. It is for this reason that a person has freedom: so that they may be affected by truth and good or may love them, and so that these qualities may become their own. 

[3.] In short, whatever does not enter into a person's freedom has no permanence, because it does not belong to their love or will; and what does not belong to a person's love or will does not belong to their spirit. This is because the very <term>being</term> <note>original: "esse," meaning the fundamental essence or core existence</note> of a person's spirit is love or will. We say "love or will" because a person wills what they love. This, then, is why a person can be <term>reformed</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reshaped or transformed by God</note> only in freedom. More on the subject of human freedom may be found in <term>Heavenly Secrets</term> <note>original: "Arcana Caelestia," Swedenborg’s multi-volume commentary on the internal sense of the Bible</note> in the passages cited below.

It is by means of hell that a person is in their own evil, while it is by means of angels from heaven that a person is in good from the Lord. In this way, the person is held in a spiritual balance—that is, in freedom. The fact that angels from heaven and spirits from hell are joined to every person can be seen in the chapter regarding the connection of heaven with the human race (sections 291–302).

These spirits—and none from hell itself or heaven itself—are the ones present with a person. By means of evil spirits in the world...

**601.** Something more must be said about the spirits that are joined with a person. An entire spiritual community can communicate with another community, or with an individual wherever they may be, by means of a spirit sent forth from the community; this spirit is called the "subject of the many." This same principle applies to a person’s connection with communities in heaven and with communities in hell: it happens through spirits from the world of spirits who are joined to the person. They said that some intelligent persons had asked them in the world what they thought about their soul after their life on earth; they replied that they did not know what the soul is. They were then asked what they believed about their condition after death; and they said they believed they would live as spirits. Again, they were asked what belief they had respecting a spirit; and they said that a spirit is a human being. They were asked how they knew this; and they said they knew it because it is so. Those "intelligent" men were surprised that the simple folk had such a faith—a faith which they themselves did not have. This is proof that in every person who is in connection with heaven, there is an intuition regarding their life after death. This intuition comes from no other source than an influence out of heaven—that is, from the Lord through heaven by means of spirits from the world of spirits who are joined with the person. ### EXTRACTS FROM THE *HEAVENLY SECRETS* <note>original: "Arcana Caelestia," Swedenborg’s multi-volume work providing a spiritual interpretation of the Bible.</note> REGARDING THE FREEDOM OF MAN, THE INFLOW OF LIFE, AND THE SPIRITS THROUGH WHOM COMMUNICATIONS ARE CARRIED OUT.

#### FREEDOM.

All freedom is linked to love or affection, since whatever a man loves, he does freely (n. 2870, 3158, 8987, 8990, 9585, 9591).

Because freedom is linked to love, it constitutes the very life of every person (n. 2873).

Nothing seems to belong to a man as his own except what comes from his freedom (n. 2880).

There is both a heavenly freedom and an <term>infernal freedom</term> <note>The perceived freedom to do evil, which is actually a form of spiritual slavery to one's own impulses.</note> (n. 2870, 2873, 2874, 9589, 9590).

[2.] Heavenly freedom is linked to heavenly love, or the love for what is good and true (n. 1947, 2870, 2872).

And since the love of what is good and true comes from the Lord, true freedom consists in being led by the Lord (n. 892, 905, 2872, 2886, 2890-2892, 9096, 9586, 9587, 9589-9591).

A person is led into heavenly freedom by the Lord through <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or being made new by God.</note> (n. 2874, 2875, 2882, 2892).

A person must have freedom in order to be regenerated (n. 1937, 1947, 2876, 2881, 3145, 3146, 3158, 4031, 8700).

In no other way can the love of what is good and true be planted in a person and adopted by them as if it were their own (n. 2877, 2879, 2880, 2888).

Nothing is joined to a person in a state of <term>compulsion</term> <note>Forced action or belief, which Swedenborg argues cannot create lasting spiritual change.</note> (n. 2875, 8700).

If a person could be reformed by force, everyone would be saved (n. 2881).

In the process of <term>reformation</term>, force or compulsion is actually harmful (n. 4031).

All worship that comes from freedom is true worship, but worship that comes from compulsion is not worship (n. 1947, 2880, 7349, 10097).

Those who are in hell know no other kind of freedom (n. 2871).
Heavenly freedom is as distant from infernal freedom as heaven is from hell (n. 2873, 2874).
This infernal freedom is not actually freedom at all, but <term>servitude</term> <note>Spiritual slavery.</note> (n. 2884, 2890).
True servitude consists of being led by the influences of hell (n. 9586, 9589–9591).

### INFLUX.

**[5.]** Everything that a person thinks and wills "flows into" them; this is known from experience (n. 904, 2886–2888, 4151, 4319, 4320, 5846, 5848, 6189, 6191, 6194, 6197–6199, 6213, 7147, 10219).
A person’s ability to pay attention to a subject, to think about it, and to draw logical conclusions is a result of <term>influx</term> <note>The "in-flowing" of spiritual life and thought from the spiritual world into the human mind.</note> (n. 4319, 4320, 5288).
No one could live for even a single moment if this influx from the spiritual world were taken away; this is known from experience (n. 2887, 5849, 5854, 6321).
The life that flows in from the Lord varies based on the state of the person and how they receive it (n. 2069, 5986, 6472, 7343).
With those who are evil, the good that flows in from the Lord is turned into evil, and the truth is turned into falsity; this is known from experience (n. 3642, 4632).
The good and truth that continually flow in from the Lord are received only to the extent that they are not blocked by the person's own evil and falsity (n. 2411, 3142, 3147, 5828).

**[6.]** All good flows in from the Lord, and all evil flows in from hell (n. 904, 4151).
In the present day, people believe that everything is within themselves and originates from themselves, when in reality it all flows in; one could know this from church doctrine, which teaches that all good comes from God and all evil from the devil (n. 4249, 6193, 6206).
However, if a person's belief were truly in line with this doctrine, they would not

It also introduces "influx," the concept that all human thought and life flow from the spiritual world rather than originating within the individual.</summary>

<header>EXTRACTS RESPECTING FREEDOM, ETC.</header>

...[if man truly understood the source of his thoughts,] he would not attribute evil to himself, nor would he claim good as his own (n. 6206, 6324, 6325).

How happy man’s state would be if he believed that all good flows in from the Lord and all evil flows in from hell (n. 6325).

Those who deny the existence of heaven, or those who know nothing about it, are unaware that there is any spiritual <term>influx</term> <note>From the Latin *influxus*, meaning "a flowing in." This is the process by which spiritual energy, thought, and life move from the divine or spiritual realm into the natural world and the human mind.</note> from heaven (n. 4322, 5649, 6193, 6479).

The nature of this influx can be illustrated by various comparisons (n. 6128, 6190, 9407).

**[7.]** Every element of life flows in from the primary fountain of life, because that is the ultimate source; it flows in continually; thus, every aspect of life is from the Lord (n. 3001, 3318, 3337, 3338, 3344, 3484, 3619, 3741–3743, 4318–4320, 4417, 4524, 4882, 5847, 5986, 6325, 6468–6470, 6479, 9276, 10196).

Influx is spiritual and not physical; that is, the influence moves from the spiritual world into the natural world, and never from the natural into the spiritual (n. 3219, 5119, 5259, 5427, 5428, 5477, 6322, 9110).

Influx occurs through the <term>internal man</term> <note>The higher or spiritual part of the human mind that is capable of communicating with heaven.</note> into the <term>external man</term> <note>The lower or natural part of the mind and body that interacts with the physical world.</note>, or through the spirit into the body, and not the reverse. This is because a person’s spirit resides in the spiritual world, while their body resides in the natural world (n. 1702, 1707, 1940, 1954, 5119, 5259, 5779, 6322, 9380).

The internal man is in the spiritual world and the external is in the natural world (n. 978, 1015, 3628, 4459, 4523, 4524, 6057, 6309, 9701–9709, 10156, 10472).

It may appear that influence flows from the external world into a person’s internal self, but this is a sensory fallacy (n. 3721).

In a person, influx moves into the <term>rational</term> <note>The capacity for higher reasoning and logic.</note> faculties first, and through these into <term>knowledges</term> <note>Specifically "scientifics" or facts gathered from the physical world; the raw data of the memory.</note>, and not the other way around (n. 1495, 1707, 1940).

The specific order and sequence of this influx (n. 775, 880, 1096, 1495, 7270).

There is a direct influx from the Lord, and also a "mediate" influx that passes through the spiritual world or heaven (n. 6063, 6307, 6472, 9682, 9683).

The Lord’s influence flows into what is "good" within a person, and through that good it flows into "truth," and not the reverse (n. 5482, 5649, 6027, 8685, 8701, 10153).

A state of goodness provides the capacity to receive this influence from the Lord, but truth without goodness does not (n. 8321).

Nothing that flows merely into the thought is harmful to a person; it only becomes harmful if it flows into the <term>will</term>, because the will is what a person truly adopts as their own or <term>appropriates</term> <note>The process by which a person takes ownership of a thought or desire, making it part of their actual character.</note> (n. 6308).

**[8.]** There is also a <term>general influx</term> <note>A universal spiritual pressure or influence that maintains the order of the entire universe, regardless of individual choice.</note> (n. 5850).

This is a constant spiritual effort or striving to act in accordance with divine order (n. 6211).

This general influx governs the lives of animals (n. 5850).

It also flows into the subjects of the vegetable kingdom (n. 3648).

It is by this general influx that a person’s thoughts are translated into speech, and their will is translated into physical actions and movements (n. 5862, 5990, 6192, 6211).

## SUBJECT SPIRITS.

**[9.]** Spirits who are sent out from one community of spirits to another community, or to other individuals, are called <term>subject spirits</term> <note>Also known as "emissary spirits." In the spiritual world, communication between distant groups is often facilitated by a single spirit who acts as a temporary mental link or mouthpiece for a whole group.</note> (n. 4403, 5856).

Communication in the afterlife is carried out through these emissary spirits (n. 4403, 5856, 5983).

A spirit who is sent out to serve as a "subject" does not think from themselves, but speaks and thinks from the group that sent them (n. 5985–5987).

Many specific details regarding these types of spirits (n. 5988, 5989).

# INDEX OF SCRIPTURE PASSAGES.

Note.—*In this Index,*
**Bold figures** (such as **1, 3**) designate verses that are fully quoted:
Figures preceded by dots (such as **..1**) show that the beginning of the verse is not quoted;
Figures with a dot above them (such as **1̇**) show that a part of the middle of the verse has been left out;
Figures followed by dots (such as **1..**) show that the end of the verse is not given:
The omission of one word is indicated by one dot; of two or three words, by two dots; of four or more words, by three dots:
*Italic figures* (such as *1, 3*) designate verses where only the general substance or meaning is given:
Small figures in parentheses (such as (1, 3)) indicate verses that are merely referenced without being quoted.

Printed on fine Bible paper in large and clear type. Bound in heavy paper cover, 30 cents; full cloth, 40 cents; half cloth, flat back, gilt top, 50 cents; half morocco <note>A high-quality goatskin leather binding.</note>, in box, $2.00, including postage.

## Three Excellent Introductory Books.

*The Spiritual Life and the Word of God.* 192 pages.
*God, Providence, and Creation.* 256 pages.

These two volumes include the supplementary doctrinal statements that are contained in the latter portions of the *Apocalypse Explained* <note>original Latin title: "Apocalypsis Explicata." An extensive, posthumously published commentary on the Book of Revelation.</note>. In these statements the subjects treated of are presented in a clearer and more attractive form than anywhere else in Swedenborg’s works. Of the portion contained in the second volume, as previously published in another form, the following was said:

> “This is one of the best books we know to put into the hands of those who desire to get a general idea of the doctrines of the New Church <note>The "New Church" refers to the religious movement based on Swedenborg’s theological writings, also known as Swedenborgianism.</note> in a small compass. It is written in a clear and attractive style, and is remarkably free from those peculiar forms of expression which are so distasteful and perplexing to many persons when they begin to read the writings of Swedenborg.”—*Rev. Chauncey Giles.*
> “The New Churchman can have by him no more useful work for devout reading; and its remarkably free and lucid style makes it peculiarly valuable for missionary circulation <note>The practice of distributing religious literature to the public to gain new converts or inform the curious.</note>.”—*Rev. L. P. Mercer.*
> “One of the most interesting of Swedenborg’s works for general reading. It contains a great part of the philosophy of the *Divine Love and Wisdom*, in a pleasant, descriptive form, which is simple and attractive as well as profound.”—*Rev. John Worcester.*
> “We hope that the friends of the New Church everywhere will take advantage of the publication of the book in a cheap form to scatter it broadcast over the land.”—*New Church Messenger.*

# Reprints of Swedenborg's Latin Text.

---

The American Swedenborg Printing and Publishing Society solicits the co-operation of all interested in the work in its undertaking to produce a reprint of Swedenborg's Latin text which shall be of permanent use to the Church <note>The "Church" refers to the New Church, or Swedenborgianism, which follows the theological teachings of Emanuel Swedenborg.</note>.

The following have been published:

| Work | Quantity |
|:---|:---|
| *The Apocalypse Revealed* <note>original Latin: *Apocalypsis Revelata*</note>, | Two volumes. |
| *The Apocalypse Explained* <note>original Latin: *Apocalypsis Explicata*</note>, | Six volumes. |
| *Minor Works* <note>original Latin: *Opera Minora*</note>, | One volume. |
| *The Four Doctrines* <note>original Latin: *Quatuor Doctrinae*</note>, }<br/>*The Last Judgment* <note>original Latin: *De Ultimo Judicio*</note>, } | One volume. |
| *Conjugial Love* <note>original Latin: *De Amore Conjugiali*. A study of the spiritual nature of marriage and its eternal aspects.</note>, | One volume. |
| *Heaven and Hell* <note>original Latin: *De Caelo et Inferno*</note>, | One volume. |
| *Divine Providence* <note>original Latin: *Divina Providentia*</note>, }<br/>*Divine Love and Divine Wisdom* <note>original Latin: *Divinus Amor et Divina Sapientia*</note>, } | One volume. |
| *The True Christian Religion* <note>original Latin: *Vera Christiana Religio*</note>, | Two volumes. |

These are carefully edited and printed, and handsomely bound in half leather binding, and are sold for $1.50 per volume, or if by mail, $1.70 each.

The Society will continue this understanding as fast as the sales will justify. It is a work of great importance to the Church, and should be speedily completed. The works, as published, ought to be placed in the larger college and public libraries; and as all that is received for sales is devoted to the continuance of this undertaking, purchasers for this purpose serve a double use. This deserves the special attention of all who have money to give to Church uses.

->Address:<-

->**AMERICAN SWEDENBORG PRINTING AND PUBLISHING SOCIETY,**<-
->3 WEST TWENTY-NINTH STREET, N. Y.<-

# WHO WILL HELP?

The Society is constantly finding more to do than its resources permit. Its income from invested funds now amounts to about $5,000 a year <note>Adjusted for inflation from the late 19th century, this would be roughly $160,000–$200,000 today.</note>. “Our field is the world.” Something, at least, of Swedenborg <note>Emanuel Swedenborg (1688–1772) was a Swedish scientist and philosopher who claimed to have received spiritual revelations, leading to the foundation of the "New Church."</note> should be translated into the language of every civilized people, and placed where it will be accessible to those who are ready for it. Every dollar contributed helps forward this work to the utmost that a dollar can. Every sum given for investment will be a permanent missionary, preaching the truths of “the True Christian Church” to generation after generation. Can you do better with what the Lord has given you to use than devote some of it, at least to this work?

## *Directions for the guidance of persons desirous of making provision by Will for the uses of this Society.*

It is the safer course for such persons to consult a competent lawyer of the State where the property be situated. Especially is this important if the property to be given consists of real estate. The laws of more than one State provide that a <term>devise</term> <note>A "devise" is a legal gift of real estate (land or buildings) made through a will.</note> of land situated within that State cannot be made directly to a <term>foreign corporation</term> <note>In this context, a "foreign corporation" refers to an organization based in a different U.S. state, not necessarily a different country.</note> organized or situated in some other State or country than the State in which the land is situated. In such cases, Form 4 (below) should be used. In several States, moreover, no such devise or <term>bequest</term> <note>A "bequest" is a gift of personal property, such as money or stocks, made through a will.</note> is good, unless a certain time after the will is made shall elapse before the death of the <term>testator</term> <note>The "testator" is the person who has written and executed the will.</note>.

It is impracticable to give directions which will be in conformity with the varying statutes of all the States. But except for those States whose law requires a certain time to elapse between the making of the will and the death of the testator, the following forms are believed to be respectively sufficient.

### FORM I.—BEQUEST OF MONEY.

> “I give and bequeath to the American Swedenborg Printing and Publishing Society, located in the City of New York, the sum of dollars.”

### FORM II.—BEQUEST OF NOTES, BONDS, ETC.

> “I give and bequeath to the American Swedenborg Printing and Publishing Society, located in the City of New York,
> *(*Here describe the notes, bonds, stock or other property intended to be given, not consisting of land or houses.*)*

### FORM III.—DEVISE OF REAL ESTATE

*Located in the State of New York, whose laws permit a devise to be made directly to this Society; and also adapted to a devise of land in any State whose laws may permit that land situated in such State may be devised to charitable or benevolent corporations located in another State than the State in which the land is situated.*

> “I give and devise to the American Swedenborg Printing and Publishing Society, located in the City of New York, and to its successors and assigns for ever, all that certain
> *(*Here describe the real estate intended to be given, following, if possible, the description given in the title deed, in order to avoid uncertainty.*)*

### FORM IV.—DEVISE OF REAL ESTATE

*Located not within the State of New York, but in any other State whose laws do not permit a devise of land to be made directly to a corporation for charitable uses organized or situated outside of such State.*

> “I give and devise to
> ->(Here insert names of trustees)<-
> all that certain piece or parcel of land and premises with the appurtenances, bounded
> and described as follows :
> *(*Here insert the description, which, if practicable, should follow that given in the title deed, in order to avoid uncertainty :)*
> 
> IN TRUST, however, for the following uses and purposes:—The said trustees are hereby empowered and directed to sell the same as soon as practicable after my decease; and to pay over the net proceeds thereof to the Treasurer of the American Swedenborg Printing and Publishing Society, located in the City of New York, for the use of said Society in printing, publishing, and circulating the works and writings of Emanuel Swedenborg according to the provisions of their certificates of incorporation, and of the laws of the State of New York affecting the powers and uses of said Society.”
